title: BUG: a node starting over a torn tail appends before the truncation's sync completes (two syncs outstanding; §7.6 requires the sync before the next append)
description:
## Context
Found in the review of W14.1 (906fc83) for cc_1, 2026-10-04: the second, independent pass (Fable), reproduced by PeachAnchor. The code is unchanged at HEAD (6b84d9d).

**A node starting over a torn tail appends before the truncation's sync completes, so two syncs are outstanding.**

`Controller::library_idle` (`crates/node/src/controller.rs`) checks only the loop's outstanding sync:

```rust
fn library_idle(&self) -> bool {
    self.core.lifecycle != Lifecycle::Failed && self.raft.outstanding_sync().is_none()
}
```

`startup_sync`, the truncation's own sync, is never consulted. So the node is `Ready` and fed, and it can campaign and append while `Sync(first_sync)` for the `Truncate` is still outstanding.

## Evidence
A scratch test, not committed, in `/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-keyval/d767163f-b7de-47a1-82c3-b6219ddfff4a/scratchpad/candidate/crates/node/src/review_scratch_tests.rs` (`startup_truncation_sync_does_not_gate_the_library`).
- **Setup:** a one-voter journal with a 4-byte torn tail is started, the truncation's sync is never completed, and the node is ticked.
- **Storage effects:** `Truncate { len: 124 }, Sync(1), Append, Sync(2)`.
- **Syncs outstanding:** `[1, 2]`.

The existing test `a_torn_tail_is_truncated_and_synced_before_the_first_append` completes the sync before ticking, so it shows effect order, not "synced before the first append".

## Why it is a defect
- §7.6: a torn tail is "physically truncated through the byte-storage port's `Truncate`, then synced, **before the next append**". Here the append is issued before that sync completes.
- §7.11's completion bypass rests on "at most one sync is outstanding per node". §7.4 keeps one outstanding Ready.
- An append written over a truncation that is not yet durable leaves the file outside DUR-9's crash model. After a crash, the lost truncation can leave old torn bytes beyond the new frame's extent, which recovery may refuse as corruption.

## Requirements
DUR-6, DUR-9, §7.4, §7.6, §7.7, §7.11.

## Area
`crates/node` (controller.rs): W14's area.

## Acceptance
- While the start-up sync is outstanding, the library takes no input, exactly as during a loop sync:
  - `library_idle()` also requires `startup_sync.is_none()`;
  - ticks become owed, peers wait, and client attempts are still handed over.
- A test ticks before completing `Sync(first_sync)` and asserts that no `Append` (and no second `Sync`) appears until it completes, and that the node then proceeds normally.
- NODE-CONTROLLER passes with `min_cases` raised.

## Out of scope
The recovery scan itself (W11).

title: raft_adapter: an admitted MsgAppend with index past the log and log_term 0 makes raft-rs fatal! (remote crash; br-1jtp incomplete)
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fix-verification review of the W13.3 codec beads, 2026-10-04, at HEAD c78862b, for cc_1. The independent reviewer rated br-1jtp INCOMPLETE. I reproduced it with a private test against HEAD: both variants below crash a fresh follower.

**An admitted MsgAppend whose index is past the node's log and whose log_term is 0 makes raft-rs `fatal!`. One message from a voter crashes a node.**

**Evidence:**
- `RaftLog::term(idx)` returns `Ok(0)` for any index past the last (vendor/raft/raft/src/raft_log.rs:122-127), so `match_term(idx, 0)` is true for every index beyond the log.
- `maybe_append` (raft_log.rs:249-275) then:
  - with no entries: `commit_to(min(commit, idx))` reaches `fatal!("to_commit {} is out of range [last_index {}]")` (raft_log.rs:286-297);
  - with entries: `append` reaches `Unstable::truncate_and_append`, then `fatal!("unstable.slice[..] out of bound")` (log_unstable.rs:156-208).
- Admission passes it, because it never checks log_term (crates/raft_adapter/src/admit.rs). `fits_log` (admit.rs:156) only looks at heartbeats.

**Reproductions** (private test, HEAD c78862b, a fresh follower node 1, both admitted):
- `08 03 10 01 18 07 20 01 30 01 40 01`: MsgAppend {to 1, from 7, term 1, index 1, log_term 0, commit 1}. Panics with "to_commit 1 is out of range [last_index 0], raft_id: 1".
- MsgAppend {term 1, index 1, log_term 0, entries [{index 2, term 1, EntryNormal}], commit 0}. Panics with "unstable.slice[1, 2] out of bound[1, 1], raft_id: 1".
- It works at any node whose term ≤ the message's: a follower, a pre-candidate, a candidate, or a leader through `become_follower`. One payload for every node is term = index = commit = 2^53−1, log_term 0.
- Even without a crash (commit ≤ last, no entries), the node acknowledges an index it doesn't hold (raft.rs:2495).

**Why refusing it is safe:** a v1 leader sends `log_term = term(next − 1)` (raft.rs:750-751, 843), which is 0 only at index 0.

**Documentation:** admit.rs:33-42 ("raft-rs's other stateful fatal! … cannot be reached") and the admit_tests comment ("an append's commit is bounded by its own entries (maybe_append), so it is safe") claim more than is enforced.

## Requirements
§7.3, §8.2, CD-3, CD-8 (no panic on peer input); br-xx08's and br-1jtp's intent; W02 audit S-1.

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (admit.rs, admit_tests.rs); the PEER-ADMISSION row (min_cases).

## Acceptance
- `admit` refuses a MsgAppend with `index != 0 && log_term == 0`, a stateless rule, with its own `Inadmissible` reason or EntryOrder.
- Tests through `RaftNode::step` on a fresh follower, each refused and leaving no Ready and no change: both reproductions above, plus the 2^53−1 payload.
- admit.rs's module doc and the admit_tests comment claim only what is enforced.
- PEER-ADMISSION passes with raised min_cases, and the cluster and seeded runs still pass (no liveness loss).

## Out of scope
Term-space exhaustion (the sibling P2 bead).

title: fs_storage: make FS-STORAGE's DUR-7 claim testable, or drop it (no test observes a sync)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W12.3 (ca94989) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, with line numbers at HEAD 807e06e (fs_storage's reviewed code is unchanged since ca94989 apart from W23.1's read-only handle), at cc_1's request. Both reviewers (Opus and Fable) raised it as P2, and I verified it by hand.

**FS-STORAGE claims DUR-7, as an invariant, but no test can observe a single sync.**

**Evidence:**
- `registry/checks.toml:685-695` and `xtask/src/check.rs` (FS-STORAGE): `covers = ["DUR-7", "DUR-8"]`, `class = "invariant"`; summary "syncs the parent directory when it creates the data directory".
- The only DUR-7 test (`crates/fs_storage/src/lib.rs:440-462`) asserts `dir.is_dir()` and the two refusals. The contract case `synced_state_survives_a_clean_restart` reopens within one process, through the page cache.
- Mutation: replace `File::open(dir)?.sync_all()` (`lib.rs:104`) or `sync_data()` (`lib.rs:392`) with `Ok(())`, or delete the parent sync at `lib.rs:99`. STORAGE-CONTRACT-FS and FS-STORAGE both stay green.

## Requirements
DUR-7; §12.2 W12 acceptance ("the file adapter syncs directories on create"); §10.15 (a claim in its class: an invariant is enforced by an assertion or checker); §10.17 (a thin OS-call trait in `fs_storage` with a recording test implementation at the syscall boundary); AGENTS.md rule 13; P10.

## Area
crates/fs_storage; registry FS-STORAGE row (a facade turn).

## Acceptance
Either:
- **(a)** add §10.17's OS-call seam now: a thin trait over mkdir, open, fsync, fdatasync, ftruncate, pwrite and flock, with a recording test implementation. Tests then assert `fsync(parent)` after `mkdir` in `create_data_dir`, `fsync(dir)` in `sync_dir` and `fdatasync(journal)` in `sync`, so removing any sync fails a test; or
- **(b)** until W24 lands that seam, drop DUR-7 from FS-STORAGE's `covers` and reword its summary to what is tested (create, refuse an existing directory, missing parent). Leave DUR-7 to SIM-DISK and W24.

Either way, the registry row claims only what a test can fail on. Option (b) narrows a claim but doesn't weaken a check: no status, `min_cases` or tier moves, so forward-only is unaffected, and SIM-DISK still covers DUR-7. Still, name the choice in the commit message (rule 13).

## Out of scope
Real-crash probes (W24).

title: raft_adapter: admitted messages with a plausible term can still reach stateful raft-rs fatal! paths (heartbeat commit past last index, append conflicting with committed)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9. Opus reviewer: P2. I verified it in the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0.

**An admitted message with a plausible term can still reach a stateful library `fatal!`, which contradicts admit.rs's stated purpose ("refuses everything else before the library sees it", including `fatal!` paths).**

**Evidence:**
- MsgHeartbeat{from 7, to 1, term current+1, commit L+1} on a follower whose last index is L:
  1. it is admitted (all stateless rules pass);
  2. it goes through `become_follower`, then `handle_heartbeat` (raft.rs:2531-2532), then `RaftLog::commit_to(L+1)`;
  3. that hits `fatal!("to_commit {} is out of range [last_index {}]")` (raft_log.rs:286-297).
- A higher-term MsgAppend whose first entry conflicts at an already-committed index reaches `maybe_append`'s `fatal!("entry {} conflict with committed entry {}")` (raft_log.rs:259-265).
- Both need a forged or buggy peer. A v1 leader sends heartbeat commit = min(matched, committed), and a follower's matched entries are durable. PLAN §2.2 puts Byzantine faults out of scope.

## Requirements
§7.3, §8.2, CD-8; br-xx08's stated intent (admit.rs:1-7); §2.2 (the threat model).

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (node.rs `step`, admit.rs docs, tests).

## Acceptance
Either:
- **(a)** `RaftNode::step` refuses a heartbeat whose `commit` exceeds the raw log's last index, and an append that would conflict at or below the committed index, both with tests; or
- **(b)** admit.rs's module doc is narrowed to "stateless refusals; forged messages with plausible state are out of scope (§2.2)", and that limit is recorded where the PEER-ADMISSION row claims robustness.

Either way, the documentation claims only what is enforced.

## Out of scope
Term 0 (the sibling P1 bead).

title: sim: public trace and scheduler types use bare integers (client u64, disk offsets and lengths, incomplete-step counts) (CD-4)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W15.1 and W15.2, run by GoldenHorizon on 2026-10-04 at HEAD 4f26119. Opus raised it as P2 and Fable as P3, and I verified it by hand. **Public sim types use bare integers where the plan wants dedicated types.**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/sim/src/trace.rs:58` has `Endpoint::Client(u64)`, and `trace.rs:212` and `221` have `client: u64`.
- `trace.rs:98-112`: `DiskOp`'s `offset`, `len` and `upto` are bare `u64`, although `types` has byte types.
- `scheduler.rs:171-173` has `Step::Incomplete { events: u64, pending: usize }`.

So `DiskOp::Append { offset: len, len: offset }` compiles, and a client number can be confused with any other count.

## Requirements
CD-4 (dedicated ID/index types, never bare integers); AGENTS.md rule 11.

## Area
crates/sim (`trace.rs`, `scheduler.rs`); a `ClientId` newtype, in sim or types as the owner of client identity decides.

## Acceptance
- Clients are identified by a `ClientId` newtype.
- Disk offsets and lengths use byte types.
- The incomplete-step counts are typed.
- The canonical lines are unchanged, and the SIM-TRACE, SIM-SCHEDULER and K-14 tests still pass.

Changing the trace format.

title: sim trace: no disk records for truncate, journal creation, directory sync or storage failure; a sync completion doesn't say which sync or incarnation asked
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W15.2 (d44178a), run by GoldenHorizon on 2026-10-04 at HEAD 4f26119. One reviewer (Opus) raised it as P2, and I verified it by hand. **The canonical trace cannot record several disk operations the plan says it contains.**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/sim/src/trace.rs:95-114`: `DiskOp` has only `Append { offset, len }`, `Sync { upto }` and `SyncDone { upto }`.
- The storage effects now include `Truncate`, `CreateJournal` and `SyncDir`, plus the input `StorageFailed` (`crates/types/src/effects.rs`; `Truncate` existed at d44178a, and the rest landed in 3c2ed19).
- `SyncDone` says neither which sync completed (`SyncSeq`) nor which incarnation asked for it. A stale completion delivered to the next incarnation (§10.2, B-17) is written the same way as a real one.

## Requirements
§10.2 "Canonical trace: contains … disk operations and completions"; "It never excludes an inconvenient protocol decision"; DUR-6, DUR-7 (simulated crash points); B-17; K-11; T-3.

## Area
crates/sim (`trace.rs`; god view change records if affected).

## Acceptance
- `DiskOp` has a canonical record for every storage `Effect` (append, sync, truncate, create journal, directory sync) and for `StorageFailed`.
- A completion record carries the `SyncSeq` and the incarnation that requested it, so a stale completion is distinguishable.
- Each new record has a fixed-format line and a canonical-line test.
- SIM-TRACE passes with raised min_cases.

## Out of scope
The simulated disk itself (W16).

title: sim: the diagnostics buffer has no total bound, and the event budget and observation bound restate the limits registry (CD-9)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W15.2, W15.1 and the 34br fix (d44178a, ea55597), run by GoldenHorizon on 2026-10-04 at HEAD 4f26119. Both reviewers raised both halves, and I verified them by hand. Severity P2.

**Evidence:**
- **The diagnostics buffer has no total bound.** `trace.rs:377-380` resets `diagnosed_in_step` at every `event()`, and `trace.rs:416-423` pushes onto `diagnostics: Vec<String>`, which is never drained. The 4,096 bound limits each step, not the queue, so retained diagnostics can reach 4,096 × events (up to about 4×10⁹ over the 1,000,000-event budget). The text length is uncapped, and `dropped_diagnostics` is counted but never reported.
- **The bounds are copied from the limits registry, not read from it.**
  - `scheduler.rs:96` has `EventBudget::DEFAULT = Self(1_000_000)`, and `trace.rs:310` has `ObservationBound::DEFAULT = Self(4_096)`.
  - These repeat `types::Limit::SimEventsPerRun` and `Limit::LogQueueRecords` (`crates/types/src/limits.rs:207-208`), whose header (lines 1-13) says each fixed value lives "here or by the type that owns it, and nowhere else", and that bounded collections use `BoundedQueue`/`BoundedMap`.
  - Sim's tests check the literals (`scheduler.rs:583`, `trace.rs:828`), so drift goes unnoticed.
  - The pending queue is a raw `BTreeMap`, with no registry entry of its own.
  - Context: the registry (W08.3, 193eb95) landed after W15.1 and W15.2.
- **An untested claim:** `scheduler.rs:248` says a refused event draws no randomness, but the past-time test (`scheduler.rs:468-484`) never checks the next tie value.

## Requirements
CD-9, CD-10; §7.11 ("Structured log queue | 4,096 records | Diagnostic records dropped and counted"); O-3; AGENTS test-logging rule 5.

## Area
crates/sim (`trace.rs`, `scheduler.rs`); read-only use of `types::Limit`.

## Acceptance
- Retained diagnostics are capped at the registered bound overall: dropped and counted past it, oversized text truncated, and the dropped count reported. There is a test at N−1, N and N+1 on the total.
- `EventBudget` and `ObservationBound` defaults come from `types::Limit`, and a test asserts they agree with the registry.
- The pending queue's bound is registered, or the reason for a raw map is documented.
- A test shows a refused `schedule` leaves the tie stream untouched.

## Out of scope
The trace's own `lines` vector: the plan requires the full trace.

title: raft_adapter: library types in the crate's public API (library_config, EntropySource, JournalStorage, RaftNode::storage) let raft types escape the Consensus port (CD-1)
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.1 (raft_adapter, e1427a8, closed 3cbaf2d) that cc_1 asked for, 2026-10-04: SunnyDog plus an independent fresh reviewer, every finding verified by hand against the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0. Thread: br-w13-1-consensus-port-construction-3wc.

crates/raft_adapter/src/lib.rs:55-58 exports:
- `library_config`, which returns `raft::Config`;
- `EntropySource`, which implements `raft::Entropy`;
- `JournalStorage`, which implements `raft::Storage`, and whose `pub fn log_mut` gives mutable access to the logical log under the library.

`RaftNode::storage()` hands out `&JournalStorage`. The Consensus trait's own signatures are clean. But DEP-RULE lets other engine crates (for example `node`) depend on the vendored raft, so they could build on these and bypass the port.

## Requirements
CD-1 ("no Raft-library type crosses the Consensus port"), §7.3 replacement boundary.

## Area
raft_adapter (lib.rs, node.rs, storage.rs, config.rs, entropy.rs, tests).

## Acceptance
- No item of raft_adapter's public API names a raft, raft-proto or protobuf type, or exposes `JournalStorage`'s mutable log.
- `RaftNode` gives read access to the logical log through a core-typed accessor, for example `log() -> Ref<'_, LogicalLog>`.
- A compile-fail fixture or a test pins the boundary.
- RAFT-ADAPTER passes.

## Out of scope
The engine crate (W14).

title: sim net tests miss dangerous mutants: drop counts and records per reason, duplicates across a cut and the global bound, byte bound at N, delivery endpoints, client-path loss
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fresh-eyes review of W16.1, the simulated network (5cc5ada, br-w16-1-network-model-40l), 2026-10-04, at HEAD 57cb984, for cc_1. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen copy; every claim was verified by hand at HEAD, where crates/sim is unchanged. Both raised parts of it: Opus P2, Fable P2 for the counts and records.

**The SIM-NET tests miss several dangerous mutants. The commit's "12 mutants killed" doesn't cover them, and the registry row claims more than the tests show on client paths.**

**Gaps, each verified at HEAD:**
- **No drop count or record for three reasons.** `cut_at_send` is never asserted (no match in net_tests.rs), and no Dropped record is asserted for QueueFull, CutAtSend or Overflow. A mutant that miscounts CutAtSend in `NetCounts::record` (net.rs:214-215), or that deletes the refused-send Dropped record (net.rs:445-446), survives.
- **Duplicates across a cut.** The in-flight cut test uses a reliable path. A mutant filtering the arrival-time cut check by `queued` (net.rs:480) delivers duplicate copies across a cut unnoticed.
- **Duplicates and the global bound.** The bound test uses only reliable paths.
- **The byte bound at exactly N.** No send lands on it (CD-9 asks for N−1/N/N+1); `<=` → `<` at net.rs:505 survives.
- **Delivery endpoints.** `Delivery.from` and `Delivery.to`, and the Sent and Delivered record contents, are never asserted. A mutant swapping from/to passes, and W17 would route packets back to their sender.
- **Client-path loss.** registry/checks.toml:890 says "loss follows its probability on peer links and client paths", but the 0/30%/100% loop (net_tests.rs:133-163) runs node→node only. Client→node profile choice is untested.

## Requirements
§10.15 (claims in their class), CD-9, P10, §8.2.

## Area
crates/sim (net_tests.rs); the SIM-NET row (min_cases, summary).

## Acceptance
- Tests kill each mutant above: full NetCounts and Dropped records per reason, duplicates across a cut, duplicates against the global bound, the byte bound at N−1/N/N+1, and `Delivery{from,to,bytes}` plus the full records.
- The loss loop also runs on client paths, or the summary is narrowed.
- SIM-NET passes with raised min_cases.

## Out of scope
W16.2's scenario tests.

title: Place the RawNode-construction proof for accepted configs: §7.10 assigns it to W08, which cannot depend on vendored raft
description:
## Context
PLAN.md §7.10 (config validation, the raft-rs Config::validate bullet) says that a config the parser accepts can never fail at RawNode construction, "proven by a W08 test that constructs a node from every accepted fixture config". W08 cannot host that test:
- W08's area is types and config (§12.2); its only dependency is W04.
- types is a pure domain crate. DEP-RULE allows the vendored raft only in engine crates, and dev-dependencies count (Appendix A, AGENTS.md Dependencies).
- The vendored raft is not a workspace member yet. raft_adapter is created by W13, which depends on W02 and W11.
- W08's own §12.2 acceptance row does not mention the RawNode test.
Found while starting W08.1 (br-w08-1-config-parser-rules-gwj).

## Requirements

title: Judge every applied entry against the applying node's synced journal in the Ready-loop harness (K-11 client-success obligation)

## Context

**What is judged today.** The harness judges every Send against its sender's synced journal (`dur2_violation`). Applies are judged only by `index <= commit` (the `Recorder`, ready_loop_tests.rs:654-660).

**What is unasserted:**
- "An applied entry released before its frame syncs": §7.4 runs step 5 after step 4.

- `next_entries_since` is bounded by `min(committed, persisted)` (raft_log.rs:423-438);
- `persisted` moves only in `advance_append`.

**What would go uncaught.** A future change in the adapter, such as applying a Ready's committed entries when it is taken, or calling `advance` instead of `advance_append`.

- DUR-2 and C-2.
- §7.4 steps 4 and 5.
- K-11 (persistence ordering).

## Area
raft_adapter tests (`ready_loop_tests.rs`, the `Cluster` harness).

## Acceptance
- At each apply, `Cluster` records the applying node's synced last index and term.
- The seeded and scripted runs assert, for every apply, that `entry.index <= durable.last` and that its term matches the synced log.
- A fixture shows the assertion fires when committed entries are applied before their frame syncs.
- RAFT-READY-LOOP passes, and T0 is green.

## Out of scope
K-11 itself (W16 and later, simulation traces).

title: A node thread that panics leaves the production node half-alive: snapshot frozen at Ready, inputs accepted unanswered, a waiting Ready never resolved
description:
## Context
JadeOx's read-only review of W18.1/W18.2 (5245e40, 1a120d4) at HEAD 5febcdb, for cc_1. Verified by reading `crates/server/src/runtime.rs`, `io.rs`, `clock.rs`, `logs.rs` and `inbox.rs`.

**A thread that panics leaves the production node half-alive, not stopped.**

CD-7 makes every broken invariant a panic, in every build, as a fail-stop. In `runtime.rs` each part of the node is its own thread: the controller, I/O, clock and log writer. A panic ends only its own thread, and nothing watches the others: the death is seen only when `Node::shutdown` joins them. Nothing sets `panic = "abort"`, no panic hook exists, and no thread catches an unwind.

What each death leaves:
- **Controller panics** (any core `invariant!`, or `IO-QUEUE` / `INBOX-UNREFUSABLE`):
  - the ticker, I/O and log threads keep running;
  - `Inbox::offer` keeps accepting client attempts and peer messages (up to 1,024) that nobody will ever answer;
  - `Node::snapshot()` stays frozen at its last publish, normally `lifecycle: Ready`, so W18.3's `/v1/health/ready` would report ready.
- **I/O thread panics** (a `FsStorage` invariant, or `IO-STORAGE-ONLY`): the Ready waiting for its `SyncDone` never resolves, which §7.12 forbids ("a waiting Ready always resolves"). The node takes no input again. Reads are still served from the old applied prefix, and writes time out as `unknown_outcome`. The next `Io::push` then panics the controller too (`IO-QUEUE`, disconnected).
- **Ticker panics:** ticks stop. No election timeouts, heartbeats or write deadlines ever fire again, silently.
- **Log writer exits** on a write error: every later record is dropped and counted, but nothing says why until shutdown.

## Requirements
CD-7 (invariants are fail-stop in all builds), §7.12 (a waiting Ready always resolves), A-2 (never serve as Ready when not), O-1/O-3 (health and logs tell the truth).

## Area
`crates/server` (`runtime.rs`, possibly `Cargo.toml` profile or `main.rs`).

## Acceptance
- A panic on any node thread stops the node: the process exits (for example `panic = "abort"` for the server's release profile, or a hook), or every other thread stops and the snapshot reads `failed`. It is never left half-alive.
- A test injects a panic on the controller thread and on the I/O thread (test-only failpoint, rule 17). It shows the node stops, or reports `failed`, and that no later client attempt is accepted unanswered.
- `./dev check SERVER-RUNTIME` passes; T0 green.

## Out of scope
W18.3's HTTP layer, beyond reading the snapshot.

title: raft_adapter: group-encoded unknown fields slip past decode_message, so 'refused at every depth' overclaims (H-3)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9. Both reviewers (Opus and Fable) raised it as P2, and I verified it in protobuf 2.28.0.

**Unknown fields encoded as groups are skipped by the protobuf runtime rather than stored, so `decode_message` admits them. "Unknown fields refused at every depth" overclaims.**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/raft_adapter/src/convert.rs:84-93` refuses only what `get_unknown_fields()` holds on the Message and its entries.
- protobuf-2.28.0 `rt.rs:812-826` (`read_unknown_or_skip_group`) matches `WireTypeStartGroup => skip_group(is)` and never adds to `unknown_fields`.
- Failure: the test heartbeat `08 08 10 01 18 02 20 03 40 01` followed by `C3 3E 08 01 C4 3E` (field 1000 start-group, a varint, field 1000 end-group), in a valid envelope, is decoded, admitted, opened and stepped. The same happens inside an `Entry`.
- Fable also found an over-long nested Entry length that decodes silently from a slice-backed stream: `limit = NO_LIMIT`, buf_read_iter.rs:100-108 and 147-162.
- Determinism is not harmed, because a skipped group is neither stored nor re-encoded. But these all claim more than the code does:
  - admit.rs:21-23;
  - the PEER-ADMISSION summary (`registry/checks.toml`, `xtask/src/check.rs`);
  - DEPENDENCIES.md's protobuf row ("the adapter refuses any message that carries one");
  - br-xx08's acceptance ("unknown fields at any depth").
- No test uses a group.

## Requirements
W02 audit H-3; DEPENDENCIES.md protobuf row; CD-3; §10.15 (claims in their class); P10.

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (convert.rs, admit_tests.rs); PEER-ADMISSION row; possibly the DEPENDENCIES.md wording (a facade turn).

## Acceptance
- `decode_message` requires canonical bytes, `message.write_to_bytes()? == bytes`, alongside the stored-unknown-field check. Every message a v1 peer sends is encoded by this same generated encoder.
- New raw-byte tests:
  - a group at the top level and inside an Entry;
  - one each of the fixed32, fixed64 and length-delimited unknown wire types;
  - an over-long nested length, a duplicate field and a non-minimal varint.
- The "every depth" wording is then true. Otherwise it is narrowed everywhere it appears.
- The sealed three-voter cluster test still passes.

## Out of scope
Pre-decode allocation bounds (the sibling bead).

title: RAFT-AUDIT: static scan keeping W02.2's 'none on any path' verdicts true in vendor/raft
description:
## Context
The W02.2 audit (spike/raft-audit.md) proved by reading tree 4ab81467 that vendored raft-rs has:
- exactly one entropy site (raft.rs:2807-2819, thread_rng);
- no clocks, no threads on production paths, no randomly seeded maps other than quorum.rs AckIndexer (test-only), and no pointer formatting.
A vendor update or the W02.3 patch could silently break these verdicts.

## Requirements
P4, T-3; PLAN §7.3 (the audit's 'unproven items get a test').

## Area
xtask: a new leaf module plus a check.rs catalogue row. These are shared facades, so sequence them in Agent Mail thread xtask-shared-facades.

## Design
A static check over vendor/raft/*/src, excluding #[cfg(test)] modules, *_test.rs and doc comments. It fails on:
- thread_rng or rand:: (expected count 1 before W02.3, 0 after; the expected count lives in VENDOR.toml or the check);
- Instant, SystemTime or thread::spawn;
- std::collections::HashMap or HashSet outside quorum.rs's AckIndexer;
- {:p}.
Each violation names the file and line.

## Acceptance
./dev check RAFT-AUDIT passes on the committed tree with nonzero cases. Fixtures, one per forbidden pattern, make it fail.

## Out of scope
Changing vendored files.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: Design note (JadeOx). The bead's literal rule, 'std::collections::HashMap or HashSet outside quorum.rs AckIndexer', would fail on the current tree: raft/src/lib.rs:605-607 names std::collections::HashMap/HashSet to define the crate's FxHash aliases, which the W02.2 audit (H-1) judges deterministic per build. RAFT-AUDIT therefore targets the actual hazard, a randomly seeded std collection. It flags RandomState; std HashMap/HashSet named or imported with the default hasher; and any use of a std-bound HashMap/HashSet name, except quorum.rs's import and its 'type AckIndexer' (H-2). A qualified std collection whose last generic argument is DefaultHashBuilder is allowed only while every 'type DefaultHashBuilder' is exactly std::hash::BuildHasherDefault<fxhash::FxHasher>; that pin is checked too. Other rules: entropy (thread_rng, rand:: paths, extern crate rand) is counted per source line against EXPECTED_ENTROPY_SITES = 0 (post-W02.3); Instant and SystemTime; thread::spawn, scope and Builder; and {:p}-style format specs in string literals. Pointer casts are not flagged, because majority.rs:84 has a legitimate 'as *mut _' that formats nothing. Excluded: comments (doc comments included), #[cfg(test)] items (inline only, because lib.rs declares raft both #[cfg(test)] and #[cfg(not(test))]), #![cfg(test)] files and *_test.rs. Acceptance labels: accept:RAFT-AUDIT for the static check on the committed tree; the per-pattern fixtures are unit tests in xtask/src/raft_audit.rs that run in XTASK and the T0 gate.

title: Bound accept trees and per-checkout target dirs (~470 MB each; disk at 6.8 GB free)
description:
## Context
Every checkout path now builds into its own cargo target dir (br-gate-shared-target-dir-dtqu): `$KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE/keyval-checkout-<sha256(realpath)[:16]>`, about 470 MB each. W07.3's `./dev accept` materialises each tree into `.local/accept/<tree-id>/` (PLAN §11.3 step 7, W07 acceptance), so every accepted tree adds a new target dir, a ~1 min cold build. The same holds for each worker's frozen candidate copies. Nothing removes them: §10.10 makes `./dev prune` (W46, M4) the **only** sanctioned deletion of generated `.local/` artifacts, under the Q9 rule (keep the last 5 gate runs, the last 5 accept trees, and every failing run's artifacts).

Measured 2026-10-03: free disk on `/` fell from 9.3 GB to 6.8 GB in one afternoon of M0 work (38 GB disk). At ~470 MB per accept, roughly a dozen more closures exhaust the disk, long before W46 exists.

## Requirements
CD-9 (a limit on everything), Q9 retention, §10.10 prune policy. Coordinate with W46.

## Decision needed (owner)
Pick one:
- (a) Land the Q9 subset of `./dev prune` now. It covers accept trees and their target dirs plus stale per-checkout target dirs whose checkout path no longer exists, and logs every removal in a receipt. W46 then extends it.
- (b) Accept trees share one target dir. That reverses the per-checkout rule for accept, which is safe only because each accept tree is freshly materialised.
- (c) Manual owner cleanup until W46.

## Acceptance (for a)
- `./dev prune` keeps the newest 5 accept trees and every failing run's artifacts.
- It removes older accept trees together with their `keyval-checkout-*` target dirs.
- It logs each removal in a receipt.
- A dry-run mode exists.
- Fixtures cover the retention boundary (N−1/N/N+1).

## Out of scope
T1–T3 run retention (W46).

title: BUG: fs_storage's lock tests can see a released lock held: the two-process test's child inherits a sibling test's LOCK flock until exec
description:
## Context
This is the same race class as the DOCTOR-CLI flake, found while tracing it. It hasn't been seen failing yet.

`crates/fs_storage/src/lib.rs`'s unit tests run on parallel threads. One of them, `a_second_process_is_refused_the_lock_until_the_first_exits`, spawns `/proc/self/exe` twice. A child spawned while another test thread holds a LOCK fd inherits that flock until it execs, as reproduced for the doctor flake: 216 of 2,000 releases were still held.

The tests that release a lock and then expect it free are the exposed ones:
- `a_live_directory_is_reported_live_and_an_examined_one_cannot_start`: after `drop(node)` it expects `LockProbe::Acquired`.
- `examining_a_directory_creates_and_changes_nothing`: `used_dir()` locks and drops, then it expects `Acquired`.
- Any later test of the same shape.

## Requirements
DUR-8 (single-node lock), W01.6 rule 4, P10.

## Area
`crates/fs_storage/src/lib.rs` (tests module only).

## Acceptance
- No unit test in fs_storage's lib test binary spawns a process while sibling threads may hold a lock. For example, move the two-process lock test into its own integration-test binary, `crates/fs_storage/tests/lock_process.rs` with `#![cfg(test)]`, where no sibling test locks. Or prove another way that no flock is inherited.
- FS-STORAGE's selector still selects the moved case.
- `./dev check FS-STORAGE` passes with min_cases unchanged; T0 green.

## Out of scope
The doctor fixture (the sibling bug).

title: journal log: the no-mutation-on-refusal test proves it for 1 of 7 refusals, and a vote for a non-voter is refused only in recovery, not on live append (CD-10)
description:

**1. The test that claims refusals change nothing proves it for one refusal of seven.**
- `crates/journal/src/log_tests.rs:189-193`: the `apply` helper runs on `log.clone()`, which is dropped, so only the error value is compared (`:243-245`).
- The only `assert_eq!(refusing, before)` (`:246-251`) follows one `append` whose error is not pinned.
- `NotRaftBatch`, `Sequence`, `Offset`, `Gap` and `CommitBeyondLog` are never shown to leave the log unchanged, although `log.rs:429` claims "On error, nothing changes".
- Opus showed the consequence: moving the `CommitBeyondLog` check after `self.positions.truncate(kept)` breaks no test. The code is right today by inspection (every check precedes the first mutation at `log.rs:485`), but the claim is unpinned (P10).

**2. Live appends and recovery disagree about a vote for a non-voter.**
- `crates/journal/src/recovery.rs:400-405` refuses a hard state whose vote is not a genesis voter.
- `LogicalLog::apply` and `check_hard_state` (`log.rs:430`, `:520-540`) have no voter set, so the live path persists such a frame. The node then runs normally and refuses to start on its next restart.
- This contradicts `log.rs:4-6`: live appends and recovery "apply frames through the same `LogicalLog::apply`, so the two can never disagree about what a journal means (CD-10)".

## Requirements
CD-10 (one source of truth for what a journal means), CD-7, P10, §7.6 ("Replacing at or below the persisted commit index is an invariant violation"; refusals before mutation), DUR-6.

## Area
crates/journal (`log.rs`, `log_tests.rs`, `recovery.rs`).

## Acceptance
- Each refusal case of `every_refusal_leaves_the_log_unchanged` asserts that the log equals `before` after the refused call, as well as the exact error.
- A mutation-order mutant, for example moving one check after `positions.truncate`, would now fail a test.
- The voter check moves into the shared path (for example, `LogBounds` or `after_genesis` carries the genesis voters, and `check_hard_state` refuses), so live and recovery give the same verdict. There is a test that a live append with a non-voter vote is refused before mutating.
- JOURNAL-LOG and JOURNAL-RECOVERY pass with raised min_cases.

## Out of scope
New refusal kinds.

title: PLAN: state the canonical command format v1 in §7.5, so the reference model counts DM-7 command bytes independently of the codec
description:
## Context
DM-7's byte half counts, at each first execution, "the canonical encoded length of the command" (§7.5, D-62). But PLAN.md defines that encoding only as "one canonical, versioned byte encoding, at most 66 KiB". The layout exists only in `crates/statemachine/src/codec.rs`'s module doc (W09.1, check COMMAND-CODEC).

The reference model (`crates/model`, an oracle, T-12) is written from the plan alone (§11.7, RISK-8). It therefore cannot count committed command bytes without either copying the implementation's own spec or being handed the length. That blocks the byte half of br-q37e: the model's DM-7 accounting, DIFFERENTIAL comparing `committed_command_bytes`, and the model server's byte-limit `history_full`.

## Decision so far (dialog answered via cc_1 overnight, 2026-10-04; recommendation adopted, logged for the owner)
- br-q37e lands only its plan-defined **entry** half now: the model refuses once the commit index reaches `max_log_entries`.
- The byte half waits for this bead.
- Rejected options:
  - the model computing the length from codec.rs's doc now (the oracle's spec would come from the implementation until ratified);
  - the length passed in as data (the model server could not compute it);
  - deferring all of q37e.

## Ask (owner)
Make the v1 command format normative in §7.5, under "Commands". The proposed text copies codec.rs's table exactly, so no code changes:

> **Canonical command format, version 1** (`COMMAND_FORMAT_VERSION`, fingerprinted, DUR-8). Fields in this order, with no padding, alternatives or trailing bytes; integers big-endian:
>
> | Field | Bytes | Encoding |
> |---|---|---|
> | format version | 1 | `1` |
> | kind | 1 | `1` PUT, `2` DELETE, `3` compare-and-swap |
> | request ID | 16 | its 128 bits, most significant byte first |
> | key length | 4 | `u32` |
> | key | key length | UTF-8, 1 byte to the key limit |
> | expectation (CAS only) | 1 | `0` absent, `1` a version |
> | expected version (expectation `1` only) | 8 | `u64`, 1 to 2^53 − 1 |
> | value length (PUT, CAS) | 4 | `u32` |
> | value (PUT, CAS) | value length | UTF-8, 0 bytes to the value limit |
>
> So a command's canonical length, as the DM-7 byte counter adds it, is 22 + key bytes for DELETE; 26 + key + value bytes for PUT; and 27 (absent) or 35 (a version) + key + value bytes for CAS. The largest envelope is 35 B (`MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES`).

Add a §16 decision row too, for example: "The canonical command format v1 is stated in the plan, so the reference model computes DM-7's byte counter independently of the codec."

The alternative is to state only the length rule, the last paragraph above, and leave the byte layout to the codec.

## Requirements
DM-5, DM-7, §7.5, D-62, T-7, T-12.

## Area
PLAN.md (owner).

## Acceptance
- PLAN.md §7.5 states the v1 command format, or at least its length rule.
- COMMAND-CODEC still passes unchanged.
- br-q37e's byte half then lands: the model counts first-execution command bytes from the plan's rule, and DIFFERENTIAL compares the counter with `StateMachine::committed_command_bytes`.

## Out of scope
Any change to the format itself; a v2 format.

comments.author: PeachAnchor
comments.text:
## A second question for the same plan change: which limit `history_full` names when both are reached (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04)

Both independent reviewers of br-q37e's entry half (Opus and Fable) raised this.

`507 history_full` names exactly one `limit` (§8.4; `api/openapi.yaml` HistoryLimit: `max_log_entries` | `max_history_bytes`). DM-7 doesn't say which one a refusal names when the commit index has reached `max_log_entries` **and** the committed command bytes have reached `max_history_bytes`. DM-6 had the same gap; that one is br-dm6-limit-order-31o5 / br-wz9r, decided keys first.

The reference model and W29.3's production admission must answer alike, or the conformance checkers diverge on such a write.

**Suggestion:** entries first, matching how DM-7 and §7.11 list them ("commit index … **or** … bytes") and DM-6's keys-first precedent. Please state the order in DM-7 or §7.11 together with the command format.

The model currently enforces only `max_log_entries`, and `HistoryLimit`'s doc points here, so nothing is decided silently in the meantime.

title: BUG: registry condition 7 accepts only checker-kind catchers, so §10.6's designated catchers (registry gate, conformance, fixtures) cannot be registered
description:
## Context

| B-20 | "Conformance suite (§10.8)" | PLAN.md:1174 |

title: BUG: Config/ConsensusSettings hand bare u64s across the types boundary for node ID, ticks, byte sizes and counts (CD-4)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Fable reviewer, verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e).

The validated `Config` and `ConsensusSettings` hand **bare `u64`s** across the `types` boundary for identifiers, ticks, byte sizes and counts, although the crate already has `NodeId`, `Tick`, `ByteCount` and `LogIndex`.

**Evidence (HEAD 1b2cf2e):**
- `crates/types/src/config/consensus.rs:133-181`:
  - `node_id() -> u64`;
  - `heartbeat_tick`, `election_tick`, `min_election_tick`, `max_election_tick` (ticks);
  - `max_size_per_msg`, `max_uncommitted_size`, `max_committed_size_per_ready` (bytes);
  - `max_inflight_msgs` (a count).
- `crates/types/src/config/mod.rs`:
  - `:248` `max_live_keys() -> u64`;
  - `:260` `max_log_entries() -> u64` (compared with a `LogIndex` under DM-7);
  - `:284` `replication_inflight_batches()`;
  - `:290` `peer_send_queue_messages()`;
  - and similar accessors.

`ConsensusSettings` is the type that crosses into `raft_adapter` (W13). Nothing in the type system stops a caller from passing any `u64` where the validated node ID was meant. `max_log_entries` will be compared with a `LogIndex` through an ad-hoc conversion at every call site.

No wrong result today, because the values come only from a validated `Config`. This is a gap against the plan rule, and the fix is mechanical.

## Requirements
CD-4: "No bare integers or strings cross a module boundary for identifiers, indices or counts … `NodeId`, …, `Tick`, …, `ByteCount` … are separate types". D-79: core-owned types for the library's settings.

## Overlap
br-w08-3-limits-registry-wrappers-sh6 (W08.3, SunnyDog, in progress) introduces bounded wrapper types for the §7.11 limits (CD-9). The *count and limit* accessors may naturally be converted there. The node ID, ticks and byte sizes in `ConsensusSettings` are separate from that. Coordinate with SunnyDog.

## Area
types (`config/consensus.rs`, `config/mod.rs`).

## Acceptance
- `ConsensusSettings::node_id()` returns `NodeId`.
- Tick values return `Tick`, byte sizes return `ByteCount`, and counts return a counted type or W08.3's bounded wrappers.
- The adapter-facing conversion to library `u64`s happens only in `raft_adapter` (W13).
- CONFIG-RULES and CONFIG-FINGERPRINT still pass.

## Out of scope
Changing any value or range.

title: BUG: AGENTS.md drifts from PLAN section 11.5 (rules 3 and 12, git session boilerplate)
description:
## Conflict (filed per PLAN.md §0.4 — lower source corrected to match higher; PLAN.md wins)

The committed AGENTS.md restatement of the §11.5 agent rules has drifted from PLAN.md v1.6:

1. **Rule 12 contradicts D-72.** AGENTS.md (## Agent Rules, rule 12) says: "When you close a bead that implements a requirement, set it to `active`." PLAN.md §11.5 rule 12 (revised v1.5, decision D-72) says the OPPOSITE: "**Never edit a requirement's status by hand:** activation is derived by `./dev commit --close` when the last listing bead closes (§10.13), and the registry gate rejects hand-edited statuses." An agent following AGENTS.md as written would hand-edit `registry/requirements.toml` and be rejected by the W05 gate — or worse, re-introduce the premature-activation bug D-72 closed.
2. **Rule 3 omits the `conflict` label.** AGENTS.md rule 3 says a genuine checker/model bug gets a bead labelled `needs-owner`; PLAN.md §11.5 rule 3 requires ONE bead with BOTH labels `conflict` AND `needs-owner` (§13 item 10 counts `conflict` beads, so the omission would let a checker-bug bead escape the Definition-of-Done check).
3. **Minor:** the tool-generated "Beads Workflow Integration" section's "Session Protocol" shows raw `git add` / `git commit` / `git push`, contradicting this repo's Git Discipline section (commits only via `./dev commit`; no remote exists). The bv-generated trailer's Git Policy note partially mitigates; the hand-written sections win, but the contradiction inside one file invites mistakes during the bootstrap window where raw commits ARE temporarily in use.

## Resolution
AGENTS.md is below PLAN.md in precedence, so AGENTS.md is corrected to match §11.5 verbatim on rules 3 and 12. The natural vehicle is W01.5 (writes AGENTS.md with all 18 rules; its acceptance requires every §11.5 rule present — W01's gate checks the list). For item 3, add a one-line banner in the Git Discipline section stating it overrides any tool-generated git instructions below. Close this bead when the committed AGENTS.md matches §11.5 exactly.

Both locations cited: AGENTS.md lines "## Agent Rules" items 3 and 12 + "### Session Protocol"; PLAN.md §11.5 rules 3 and 12, §10.13 (status lifecycle), D-72.
acceptance_criteria: Committed AGENTS.md matches section 11.5 verbatim on rules 3 and 12; Git Discipline section states it overrides tool-generated git instructions; verified by W01 gate check of the rule list
notes: Second-round audit readback: the shared checkout already contains the rule-3 dual-label correction, receipt-derived rule-12 activation, and the Git Discipline override banner. Preserve those prior edits. This existing conflict stays open until its required committed-tree acceptance receipt exists; a correct working-copy readback alone does not permit closure.

title: BUG: DataDir create_journal/sync_dir are synchronous in-process calls, so DUR-7's create/dir-sync crash point cannot be scheduled
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W04.3's ports (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand; medium confidence).

The data-directory steps that **mutate** state are synchronous in-process calls. The plan limits in-process ports to entropy and bounded **reads**, and it requires mutating operations to be separately scheduled fault points. With `create_journal()` and `sync_dir()` called back to back inside one core step, the simulator cannot place a scheduled crash between file creation and the directory sync.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01):**
- `crates/types/src/in_process.rs:98-118`: `trait DataDir { fn lock(&mut self); fn create_journal(&mut self); fn sync_dir(&mut self) }`, all returning `Result<(), StorageError>` synchronously.
- `PLAN.md` §7.2: in-process ports are "entropy, and bounded **reads** from byte storage". The byte-storage row's kind is "effect + in-process reads", and it lists "create file + sync directory; exclusive lock".
- `PLAN.md` §10.2:
  - "a crash between create and directory sync loses the file (DUR-7 has a simulated crash point …)";
  - "mutating operations and sync boundaries are separately scheduled fault points".
- The W04.3 bead text did list these as in-process calls. PLAN.md wins (§0.4), so this may also need a `conflict` note.

Scenario: W12's simulated disk can't schedule the DUR-7 crash point. It could only fake one by failing from inside the call, which is a different fault from a crash.

## Requirements
DUR-7, §7.2, §10.2, T-14 (complements).

## Area
types (`in_process.rs`, `effects.rs`); its consumers are W11, W12 and W14.

## Acceptance
- `create_journal` and `sync_dir` become effects with incarnation-stamped completions, in the same way as `Append`/`Sync`.
- `lock` stays in-process: it is a boot-time precondition, not a crash point.
- If the owner decides otherwise, record that decision instead.
- A test shows the sim adapter can schedule a crash between `create_journal` and `sync_dir`, once W12 exists. A port-shape test is enough here.

## Out of scope
The real-file probes (W24).

title: Test the §7.7 restart path through the Ready loop: a node built at its replayed applied index must hand over nothing at or below it
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.2, the Ready loop (VioletOwl; br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa, 7eb3316), for cc_1 on 2026-10-04. The review was at HEAD 7ec6be4, by SunnyDog plus two independent fresh reviewers (Opus and Fable). Both reviewers raised it as P2, and SunnyDog verified it in the tests. Thread: br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa.

**The production path.** On restart (§7.7 steps 5-6), the node replays the state machine to the persisted commit, then constructs `RaftNode::new(.., applied = replayed)`. Correctness rests on three things:
- `Raft::new` calls `commit_apply(c.applied)` after `load_state` (raft.rs:397-402);
- `RawNode` sets `commit_since_index = config.applied` (raw_node.rs:320);
- `ReadyLoop::new` reads `raft_log.applied` (ready_loop.rs:152).

If any of them drifts, the first committed entry after a restart either hands over entries already replayed (applying them twice) or trips `RA-APPLY-ORDER` on every node.

**No test runs it:**
- `a_commit_after_a_restart_drains_past_the_per_ready_bound_within_one_sync` constructs the restarted node with `applied = LogIndex::ZERO` (`member_over`, ready_loop_tests.rs:55-62) and lets the loop re-apply 1..commit.
- `node_tests::a_restarted_node_keeps_its_term_and_refuses_an_applied_index_past_commit` and `a_restart_through_recovery_resumes_the_persisted_term_vote_commit_and_log` construct at `commit`, but never take a Ready.

## Requirements
- §7.7 steps 5-7.
- §7.4 step 5: entries apply once each, in index order.
- C-4.

## Area
raft_adapter tests (`ready_loop_tests.rs`).

## Acceptance
- A loop test over a recovered log constructs the node with `applied = k`, for 0 < k < the persisted commit and for k = the persisted commit. It then calls `poll` and commits a new entry. Assert:
  - the first entry handed to `Apply` is k+1;
  - nothing at or below k is handed over;
  - `applied()` and `node().applied_index()` end at the new commit.
- RAFT-READY-LOOP's min_cases is raised to match, and T0 is green.

## Out of scope
The state machine's replay itself (W14, W11).

title: BUG: peer envelopes queued before a node fails during a sync are never drained or counted, and keep their queue slots
description:
## Context
Found in the review of W14.1 (906fc83) for cc_1, 2026-10-04: the second, independent pass (Fable), reproduced by PeachAnchor. The code is unchanged at HEAD (6b84d9d).

**Peer envelopes queued before a node fails during a sync are never drained or counted, and they keep their queue slots.**

A storage failure typically arrives while the loop has a sync outstanding, for example a failed fsync (`StorageFailed { op: Sync(seq) }`).
- `Controller::sync_done` returns early once the node is `Failed`, so the loop's `outstanding_sync()` stays `Some` forever.
- `turn` then computes `peers_wait = self.raft.outstanding_sync().is_some()`, which is always `true`.
- So `queue.next(true)` never yields a peer.

The envelopes queued during that sync are never handed to `peer()`, which would drop them and count them under `peers_failed`. They stay in the 1,024-input queue for the incarnation's lifetime.

## Evidence
A scratch test, not committed, in `/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-keyval/d767163f-b7de-47a1-82c3-b6219ddfff4a/scratchpad/candidate/crates/node/src/review_scratch_tests.rs` (`peers_queued_before_a_failure_are_stranded`).
- **Setup:** a one-voter node with a sync outstanding gets three peer envelopes, which are queued because peers wait. Then its sync fails, and it gets 50 ticks.
- **Result:** lifecycle `Failed`; queued 3 (unchanged); outstanding sync `Some(1)`; `peers_failed` 0; codec drops 0.

The failure test `a_failed_storage_effect_fails_the_node_which_stops_feeding_raft` steps a peer only after failing (admission-time dropping), so this path is untested.

## Why it is a defect
- DM-7 and §7.11 say a failed node drops peer messages "and counts" them, and answers clients `recovering` (A-2). Here they are neither dropped nor counted (CD-9: never silent).
- If the queue filled with peer envelopes during the stalled sync, which is exactly when peers accumulate, every later client attempt gets `429 busy` at admission. The policy never gets to answer `recovering`, so the node reports the wrong state until it restarts.

## Requirements
DM-7, A-2, §7.11, CD-9.

## Area
`crates/node` (controller.rs): W14's area.

## Acceptance
- Once the node is `Failed`, queued peer envelopes leave the queue and are counted under `peers_failed`. For example, `peers_wait` is `outstanding && lifecycle != Failed`, or `fail()` drains and counts the peer lane.
- A test queues peers during a sync, fails that sync, and asserts the queue empties, `peers_failed` counts them, and a later client attempt reaches the policy (`recovering`), not `busy`.
- NODE-CONTROLLER passes with `min_cases` raised.

## Out of scope
Recovering a failed node (it restarts, §7.7).

comments.author: PeachAnchor
comments.text:
## Closure: br-dkov (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04)

**Work:** ba53c1f, tree 51da6f83, on parent b81c774 (after br-m7x7 6dce003 and br-0fha 294b5dd).
- The private gate passed on 78e696a0, the same 7 paths on 294b5dd: 83/83, NODE-CONTROLLER 37.
- The wrapper's gate then passed on the first attempt (`artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261004T083440Z-51da6f8339cf-3490064.json`).

**Accept:** passed on tree 51da6f83. `./dev check NODE-CONTROLLER` passed with 37 cases. Receipt: `artifacts/receipts/accept-br-dkov-51da6f8339cf-20261004T083749Z-3519852.json`.

**The fix:**
- `Controller::fail`, the only way into `failed`, now drains the peer lane through `InboundQueue::drain_peers`, adds the count to `peers_failed`, and logs one `Dropped { PeerMessage }` per envelope. Later envelopes are dropped at admission, as before.
- `peers_wait` is untouched, so the fix holds with br-0fha's `peers_wait = self.syncing()`.
- `peer()`'s failed-node branch could no longer run, so it is now the CD-7 invariant NODE-FAILED-PEERS, with a firing fixture.

**The bead's acceptance:**
- Queued envelopes leave the queue and are counted under `peers_failed`.
- A test queues peers during a sync, fails that sync, and asserts the queue empties, `peers_failed` counts them (with one log record each), and nothing is left or counted twice after 10 ticks.
- A second test fills the queue with 1,024 envelopes at the failure. A later client attempt reaches the request lifecycle (as `Failed`, whose policy answers `recovering`), not `busy`.
- With the drain disabled, both tests fail (a scratch negative control).
- NODE-CONTROLLER `min_cases` 28 → 32.

**Fix verification by the original reviewer (me), against HEAD ba53c1f:**
- My review reproduction: a failed Sync with 3 envelopes queued, then 50 ticks. Now `queued 0, peers_failed 3`; before, it was 3 queued and 0 counted.
- A variant: a failed Append with 5 queued, then 4 more arrive. Now `queued 0, peers_failed 9`.

**Review:** two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable), no P1 or P2. The P3s both raised are done.
- **Reported, not changed:** NODE-CONTROLLER's `invariant_fixtures::` filter also selects W14.2's write-path fixtures, 4 cases of slack. That is VioletOwl's selector and is flagged in the W14 thread.

**Claims:** invariant tests of the controller on the cases they name (§10.15).

title: PLAN: which DM-6 limit a write that breaches both max_live_keys and max_live_bytes reports (keys first, as W09.3 implements)
description:
## Context
W09.3 (DM-6 live-state quota) found a gap in PLAN.md §7.5. A PUT, or a matching CAS, that creates a new key can breach both `max_live_keys` and `max_live_bytes` at once. The `507 capacity_exceeded` body names exactly one `limit` (§8.4, `api/openapi.yaml` CapacityExceededError `limit`), but §7.5 step 4 says only "if it would create a key or grow bytes beyond DM-6 → `capacity_exceeded`".

W10's reference model is written independently from the plan's prose (§11.7, RISK-8). It must pick the same limit, or the conformance checkers diverge on such a write.

## Decision taken for W09.3 (dialog answered via cc_1 overnight, 2026-10-04; recommendation adopted, logged for the owner)
**Keys first.**
- A write that would create a key while the live key count is at `max_live_keys` gets `limit = max_live_keys`, whatever its bytes.
- Only otherwise is growth beyond `max_live_bytes` checked, giving `limit = max_live_bytes`.

This follows §7.5's own word order, "create a key or grow bytes". It is recorded on br-w09-3-capacity-counters-gel.

## Ask (owner)
Record the order in §7.5 step 4, and the DM-6 row if useful, plus a §16 decision row, so that W10, W27 (CAS) and W40 follow it. Or choose the other order, in which case W09.3's code is changed to match.

## Requirements
DM-6, F-1, F-5, §7.5, §8.4.

## Area
PLAN.md (owner).

## Acceptance
PLAN.md states which limit a write that breaches both quotas reports, and W09.3's tests (CAPACITY) assert that order.

## Out of scope
The quota values.

title: BUG: StateMachine::live_keys() returns a bare usize across the statemachine boundary (CD-4); return ItemCount before W09.3's DM-6 check compares it with max_live_keys()
description:
## Context
Found in the fresh-eyes review of W09.1 (dd333d6), by PeachAnchor for cc_1 on 2026-10-04. Both reviewers flagged it: an independent second reviewer rated it P2, I rated it P3, and it is filed at P2 for consistency with the w23k precedent (VioletOwl's second review rated the same CD-4 bare-count pattern P2). The rest of W09.1 reviewed clean (summary in thread review-statemachine-w09-1-2026-10-04).

`StateMachine::live_keys()` is a public method on the crate's main exported type, and it returns a bare `usize`:
- `crates/statemachine/src/apply.rs:97-101`: `pub fn live_keys(&self) -> usize { self.map.len() }`.
- `types::ItemCount` exists for exactly this. Its documentation reads "A number of items: live keys (DM-6), …" (`crates/types/src/counts.rs`). `Config::max_live_keys()` returns `ItemCount` (`crates/types/src/config/mod.rs:254`) since 83575df (w23k), which landed shortly before W09.1.

**Why it matters next.** W09.3's DM-6 quota check compares the live-key count with `config.max_live_keys()`. With this signature it can only do so through a hand-made conversion such as `u64::try_from(state.live_keys())` against `.get()`. That is the raw integer comparison CD-4 bans, and the W10 reference model and W14's health and status code would copy it. No check covers it today: NEWTYPES runs only `types` tests, and `statemachine` has no public-API audit.

## Requirements
CD-4 (PLAN.md §5.2): "A distinct type for each kind of quantity. No bare integers or strings cross a module boundary for identifiers, indices or counts. Arithmetic is checked." Also DM-6.

## Area
statemachine (`crates/statemachine/src/apply.rs`); VioletOwl's W09 chain. Folding it into W09.3, which adds the DM-6 comparison, is cheapest.

## Acceptance
- `live_keys()` returns `ItemCount`, built with a checked conversion from `map.len()`.
- Any live-byte counter W09.3 adds is a `ByteCount`.
- W09.3's DM-6 check compares typed values with no raw `u64` conversion at the call site.
- APPLY-PUT passes.

## Out of scope

title: raft_adapter: admission lets term-0 messages through; a forged term-0 vote request makes raft-rs fatal! (node panic)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9, for cc_1. Opus reviewer: P1. I verified it by hand in the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0. admit.rs, convert.rs, envelope.rs and node.rs are unchanged at the time of filing.

**Admission lets through messages with term 0 for every admitted type, and one forged vote request with term 0 makes raft-rs `fatal!` (the node panics).**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/raft_adapter/src/admit.rs:100-110` bounds terms above 2^53−1 but never refuses `message.term == 0`.
- v1 never sends term 0:
  - `RaftCore::send` (vendor/raft/raft/src/raft.rs:643-660) calls `fatal!` on a vote or pre-vote message, or a response to one, with term 0;
  - every other message is stamped with `self.term` ≥ 1.
- `Raft::step` treats `m.term == 0` as a local message and skips every term rule (raft.rs:1342).

**Failure** (verified in the source):
1. Voter 7 seals the payload `08 05 10 01 18 07` (MsgRequestVote, to=1, from=7, no term field) for a fresh node 1 with matching identity.
2. `open` passes, and so do admission and binding.
3. `step` takes the local branch, then the vote branch. On a fresh node `can_vote` holds and `is_up_to_date(0,0)` is true, so it grants with `to_send.term = m.term = 0` (raft.rs:1478-1503).
4. `send` hits `fatal!("term should be set when sending MsgRequestVoteResponse")`.

The reject branch echoes `self.term`, which is also 0 on a fresh node. MsgRequestPreVote behaves the same.

**Also, with term-0 MsgAppend:**
- At a candidate, it hits `debug_assert_eq!(self.term, m.term)` (raft.rs:2285): a panic in test and sim builds. In release, `become_follower(0)` regresses the term, and the journal later fails the node (TermRegression).
- At a follower, an empty term-0 MsgAppend advances commit through `maybe_append` with no term check.

br-xx08 (P1) exists to keep library `fatal!` paths away from peer input (admit.rs:3-7). PLAN §2.2 puts Byzantine faults out of scope, but a correct v1 peer never sends term 0, so refusing it costs nothing and closes the gap br-xx08 claims to close.

## Requirements
§7.3, §7.8, §8.2; br-xx08's acceptance; W02 audit S-1; CD-3 and CD-8 (no panic on peer input).

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (admit.rs, admit_tests.rs); PEER-ADMISSION row (a facade turn for min_cases).

## Acceptance
- `admit` refuses `term == 0` on all eight admitted types (`OutOfRange`, or a new `Inadmissible` variant).
- New tests:
  - a term-0 MsgRequestVote and a term-0 MsgRequestPreVote stepped into a fresh follower are refused, not panicking;
  - a term-0 MsgAppend and a term-0 MsgHeartbeat are refused.
- PEER-ADMISSION passes with raised min_cases, and the sealed three-voter cluster test still passes (no liveness loss).

## Out of scope
Forged messages with a plausible term (the sibling bead on stateful fatal paths).

title: E2E: CLI-vs-real-cluster journey script, registered as a T1 check — discovered work
description:
## Context (discovered work — closes a coverage gap)
The conformance suite exercises the HTTP API, the lifecycle smoke exercises crash recovery, and W33's tests exercise the CLI — but nothing GATED exercises the full user journey of the real CLI against a real five-node cluster (demo m3 does, but demos are owner-facing, not checks). This bead adds that end-to-end script as a registered T1-tier check, following the W01.6 test-logging standard throughout.

## The journey (scripted, non-interactive, every step logged: action, expected, observed, duration; non-zero exit on first failure)
1. Fresh per-run config + data dirs; `./dev cluster init` + `up`; wait for ready.
2. `keyval put/get` round trip on every node (stale-read polling per §10.8 discipline).
3. Two concurrent `keyval cas` against one version — exactly one success, one `version_mismatch` with the terminal-decision semantics verified via `keyval status`.
4. `keyval delete` (existed true/false), SCAN pagination across Unicode keys with `next_after` continuation.
5. Kill the leader mid-write burst (`./dev cluster kill`); use a bounded fixture that reliably leaves an unresolved request in `keyval pending`; `keyval resume` after restart resolves it with the SAME request ID and exact command. Both legal paths are tested: the earlier attempt committed and resume replays its original result, or it never committed and resume first-executes once. A subsequent same-ID retry/status returns the same first execution index/version, never a second execution.
6. Request-ID misuse: same ID + different command → `request_id_conflict`, nothing changed.
7. `./dev cluster down`; `keyval doctor` green on every stopped data directory.

## Registration
Registered in `registry/checks.toml` (tier t1, covers O-4, C-6, F-6, F-9 end-to-end; min_cases = the journey's step count) with its code marker — so T1 runs it hourly once implemented, per the W46 staging rules. Uses only public surfaces: the CLI, `./dev cluster`, HTTP status endpoints.

## Acceptance
The script passes against a fresh five-node cluster; each step emits a structured log record per the W01.6 standard, tee'd into the gate run's artifact directory; catchable interruption stops receipted processes, and uncatchable script termination leaves durable PID/config receipts that the outer gate harness or next invocation uses to stop only its owned processes (never promise SIGKILL runs cleanup handlers); the registry row resolves and executes with its min_cases.

## Area
`xtask` (script); separately reserve shared registry/checks.toml and output schema paths for registration; exercises `cli` and `server` as black boxes only.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.8 (stale-read discipline), §8.7, O-4, RISK-15, rule 12 (§11.5: register every new check).
acceptance_criteria:
Journey passes against a fresh 5-node cluster; every step logs action/expected/observed/duration per the W01.6 standard; resume-after-kill proves same-ID replay with no double execution; registry row resolves with min_cases; no stray processes
- [ ] Use deterministic public-surface preconditions for both executed-replay and never-executed-first-application resume paths; a timing-dependent leader kill that happens to lose no response cannot count as the unresolved-path assertion. Register the journey before W50, include its receipt in the M4 audit and preserve real CLI/HTTP-only assertions. Test catchable interruption and outer-harness cleanup after SIGKILL via owned PID receipts.
notes: This discovered check supplements the plan; it never changes the 53-item workgraph or activates O-4/C-6/F-6/F-9 through its own closure. Reserve xtask and shared registry/schema surfaces explicitly (§11.7).

title: Resolve a pending same-ID attempt when an entry with another digest for its ID applies (§7.8 Submitted row), instead of waiting for its own entry
description:
Context: found in SunnyDog's review of W14.2 (br-w14-2-write-path-attempts-h2t). The Opus reviewer raised it (P2) and the Fable reviewer raised a facet (P3). Thread: review-w14-2.

PLAN §7.8's Submitted row reads: "on application of an entry carrying R with this attempt's digest: the terminal result (an entry carrying R with a different digest resolves this attempt per §7.5 step 3, never with the other command's result)". The words "the other command's result" make the different-digest entry the other command's entry: when it applies, it resolves this attempt with `request_id_conflict`.

The code doesn't. `WritePath::applied` (crates/node/src/write_path.rs) returns early when the applied entry's digest differs from the pending proposal's. The owner and attached waiters keep waiting for their own entry. On their deadline, or on leadership loss before that entry applies, they answer `unknown_outcome`, although `request_id_conflict` is already decided. A fresh same-ID attempt meanwhile gets the conflict at once from the history (F-7 step 4).

The test `only_an_entry_with_the_attempts_own_command_answers_it` pins the code's reading, against the plan text. Hence the `conflict` label (§0.4: PLAN > tests > code). The plan wins unless the owner or cc_1 reads §7.8 otherwise.

Facets:
- **Behind waiters (Fable).** A waiter behind the pending proposal whose digest equals the applied entry's waits for the pending proposal's own entry, or its deadline (`busy`), although the history already answers it (replay).
- **A Queued pending (SunnyDog).** When another command for R applies before the queued proposal is handed over, the queued proposal is still proposed later, only to apply as a conflict.
- **In-flight bytes (design note).** If a Submitted pending is resolved early, its own copy is still uncommitted in the library's log. Decide whether its bytes stay counted until that copy applies or leadership is lost, or whether the library's synchronous drop stays the backstop.

Requirements: §7.8 (Submitted and attach rows), §7.5 step 3, F-6, F-7 steps 4–5, A-5. W29 accepts the race (`conflict` row). W14 accepts the PUT rows.

Area: crates/node (write_path.rs, write_path_tests.rs). If the case count changes: NODE-WRITE-PATH's min_cases (xtask/src/check.rs, registry/checks.toml) under a short shared reservation.

Acceptance:
- once cc_1 or the owner confirms the reading, an entry carrying R with another digest resolves a pending R proposal:
  - owner and attached waiters answer `request_id_conflict` (original index), never the other command's result;
  - behind waiters are answered from the history (a replay on their own digest, a conflict otherwise);
  - a Queued pending is withdrawn, never proposed;
- the test `only_an_entry_with_the_attempts_own_command_answers_it` is replaced by tests of these three cases;
- the in-flight byte accounting for an early-resolved Submitted pending is decided and tested;
- `./dev check NODE-WRITE-PATH` passes; T0 green.

Out of scope: DELETE/CAS (W27); the double hand-over after a queued expiry (separate P1 bead).
