title: raft_adapter: admitted terms reach 2^53-1 but a node's own next term is one higher: one forged message stalls the cluster, two crash a node (RA-HARD-STATE)
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fix-verification review of the W13.3 codec beads, 2026-10-04, at HEAD c78862b. The independent reviewer raised it as P2, and I checked the path in the vendored source and the adapter.

**Admission accepts any term up to 2^53−1, but a node's own next term is one higher. So a forged term at the ceiling can stall the cluster for good (one message) or crash a node through the adapter's own invariant (two messages).**

**Evidence:**
- admit.rs bounds every peer term at 2^53−1 (R-22). raft-rs's `become_candidate` sets `self.term + 1` (vendor/raft/raft/src/raft.rs:1167), and pre-votes carry term + 1 (raft.rs:1281).
- `RaftNode::core_hard_state` (crates/raft_adapter/src/node.rs:323-338) fires `RA-HARD-STATE` on a term ≥ 2^53, and `term()` (node.rs:378-387) fires `RA-TERM-RANGE`. Its doc ("a node's own term grows by one per election") assumes the ceiling is never reached.

**Liveness, one message:**
1. A forged MsgHeartbeat {term 2^53−1, commit 0} is admitted, and the node follows at that term, persisted.
2. Its pre-votes carry 2^53, which every peer refuses (OutOfRange).
3. It answers the real leader's lower-term messages with higher-term MsgAppendResponses (raft.rs:1435), so the leader steps down. No admissible election term remains, so the cluster can't elect again.

**Crash, two messages:**
1. As above, then a forged MsgRequestPreVoteResponse {term 2^53−1, reject false} to the pre-candidate.
2. Its term equals `self.term`, so it reaches `poll` (raft.rs:2311). The pre-vote is won, `become_candidate` sets the term to 2^53, and the next `ready()` panics at RA-HARD-STATE.

PLAN §2.2 puts Byzantine faults out of scope. But this is a bound the adapter itself states (R-22) without the headroom its own increments need.

## Requirements
R-22, §2.2, §7.3, CD-7, CD-8.

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (admit.rs, node.rs, tests); the PEER-ADMISSION row.

## Acceptance
Either:
- refuse peer terms above 2^53 − 2, so a node's own increment stays in range; or
- add a stateful rule refusing a granted pre-vote response, and a step that would raise the term, while the term is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

In both cases:
- record term-space exhaustion as a stated §2.2 limit next to the PEER-ADMISSION claim;
- tests cover the one-message liveness case and the two-message crash case;
- node.rs's RA-TERM-RANGE doc states the real guarantee.

## Out of scope
The log_term-0 append crash (the sibling P1 bead).

title: BUG: the semantic-config fingerprint omits the SCAN default page size (W08.2 acceptance, DUR-8)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e).

The semantic-config fingerprint's canonical encoding includes the SCAN item cap and the byte cap, but **not the default page size**:
- `crates/types/src/config/fingerprint.rs:75-77` writes `scan_page_max_items` and `scan_page_max_bytes`, and nothing for `PageSize::DEFAULT`.
- `PageSize::DEFAULT` is 32 (`crates/types/src/counts.rs:122`).
- The pinned-encoding test (`fingerprint.rs:121-147`) fixes the omission in place rather than catching it.

**Scenario.**
1. A build changes `PageSize::DEFAULT` to 64. Its fingerprint is byte-identical, so its nodes pass the genesis check (§7.7 step 2) and the peer-envelope check (§8.2) against nodes running the old build.
2. The same `GET /v1/scan` without `limit` then returns 32 or 64 items, depending on which node serves it.

## Requirements
- W08.2's acceptance criterion, in br-w08-2-semantic-fingerprint-pr9: "Fingerprint tests include every fixed semantic SCAN constant (item/**default**/decoded-byte caps and command-format version)".
- §7.10: the fingerprint "covers every parameter that can change a result".
- F-4: "(1–128, default 32)".
- §7.11 SCAN page row: "The caps are fixed semantic constants (part of the fingerprint)".
- DUR-8.

## Area
types (`config/fingerprint.rs`); the pinned `local.toml` fingerprint changes, and with it the fixtures and tests that pin it.

## Acceptance
- The encoding gains `scan_page_default_items=32`, with the encoding version tag bumped because the canonical text changes.
- A test shows the fingerprint changes when the default changes.
- The pinned digest is re-derived independently, and CONFIG-FINGERPRINT passes.
- If the owner decides the default is not part of the fingerprint, record that decision and correct W08.2's acceptance text instead.

## Out of scope
Making the default configurable.

title: BUG: forward-only protects only status: lowering a check's min_cases (live) or moving it out of T0 (latent) silently weakens or skips it
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W05.4 and kdo9 (497e738), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Verified at HEAD d1db21e.

The forward-only rule compares only `status` and row presence. At `xtask/src/staging.rs:146-166`, `demotions()` flags a row only when it is removed, or when an `implemented` row's status changes. Two other ways to weaken or skip a check pass it.

1. **Lowering `min_cases`. Live today.**
   - The commit lowers `min_cases` in both `check.rs` CATALOGUE and `checks.toml`, so REGISTRY-FILES' mirror test still passes. It also deletes the family's tests down to the new count.
   - Condition 4 checks only `min_cases ≤ matched #[test] fns`, an upper bound.
   - The gate then judges the family against the lowered count (`judge_cargo` uses the row's `min_cases`).
   - §10.13 says "a broad family is never reported passed while any of its registered cases is missing". `min_cases` is the registered count, and nothing protects it.
   - Narrowing a check's `filters` in `check.rs` together with `min_cases` works the same way.
2. **Moving a row out of T0. Latent.**
   - `stage()` runs only `tier == "T0"` rows, and `demotions()` ignores tier. An implemented row moved to T1 silently leaves every commit gate; staging reports 0 rows, not a problem.
   - Today REGISTRY-FILES blocks this, because `check::Tier` has only T0 and the mirror test requires the row tier to equal the catalogue's. It goes live as soon as W46 adds T1–T3 to the catalogue.
   - §10.6 calls this "silent reclassification", which "fails the gate".

**Evidence.** A scratch probe in a private copy of d1db21e, never committed: `staging::tests::review_probe_forward_only_ignores_min_cases_and_tier`.
```
REVIEW lowered=(1, []) retiered=(1, [])           # demotions(): parent A-TESTS T0 min 19 -> tree min 1, or -> T1: none
REVIEW retiered T0 staging: run=0 rows=0 problems=[]
```
- `stage(lowered, "T0")` runs A-TESTS with `min_cases` 1.
- `judge_cargo("alpha", ["a::"], 1, <one passing case>)` returns `Ok(1)`, so one surviving case of a 19-case family passes.

## Requirements
- §10.6: removal, skipping or silent reclassification fails the gate.
- §10.13 forward-only, and "a broad family is never reported passed while any of its registered cases is missing".
- D-56.
- §11.5 rules 3 and 12.

## Area
xtask (`staging.rs` `demotions` and `approve`; `gate.rs` `forward_step`), with GATE-STAGING fixtures.

## Acceptance
- Forward-only also fails:
  - a decrease of an `implemented` row's `min_cases`;
  - a tier change of an `implemented` row away from the tier that ran it, T0 today.
- Each of these, like a status demotion, passes only with `--allow-demotion <ID>=<closed plan-change bead>`, and the receipt records it, for example with a `from`/`to` pair that names the field.
- Increases of `min_cases`, and promotions, stay free.
- Fixtures cover the lowered `min_cases` case and the moved-tier case, refused and then approved.

## Out of scope
Detecting gutted test bodies, which is the general P9 problem (bug-variant self-test, W45). Filters live in `check.rs`, not `checks.toml`; a filter-only narrowing is already bounded by `min_cases` through condition 4.

title: BUG: RaftNode::status() panics (RA-VIEW-SEALED) while a frame without entries is syncing, reachable through ReadyLoop::node(); unsynced state readable and SyncDone routing undocumented
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.2, the Ready loop (VioletOwl; br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa, 7eb3316), for cc_1 on 2026-10-04. The review was at HEAD 7ec6be4, by SunnyDog plus two independent fresh reviewers (Opus and Fable). All three raised this, and SunnyDog verified it by hand against the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0. Thread: br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa.

**The fault.**
- `ReadyLoop::node()` (ready_loop.rs:165) hands out `&RaftNode`, and `Consensus::status(&self)` is public.
- `RaftNode::status()` (node.rs:459) computes `last` with `raw.raft.raft_log.last_index()`.
- When the unstable log is empty, that falls through (raft_log.rs:159-164) to `JournalStorage::last_index`, which asserts the seal is off (storage.rs:198-200, `RA-VIEW-SEALED`).

**Scenario.**
1. A follower steps `MsgRequestVote` and grants it.
2. The Ready has hard state {term, vote} and no entries, so `persist()` seals the view while the unstable log is empty.
3. Before `SyncDone`, the controller (W14), an observer or a `/v1/cluster` lookup calls `lp.node().status()`.
4. The invariant fires and the node is dead.

A Ready with entries does not panic, because `last_index` is then answered from the unstable log, so the happy-path tests never see it. The loop protects itself by caching its status before `persist` (ready_loop.rs:302-303). The public path is unguarded and undocumented.

**The same surface: P3s that both reviewers raised.**
- **Unsynced state is readable during a sync.**
  - `RaftNode::log()` (node.rs:134) and `ReadyLoop::status()` already include the unsynced frame: its term, vote, role and `last`.
  - `LogicalLog::hard_state` is documented as "the latest persisted hard state" (journal/src/log.rs:661-666), and `RaftNode::log`'s doc says the same.
  - That is fine for redirects, but wrong for anything that treats it as durable: K-11 observations, health, or the doctor.
- **`sync_done` routing is an unwritten contract.**
  - `sync_done` fires `RA-SYNC-UNEXPECTED` for any same-incarnation completion the loop did not issue (ready_loop.rs:263-271).
  - `Effect::SyncDir` shares the `SyncSeq` numbering.
  - W14 must route only the loop's own `Sync` completions to `sync_done`, and nothing says so.

## Requirements
- §7.4 step 3: reads are served from the published view during a sync.
- §7.4 step 4.
- CD-6/CD-7: a routine state never panics.
- CD-11: the docs state the invariants.

## Area
raft_adapter (`node.rs`, `ready_loop.rs`). If the wording changes, also the doc of `hard_state` in journal's `log.rs`.

## Acceptance
- `status()` cannot panic while any sync is outstanding. Any of these would do:
  - take `last` from the logical log;
  - cache it at `persist()`;
  - stop exposing `Consensus` through `ReadyLoop::node()`.
- A test: a follower grants a vote (a frame with hard state only). While the sync is outstanding, every public read on the loop and on the node returns without panicking.
- The docs of `RaftNode::log()`, `ReadyLoop::status()` and `LogicalLog::hard_state` say what is unsynced during a sync.
- `ReadyLoop`'s docs say that only the loop's own `Sync` completions go to `sync_done`.
- RAFT-ADAPTER and RAFT-READY-LOOP pass, and T0 is green.

## Out of scope
The persist-then-release protocol itself. All three reviews verified it sound.

title: BUG: a commit that deletes registry/checks.toml drops gate fast back to the bootstrap set, skipping forward-only and every check's min_cases
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W05.4 and kdo9 (497e738, closed as f5bbf45 and a4dfdf2), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Verified at HEAD d1db21e.

`./dev gate fast` chooses its set from the **tree under test**. At `xtask/src/gate.rs:517`, `run_fast` runs the registry set only if `ctx.root.join(registry/checks.toml).is_file()`. Otherwise it runs W01's bootstrap set, which has no staging step, no forward-only step and no per-check `min_cases`. In that branch the parent registry that `./dev commit` passes (`--parent-checks`) is ignored.

**Scenario.** One commit deletes `registry/checks.toml` and the handful of xtask tests that read it:
- `registry::files::checks_toml_mirrors_the_bootstrap_catalogue` (registry.rs:660);
- `registry_gate::tests::the_real_registry_passes_the_gate` (registry_gate.rs:1561);
- the traceability and DEV-SCHEMAS real-registry tests.

The candidate gate falls back to the bootstrap set:
- forward-only never runs, so every check row disappears without a demotion;
- no check's `min_cases` is enforced, so any family's tests can be deleted too;
- registry staging is gone for every later commit.

This is kdo9's scenario (delete a check with its row, marker and tests) at registry scale. kdo9's fix doesn't apply because the fix itself is switched off by the tree under test. §10.10 makes the switch one-way: "registry-driven staging takes over when W05 lands".

**Evidence.** A scratch probe in a private copy of d1db21e, never committed: `gate::tests::review_probe_a_tree_without_checks_toml_skips_forward_only`. It builds the gate-ok fixture with no `registry/checks.toml` and sets `ctx.parent = Parent::Checks(<two implemented rows>)`, as `./dev commit` would. Then it calls `run_fast`. Observed:
```
REVIEW set=bootstrap ok=false steps=["fmt", "clippy", "LINT-ALLOWS", "LINT-TIERS", "DEP-RULE", "DEP-LEDGER", "tests", "ubs"]
```
There is no `staging` or `forward-only` step, although the parent had a registry. `ok=false` comes only from the fixture's missing DEPENDENCIES.md and similar files, and isn't relevant.

## Requirements
- §10.10 "Staged contents": registry staging takes over when W05 lands.
- §10.13 and D-56: forward-only statuses.
- §10.6: protected manifests; removal fails the gate.
- §11.5 rules 3 and 12.

## Area
xtask (`gate.rs` `run_fast`), with a GATE-STAGING fixture.

## Acceptance
- When the parent commit has a registry (`Parent::Checks`), or in candidate mode with the parent unknown, `./dev gate fast` runs the registry set even if the tree lacks `registry/checks.toml`. A missing tree registry then fails staging, and forward-only reports every parent row as removed.
- The bootstrap set runs only when the parent also has no registry (`Parent::Absent`), matching §10.10's one-way switch.
- A fixture fails a candidate that deletes `checks.toml` against a parent that has one.

## Out of scope
T1–T3 staging (W46).

title: BUG: gate and tests can run another checkout's build through the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR
description:
Context: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target comes from the tmux global environment (ACFS), so every keyval checkout on this box shares one target dir, including nested ones (`<target>/keyval-probes`, `keyval-probes-manual`, `keyval-scratch`). Cargo hashes path packages relative to the workspace root and judges freshness by mtime, and `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (xtask/src/test_support.rs:10 `workspace_root`) is not part of the fingerprint. So a checkout whose sources are older than another checkout's last build reuses that build, with the other checkout's path baked in.

Observed 2026-10-03: main@459f437 `./dev gate fast` (receipt artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261003T141320Z-283675ab760c-1437177.json) ran the xtask test binary built 13:44 by the audit clone /data/projects/keyval-audit, so LINT-PROBES ran clippy against the audit clone's tree (an uncommitted-to-main `Instant::now` probe) and reported 19 false failures; "tests" counted 115 instead of 147. With a private target dir, and again after `cargo clean -p {types,xtask,lint-probe-production,lint-probe-deterministic}` in the shared dirs, the same tree passes 147 tests. The reverse direction is worse: a checkout can falsely PASS by running another tree's clean build. Gate receipts name a tree ID that the tests may not have run against (P11).

Risk to check: W07's `.local/candidate/` and `.local/accept/<tree-id>/` are further checkouts at different paths sharing the same target dir.

Requirements: P11 (exact-tree evidence), §11.10, §10.10, W01/W07 acceptance.
Area: xtask (./dev launcher, test_support.rs, gate/commit/accept target-dir handling).

Acceptance:
- Fixture: two checkouts of the same commit at different paths with one shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR; build a modified tree in checkout B, then `./dev gate fast` in checkout A tests A's sources (no diagnostics or results from B), and vice versa.
- `./dev` gate/commit/accept either use a per-checkout target dir (e.g. derived from the checkout's realpath) or prove the binaries under test were built from the receipt's tree; the receipt records the target dir used.
- No test locates the workspace via a compile-time path that can outlive its checkout.

Out of scope: changing the machine-wide CARGO_TARGET_DIR (ACFS-managed).
close_reason: Fixed in 665e60c (tree 06abad96); committed-tree gate receipt gate-fast-20261003T153116Z-06abad967f61-1673248 passed (158 tests, ubs clean, ast-grep rules_ran=true); details in comment

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote): one target directory per checkout.

- `./dev` launcher: the shared base (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, else <root>/target) goes into KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE. CARGO_TARGET_DIR becomes `<base>/keyval-checkout-<first 16 hex of sha256(realpath of root)>`. Nested launchers derive from KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE, so nothing compounds. Every cargo run below ./dev inherits it, including the build of xtask itself, which was also exposed: a checkout could run another checkout's gate binary.
- xtask/src/cargo.rs: `target_base` and `checkout_target_dir` compute the same name in Rust. A unit test runs the real launcher with a fake cargo and checks that the two agree, that two checkouts sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR get different dirs, that nested runs don't compound, and that a symlinked spelling maps to the same dir.
- W07 `.local/candidate/` (xtask/src/commit.rs `gate_command`): the candidate's gate now always builds into `checkout_target_dir(base, candidate)`. Before, it used `.local/candidate-target` only when CARGO_TARGET_DIR was unset. Under ACFS it is always set, so the candidate shared /data/tmp/cargo-target with every checkout. Unit test: `commit::tests::the_candidate_gate_builds_into_the_candidates_own_target_dir`.
- `.local/accept/<tree-id>/`: `./dev accept` does not exist yet (later W07 subtask). When it lands it must run cargo with `cargo::checkout_target_dir(&cargo::target_base(root), accept_dir)`, as commit.rs does. Note that every new accept path then costs a cold build and about 470 MB of target dir, so W46's prune of accept trees should prune their target dirs too.
- Receipts record `tools.cargo_target_dir`. Schemas bumped: keyval.dev.receipt/v2, keyval.dev.gate/v2 (rule 14). The receipt test asserts the field.
- No test locates the workspace through a compile-time path any more. Every `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` in xtask (test_support, gate, lint, check, workspace, metadata, tests/check.rs, tests/doctor.rs) now reads the runtime CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR that `cargo test` sets. (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask")` remains. It names the binary inside this checkout's own target dir, not the workspace.)

Acceptance fixture (manual, too heavy for T0; my scratchpad dtqu-fixture/):
- Two checkouts of tree 4cbc306e20e1 (= 459f437 + beads 1–2 paths) at different paths, one shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR. B adds a test `clock::only_in_checkout_b` that fails (tree 8d64c76306e0). B's files are newer than A's.
- Bug reproduced with the old launcher's behaviour (`cargo run` with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=shared): after B's gate, A's gate FAILED with "1 test(s) failed: clock::only_in_checkout_b::only_in_checkout_b", a test A does not contain. A had run B's build.
- With the fixed `./dev`, same shared base: B first, failed with its own test (target keyval-checkout-c0aadf6b9839f569). Then A passed, 153 tests, zero mentions of only_in_checkout_b in tests.log (target keyval-checkout-3ab90700d0a40cf8). Then B again: B's own result again (failed, only_in_checkout_b), so A's build never leaks into B.
- The A run is also a full gate for tree 4cbc306e: fmt, clippy, LINT-ALLOWS, LINT-TIERS, DEP-RULE, DEP-LEDGER, 153 tests, UBS on all 27 sources: passed.

Operational notes: the first `./dev` run in each checkout is a cold build (about 1 min, about 470 MB). The coordinator's pre-W07 flow, `.local/bootstrap-candidates/<tree>`, now costs that per commit (30 such dirs exist). It should materialise into one fixed directory instead.

title: BUG: gate counts a UBS run whose ast-grep rules never ran as passed
description:
Context: from at least 2026-09-30 02:04 until 2026-10-03 ~14:10, `ast-grep` on PATH was ~/.local/bin/ast-grep, a misnamed copy of ast-grep's `sg` deprecation shim that spawns `ast-grep` from PATH, i.e. itself, until fork fails with EAGAIN at the cgroup pids cap. Every cold UBS scan therefore ran none of its ast-grep rules, yet UBS exited 0 with `status: ok` and `failed_modules: []`, and the gate recorded "ubs passed". The same loop exhausted the M0 auditor agent's pids cap (TasksMax=3644) and it aborted (SIGABRT) mid-audit at 13:46:36. The shim was moved aside on 2026-10-03 (~/.local/bin/ast-grep.sg-shim.bak) and the UBS cache from that period moved to ~/.cache/ubs-pre-shim-fix-20261003; the environment is fixed, but the gate still cannot tell a partial UBS scan from a clean one.

Consequence: every UBS "passed" receipt before 2026-10-03 14:13 (including W01's final acceptance and W07.1) is a partial scan. The first full scan is artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261003T142021Z-283675ab760c-1445981.json (UBS red; see the UBS-vs-CD-8 conflict bug).

Requirements: §10.10 (UBS in the gate fast set), O-8, W01 acceptance (doctor capability probes).
Area: xtask (gate.rs UBS step, doctor.rs ubs/ast-grep probes).

Acceptance:
- Fixture: with a failing `ast-grep` first on PATH (exits non-zero, or a self-spawning stub under a small pids cap), `./dev gate fast` fails the UBS step instead of passing.
- `./dev doctor` runs a bounded real ast-grep query (not just `--version`) and fails on such a stub.
- The gate receipt records which ast-grep binary/version UBS used and that its rules ran.

Out of scope: fixing UBS's exit status upstream; the shim installer (report separately to UBS/ACFS).
close_reason: Fixed in 665e60c (tree 06abad96); committed-tree gate receipt gate-fast-20261003T153116Z-06abad967f61-1673248 passed (158 tests, ubs clean, ast-grep rules_ran=true); details in comment

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote).

Root cause, measured with UBS 5.4.17 using `--no-cache`, on a file holding one production panic!:
- With ast-grep absent from PATH: status ok, exit 0, 0 criticals. The Rust module checks only `command -v ast-grep` and silently skips every ast-grep rule.
- With a stub that exits 1, or one that exits 0 and prints nothing, first on PATH: also status ok, exit 0, 0 criticals.
- UBS's scan cache is keyed by file content, not by the ast-grep that produced an entry. A hit can therefore replay a hollow scan, and with a warm cache the broken stubs still "found" the panic.

Fix (xtask/src/gate.rs `ubs_step`):
1. Canary. Every UBS step first scans a canary file (`UBS_CANARY`: one production panic!, which only the ast-grep rule pack detects). It requires exactly 1 critical and exit 1 (`canary_verdict`). Otherwise the step fails with "UBS did not report the canary's panic!, so its ast-grep rules did not run", and stops before passes 1–2, whose results would be meaningless.
2. Every gate UBS run uses `--no-cache` (measured cost: 12.3 s vs 12.0 s on 27 files).
3. Each pass must report every given file as scanned (added with br-gate-ubs-test-panics-brzy).
4. Receipt `tools.ast_grep = {path, version, rules_ran}`: the ast-grep on UBS's PATH, its `--version` line (or why it failed), and whether the canary proved its rules ran. Covered by the receipt/v2 bump from br-gate-shared-target-dir-dtqu.
5. `./dev doctor` lists ast-grep as required. Its capability probe is a real, bounded query (`ast-grep run --lang rust --pattern 'mod $NAME;' --json=compact xtask/src/main.rs`, under doctor's 30 s limit) that must return a JSON array with ≥1 real match.

Tests (all run in T0):
- `gate::tests::ubs_fails_when_its_ast_grep_rules_do_not_run`: the real UBS, with a failing ast-grep stub and then a silent one first on PATH. The step fails on the canary, and the receipt names the stub, its version outcome and rules_ran=false.
- `gate::tests::canary_verdicts`.
- `gate::tests::ubs_lets_tests_panic_but_never_production_code` now also asserts rules_ran=true with the real ast-grep.
- `doctor::tests::the_ast_grep_query_must_return_real_matches` (failing, silent, deprecation text, `[]`, lookalike JSON).
- `doctor::tests::the_installed_ast_grep_answers_the_real_query`.
- `tests/doctor.rs::an_ast_grep_that_matches_nothing_fails_doctor`: a fake whose --version works but whose query prints nothing.

Self-spawning stub (the real incident shim, a copy of ~/.local/bin/ast-grep.sg-shim.bak named ast-grep, first on PATH). Run by hand, only under `systemd-run --user --scope -p TasksMax=40`, never in the test suite:
- `xtask --json doctor`: ast-grep status "broken" (`ast-grep --version` exited 1).
- `xtask gate fast` on the gate-ubs fixture: the ubs step FAILED with "canary: UBS did not report the canary's panic!, so its ast-grep rules did not run …". The receipt has tools.ast_grep = {path: <stub>, version: "`ast-grep --version` exited with exit status: 1", rules_ran: false}.

Evidence for the combined tree 06abad967f61 (459f437 + all three beads' paths), frozen, git-isolated candidate:
- `./dev gate fast --changed …`: passed (158 tests, ubs 14 files).
- Full UBS scan: passed. Canary 1 critical (expected), pass 1 0 critical / 27 files, pass 2 0 critical / 23 production views. Receipt: ast_grep /home/charlie/.cargo/bin/ast-grep 0.45.3, rules_ran true.
- This gate also caught a real issue in my first draft: rust.security.command-executable on `Command::new(<looked-up path>)`, fixed to a fixed program name resolved on the child's PATH.

Not done (out of scope): UBS upstream (its Rust module should mark a scan partial when ast-grep is missing or fails, and its cache key should include the ast-grep identity), and the shim installer.

title: BUG: ./dev gate fast is red on main: UBS panic-macro rule flags test-only panic! that CD-8 allows
description:
Context: `./dev gate fast` is red on a clean main@459f437 (receipt artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261003T142021Z-283675ab760c-1445981.json): the UBS step fails with 7 critical findings, all from UBS rule `rust.ownership.panic-macro` on `panic!` in test code. This is the first gate run in which UBS's ast-grep rules actually executed (see the companion UBS partial-scan bug), so every gate that changes xtask/tests will now be red.

Conflict (both locations, per AGENTS.md "never quietly pick the convenient side"):
- Policy: clippy.toml `CD-8: tests may use unwrap/expect/panic` (allow-panic-in-tests = true); AGENTS.md:184-186 and AGENTS.md:307 ("Tests may use `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`").
- Gate: xtask/src/gate.rs `ubs_step`/`ubs_verdict` (UBS step of the §10.10 bootstrap set) fails on any UBS critical, and UBS does not exempt test code.
Flagged locations: xtask/src/gate.rs:962 (inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests), xtask/tests/cli.rs:12, xtask/tests/cli.rs:64, xtask/tests/doctor.rs:175, xtask/tests/doctor.rs:183.

Requirements: CD-8, §10.10 (gate fast bootstrap set incl. UBS), W01 acceptance.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-10-03: CD-8 wins (tests may use unwrap/expect/panic!). Resolve on the gate side: make the UBS step stop failing on panic! in test code (tests/ and #[cfg(test)]) while panic! in first-party production code still fails the gate. Do not change clippy.toml or AGENTS.md policy.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote, per the owner's CD-8 decision above; policy files untouched):

The gate's UBS step now runs two passes (xtask/src/gate.rs `ubs_step`):
1. The exact changed files, every UBS rule except category `rust.ownership` (`--skip=rust.ownership`).
2. A production view of the same Rust files, every rule. In this view, test code is blanked to spaces, with line numbers kept (`lint::production_view`). Test code is what clippy's allow-panic-in-tests means: `#[test]` and `#[cfg(test)]` items, and `#![cfg(test)]` scopes, which every tests/*.rs file starts with. The views are kept next to the receipt under `gate-<run>/ubs-production/`.

Why: UBS 5.4.17's Rust module drops its per-finding records from every machine format (JSON, JSONL and SARIF carry only counts). So the gate cannot tell which rule or location a critical came from. `rust.ownership`'s only critical rule is `rust.ownership.panic-macro`. Its other rules (unwrap/expect, todo!, unimplemented!, unreachable!, dbg!, println!) are warnings or infos, which never fail the gate. Net effect: only `panic!` inside test code stops failing the gate, and production code still faces every rule. Rejected: `ubs:ignore[rust.ownership.panic-macro]` markers on test lines, because UBS's statement-interval semantics let a marker on the line above a statement suppress it, so a production panic! right after a test item could be hidden. Also rejected: the Rust module's own `--exclude-tests`, which the meta-runner does not forward, and which drops every rule in test code, using a boundary heuristic UBS itself calls permissive.

Each pass is judged by its `--report-json` (status, failed_modules, criticals, exit code). It must also report every given file as scanned, otherwise it is a partial scan and fails. The text report goes to ubs.log, so the log shows the panic rule ran ("No panic! macros" in pass 2) and where any finding is.

Evidence (pre-commit, my frozen git-isolated candidate = 459f437 + the paths below, tree c44e7f3e85772133d4ac177da18109e528b890cc, private CARGO_TARGET_DIR):
- `./dev gate fast --changed <paths>`: passed, 150 tests, ubs 2 files.
- `./dev gate fast` with no --changed (UBS on all 27 first-party sources, as on the red main receipt): passed. Pass 1: 0 critical / 27 files. Pass 2: 0 critical / 23 production views.
- Probe `gate::tests::ubs_lets_tests_panic_but_never_production_code` uses the real UBS on fixture xtask/tests/fixtures/gate-ubs. The step fails with exactly "pass 2 (production code): UBS found 1 critical issue(s)" at src/halve.rs:7:9 [rule:rust.ownership.panic-macro]. The test panics at src/lib.rs:18 (#[cfg(test)]) and tests/doubling.rs:6 (#![cfg(test)]) are not flagged.
The official receipt will come from the coordinator's commit run.

title: W02.1x: RAFT-VENDOR check, ./dev doctor probe and build_id input for the vendored Raft library
description:
## Context
W02.1 vendored raft and raft-proto 0.7.0 under vendor/raft/ and pinned code generation by vendoring raft-proto's generated eraftpb code: build = false, so no protoc runs at build time. Provenance and every file's sha256 are in vendor/raft/VENDOR.toml. The xtask half of W02.1 is split out here, because xtask/** was reserved for W07 when W02.1 ran: the executable check, the ./dev doctor probe, and the explicit build_id input. W02.1 closes with accept:RAFT-VENDOR once this lands.

## Requirements
P4, T-3 ("same build" covers generated-code provenance, pinned protoc), T-11; PLAN §7.3, §12.2 W02.

## Area
xtask: a new leaf module plus a catalogue row in check.rs, doctor.rs and gate.rs build inputs. These are xtask facades, so they need a short reservation.

## Design
1. Static check RAFT-VENDOR (catalogue row; marker; covers P4, T-3; class invariant; tier T0; min_cases = the files listed in VENDOR.toml, 73 today). It fails when:
   - VENDOR.toml is missing, or its schema is not keyval.vendor.raft/v1;
   - any vendored file is missing, unlisted, or has a sha256 different from [crate.files];
   - a [codegen].outputs entry is not a listed file;
   - raft-proto/Cargo.toml has build != false, any build-dependencies, or a prost/protobuf-build dependency or feature;
   - raft does not resolve raft-proto via path = "../raft-proto";
   - raft-proto's protobuf requirement is not "=<[codegen].protobuf_runtime>";
   - the root Cargo.lock contains protobuf-build or protobuf-codegen, or contains protobuf at a version other than the runtime.
   Negative fixtures for each of these. A reference implementation of the same assertions, used as W02.1's evidence, is described in the bead thread.
2. ./dev doctor probe 'raft-codegen-pin': runs the RAFT-VENDOR assertions (cheap, file hashing only) and reports the pinned protoc (libprotoc 3.9.0, sha256 from VENDOR.toml). It fails if vendor/raft exists and the check fails; once W02.1 has landed it also fails if vendor/raft is missing.
3. build_id: add raft_vendor_sha256 (sha256 of vendor/raft/VENDOR.toml) to BuildInputs and the build_id preimage, beside raft_patch_sha256. The receipt then shows codegen provenance explicitly; bump the receipt schema version (O-6).

## Acceptance
./dev check RAFT-VENDOR passes on the committed tree and executes >= min_cases; every negative fixture fails as specified; ./dev check DEV-DOCTOR covers the new probe (pass and fail); DEV-GATE covers the new build input; then add the accept:RAFT-VENDOR label to br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi.

## Out of scope
Changing vendored files; the entropy patch (W02.3); any workspace consumer of raft (W02.4 / W13).

title: sim net: loss, duplication and delay profiles cannot change after construction, so faults cannot be scheduled or healed mid-run
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fresh-eyes review of W16.1, the simulated network (5cc5ada, br-w16-1-network-model-40l), 2026-10-04, at HEAD 57cb984, for cc_1. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen copy; every claim was verified by hand at HEAD, where crates/sim is unchanged. Opus raised it as P2.

**Loss, duplication and delay profiles can't change after the network is built, so faults can't be scheduled or healed mid-run.**

**Evidence:**
- `Network.config` is private, with no setter; only `links_mut` exists (net.rs:317-333, 367-370).
- Replacing the `Network` mid-run would orphan the in-flight copies and their queue slots, since the rng and copies live inside it.

**Failure:**
- A seed that enables loss has it from t=0, so the baseline isn't fault-free (§10.2; §10.16 "successful writes before the first fault").
- Heal can't stop injecting faults, and chaos delays above 50 ms break §9.4's "delivers within 50 ms" for the healthy phase.
- W37 (area sim/nemesis) can't schedule these faults without editing sim/net.

## Requirements
§10.2, §10.4, §10.16, §9.4.

## Area
crates/sim (net.rs, tests).

## Acceptance
- `set_profiles(peer, client)`, or a profiles accessor, applies to later sends deterministically.
- A test shows a change mid-run takes effect at the next send, and copies already in flight keep their arrival times.

## Out of scope
The nemesis schedule itself (W37).

title: OWNER: record the semantic-config encoding v2 (SCAN default page size) in PLAN.md §16
description:
## Context
br-fingerprint-misses-scan-default-3pu0 (commit 6954eda) changed the semantic-config fingerprint's canonical encoding: it gained `scan_page_default_items=32` (F-4's default page size, which changes a SCAN's result), so the encoding name became `keyval semantic config v2`. The pinned `config/local.toml` fingerprint moved from 3b2e3ed3… to 48205fd1…, re-derived independently. PLAN.md §5 ("A format change is deliberate: bump the format version, …, record it in §16") and the fingerprint module's documentation require the change to be recorded in §16. §16 rows are owner decisions, so on cc_1's overnight decision (the recommended option, logged for the owner) the code landed without a PLAN.md edit, and this bead carries the row for the owner.

## Proposed §16.1 row (text ready to paste; the D-number is the next free one)
| D-81 | **The semantic-config fingerprint's canonical encoding is versioned (`keyval semantic config vN`) and covers every fixed constant that can change a result, including the SCAN default page size; v1 → v2 adds `scan_page_default_items`** (v1.10.1, 2026-10-04) | Decided | br-fingerprint-misses-scan-default-3pu0: a build with another `PageSize::DEFAULT` would have matched the old fingerprint and interoperated (genesis §7.7 step 2, peer envelope §8.2), while a SCAN without `limit` returned a different number of items depending on the serving node. §7.10 makes the fingerprint cover every parameter that can change a result, §7.11 makes the SCAN caps part of it, and W08.2's acceptance names the default. A changed canonical text changes every fingerprint, so the encoding version is bumped (DUR-8). |

## Requirements
§16 (decision log), §5 golden-file/format rule, DUR-8, F-4, §7.10.

## Area
PLAN.md §16 (owner).

## Acceptance
The owner adds the row (or records a different decision); PLAN.md's patch version is bumped; this bead closes with a note naming the PLAN.md commit.

## Out of scope
Any further encoding change.

title: raft_adapter: OutboundMessage doc says 'encoded envelope' but holds bare protobuf; the peer path decodes and admits twice
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9. Both reviewers raised it as P3, so it is filed.

**The port's documentation contradicts the codec, and the peer path decodes twice.**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/types/src/consensus.rs:75-81` documents `OutboundMessage.bytes` as "the encoded envelope (§8.2)". But `convert::outbound` fills it with the bare Raft protobuf, and `PeerCodec::seal` wraps it.
  - This is a wiring trap for W16 and W21: unsealed sends would all drop as `Malformed`.
- `open` decodes and admits the message, then returns raw bytes. `RaftNode::step` (node.rs:320-324) decodes and admits again, and maps every `Inadmissible` to `StepError::Rejected`, losing the reason.
- CD-3 says to convert once at the boundary. Defence in depth is defensible, but it isn't documented as a decision.

## Requirements
CD-2, CD-3, CD-11 (docs state the contract); §8.2; D-71.

## Area
crates/types (consensus.rs doc), crates/raft_adapter (envelope.rs, node.rs). This is a shared surface for the types crate.

## Acceptance
- The `OutboundMessage` doc says "the Raft message's protobuf bytes; `PeerCodec::seal` wraps them for the wire".
- Either `open` returns an opaque, already-admitted payload type that `RaftInput::Peer` requires, so stepping unopened bytes can't be written (CD-2), or the double decode is documented as a deliberate decision.
- The reason is kept in `StepError` (or `Debug`) for diagnosability.

## Out of scope
The transport's sender authentication (a W21 note).

title: BUG: registry item closure and activation trust unverified inputs (any plan:W-labelled bead closes an item; empty bead skips condition 8; reopen forces a hand edit)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03). **Both independent reviewers raised item 1.** The Opus reviewer added items 2–4. All verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e.

The registry's derivation of "work item closed" and of requirement activation trusts inputs it doesn't verify.

**1. Any bead labelled `plan:W<nn>` closes the item.**
- `xtask/src/registry.rs:152-170` (`closed_items`) and `xtask/src/closure.rs:380-387` (`is_closed`) count an item as closed when `bead.id == item.bead || bead has label plan:<id>`, with `status == "closed"`.
- The gate never checks that the label is unique, or that the recorded bead carries it. Only `./dev beads import` checks that (`beads.rs:166`).
- Scenario: a discovered-work bead mislabelled `plan:W28` closes while `br-w28-…` stays open.
  - W28 counts as closed, so DM-4 (listed by W04 and W28) derives `active`.
  - The next canonical closure's catch-up (`registry.rs:114-130`) flips it.
  - Traceability then reports a MUST requirement passed while its work is open.
- Every item now records its `bead`, so the label fallback adds only risk.

**2. Condition 8 silently skips an item whose `bead` is empty** (`registry_gate.rs:796-799`). Setting `bead = ""`, or pointing `bead` at a subtask, removes the item from the tracker comparison.

**3. The activation hook only promotes, but condition 1 demands an exact match.**
- `registry.rs:114-130` ("never demoted here") against `registry_gate.rs:453-463`.
- Scenario: a closed W bead is reopened. Its requirements now derive `planned` but are still declared `active`, so every T0 run fails. The only fix is a hand edit, which §11.5 rule 12 forbids.

**4. Low confidence: malformed §6 rows are dropped silently.** `registry.rs:133-147` keeps only rows whose level cell is exactly `MUST`/`SHOULD`/`MAY`. A plan change that adds a row with a decorated level cell (for example bold) is skipped by the parse, so the requirement is never tracked. An existing row reformatted the same way does surface as a mismatch.

Malformed tracker-export lines are dropped too (`registry.rs:155`). That direction is conservative: fewer items count as closed.

## Requirements
- §10.13: a requirement is active "when all work items listing it … have closed"; condition 8 compares the work graph with the imported beads' dependencies.
- §11.4 and AGENTS.md: `plan:W<nn>` goes "on the one bead per §12.2 item".
- §11.5 rule 12.

## Area
xtask (`registry.rs`, `registry_gate.rs`, `closure.rs`), with fixtures.

## Acceptance
- An item is closed only by its recorded `bead`, and the gate fails when that bead lacks `plan:<id>` or the label appears on more than one bead.
- An empty `bead` fails condition 8.
- A reopened item's requirements are demoted by the recomputation, or the case is reported with a defined owner path rather than forcing a hand edit.
- A §6 table row whose ID matches the requirement-ID pattern but whose level doesn't parse fails condition 1.
- Fixtures for each.

## Out of scope
Changing how `./dev beads import` assigns labels.

comments.author: JadeOx
comments.text:
Design decisions (JadeOx, 2026-10-04 ~00:55Z, for the morning review):
(1) Item 3: GoldenHorizon (thread xtask-shared-facades, msg 337) reads §10.13 as defining activation as 'all listing items closed'. Only check status is forward-only (D-56), not requirement status. So a reopened item derives planned again, and the recomputation demotes.
(2) Item 3 mechanism: cc_1's overnight dialog, logged for the owner, chose the (Recommended) option: every ./dev commit --close (subtask or canonical, and --failed) recomputes ALL statuses both ways from the tracker export it commits. Reason: every candidate gate runs the_real_registry_passes_the_gate (condition 1 exact match), and every closure commits the whole export, so the closure that carries a reopen must also carry the demotion or it fails its own gate.
This changes W05.3's 'a subtask's closure catches nothing up' assertion: a subtask still never activates anything by its own closure; it only syncs statuses to the export it commits. The close JSON gains 'demoted', so keyval.dev.close/v1 becomes v2. Removing the v1 files needs a separate file-deletion OK.
(3) Items 1 and 2: closure is by the recorded bead only, in registry::closed_items, closure.rs is_closed and item_for_bead (the label fallback goes). Condition 8 fails on an empty bead, a recorded bead without plan:<id>, or plan:<id> on another bead. A real-export audit at 5f137aa found all 53 items clean: every bead recorded, labelled, and unique.
(4) Item 4: plan_requirements keeps every §6 row whose ID cell is a requirement ID, and condition 1 fails a level cell that isn't MUST/SHOULD/MAY.

title: BUG: a cargo-test check is judged passed on a truncated package run (aborted test binary); the receipt reports a family passed with cases missing
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W05.4 (497e738), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Verified at HEAD d1db21e.

`staging::judge_cargo` (`xtask/src/staging.rs:282-340`) looks at the package run's `failure` only when the selection is empty. If at least `min_cases` selected cases printed `... ok`, the check passes, even when the package's test run ended abnormally and some of the check's cases never ran.

A test binary that aborts drops all its remaining cases from the output. Causes include `std::process::abort`, a stack overflow, SIGSEGV, or the OOM killer. `package_tests_step` (gate.rs:978) then records the failure as "cargo test exited unsuccessfully", with no failed count, and the cases that never ran are simply absent from `outcomes`.

There's also no reconciliation between the parsed result lines and libtest's own counts (`running N tests`, or `test result:`). A dropped or unparsed result line, or a name that appears in two targets of one package, changes the per-check count silently.

**Impact.**
- The gate's overall verdict is still `failed`, because the tests step fails, so no commit lands on such a run.
- But the receipt's per-check step says `passed`, with the partial count. Receipts are the evidence (rule 16), and `./dev report traceability` takes a gate step as a full-family run on its tree (`full: true`) whatever the receipt's overall result. A clean-checkout or later-tier gate on a committed tree can therefore yield "passed" evidence for a family whose cases never all ran.
- §10.13 says "a broad family is never reported passed while any of its registered cases is missing". The receipt claims what didn't happen.

**Evidence.** A scratch probe in a private copy of d1db21e, never committed: `gate::tests::review_probe_an_aborted_test_binary_still_passes_its_check`. In the gate-ok fixture crate, `tests::a_passes` passes and `tests::z_aborts_the_binary` sleeps 800 ms, then calls `std::process::abort()`. The row is `R-TESTS`, implemented, `min_cases` 1, with filters `tests::`. `registry_run` gives:
```
REVIEW2 step tests Failed cases=0 detail=Some("1 test run(s) failed:\n  gate-ok: cargo test exited unsuccessfully")
REVIEW2 step R-TESTS Passed cases=1 detail=None
```

## Requirements
- §10.10: the runner rejects incomplete selections.
- §10.11: every selected check executed at least its minimum and passed.
- §10.13: a broad family is never reported passed while any registered case is missing.
- P10; rule 16.

## Area
xtask (`staging.rs` `judge_cargo` and `PackageRun`; `gate.rs` `package_tests_step`; `libtest.rs`), with GATE-STAGING fixtures.

## Acceptance
- A cargo-test check fails, saying why, when its package's run did not complete: a non-zero exit not explained by failed cases, a tally that can't be parsed, or a binary with no `test result:` line. Failed cases outside the check's selection still don't fail it.
- The parsed per-case outcomes are reconciled with libtest's counts per binary: passed + failed + ignored must equal the result lines parsed. A mismatch fails the checks of that package.
- A fixture with an aborting test binary fails the check whose family it truncates, as well as the tests step.

## Out of scope
Timeouts for hung tests. That's a separate concern, since today the gate waits forever.

title: BUG: Key::parse/Value::parse ignore the configured max_key_bytes/max_value_bytes (DM-1/DM-2 fixed vs §7.10 configurable)
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W04/W15.1 code (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand).
`Key::parse` and `Value::parse` enforce only the fixed DM-1/DM-2 maxima, but W08.1's parser accepts smaller *configured* limits. Under such a config, an over-limit key or value parses, and by CD-3 nothing downstream re-checks it.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01):**
- `crates/types/src/data.rs:32` (`Key::MAX_BYTES = 256`) and `:39` (`Key::parse(raw)` takes no limit).
- `crates/types/src/data.rs:103` (`Value::MAX_BYTES = 65_536`) and `:113` (`Value::parse(raw)`).
- `crates/types/src/config/params.rs:251`: `max_key_bytes` is allowed from 1 to `Key::MAX_BYTES`, and `max_value_bytes` from 0 to `Value::MAX_BYTES`.
- `config/fixtures/small-limits.toml:16-17`: `max_key_bytes = 16`, `max_value_bytes = 64`. This is an *accepted* fixture.
- Scenario: under `small-limits.toml`, a 200-byte key or a 60 KiB value passes `Key::parse`/`Value::parse`. It is admitted and proposed, so the configured semantic limit is never enforced. A reference model that honours the config disagrees with the system.

## Conflict: two plan locations disagree
1. **The limits are fixed.** PLAN.md §6.2 DM-1 says "A key is a UTF-8 string of 1–256 bytes", and DM-2 says "A value is a UTF-8 string of 0–65,536 bytes". The §7.11 limits table gives "Key / value | 256 B / 64 KiB decoded UTF-8".
2. **The limits are configurable.** In PLAN.md §7.10:
   - the config example carries `max_key_bytes = 256` and `max_value_bytes = 65536` as required keys;
   - the semantic-config fingerprint covers "key/value limits";
   - the cross-limit rule "applies to small test limits", and a limit outside its allowed range is rejected.

   O-5 says no built-in default may silently override a configured semantic parameter.
- CD-3 ("The core never re-checks") means the domain parse must apply whichever limit is in force.

## Requirements
DM-1, DM-2, F-8, O-5, CD-3, §7.10, §7.11.

## Area
types (`data.rs`, possibly `config/params.rs`); the boundary callers (W18 HTTP, the peer and disk decoders) once they exist.

## Acceptance (once the owner decides)
- **Option A (configured limits apply):** `Key::parse`/`Value::parse` take the configured limit, or a `Limits` value from the `Config`. Under `small-limits.toml`, keys of 15, 16 and 17 bytes and values of 63, 64 and 65 bytes behave as configured, with multibyte straddling. The DM-1/DM-2 maxima remain the upper bound.
- **Option B (fixed limits):** PLAN §7.10 pins `max_key_bytes`/`max_value_bytes` to exactly 256/65536, or removes them from the config. W08's parser and fixtures follow.

Either way, a test proves that no accepted config lets a key or value past its effective limit.

## Out of scope
Changing DM-1/DM-2's absolute maxima.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
SunnyDog (author of W08.1's ConfigParam ranges): the finding is right. Under config/fixtures/small-limits.toml, a 200-byte key passes Key::parse.
Recommendation: Option B, worded as a range pin: keep max_key_bytes and max_value_bytes as required keys, but allow exactly 256 and exactly 65536.
- **The API contract stays fixed.** api/openapi.yaml says x-maxUtf8Bytes 256/65536 (§8, the source of truth after PLAN), and conformance is HTTP-only against that spec (§10.8). Under Option A, a small-limits config would answer 400/413 to keys and values the spec calls valid, a spec deviation by configuration.
- **Option A spreads config through every boundary parser:** HTTP (W18), the peer envelope and command codec (W09, W13) and journal decode (W11), plus the model and conformance. Option B changes one range table.
- **Small-limit capacity profiles keep working.** The 'small test limits' in §7.10's margin rule are history and live-state limits (DM-6, DM-7), which stay configurable.
- **The fingerprint and §7.10's key list are unaffected.** Both keys stay required and fingerprinted, now as fixed values. This needs no change to W08.2's encoding.
If the owner picks B, the W08 follow-up is small:
- ConfigParam::MaxKeyBytes range becomes 256..=256 and MaxValueBytes 65536..=65536;
- small-limits.toml moves to 256/65536;
- the range tests cover 255 and 257 refused;
- one PLAN §7.10 sentence: these two keys must equal the DM-1/DM-2 maxima.
I can take it straight after W08.2, which isn't blocked either way. -- SunnyDog

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: OWNER DECISION (owner, about 23:15Z 2026-10-03, relayed by cc_1): Option A. Configured limits apply: Key::parse and Value::parse take the configured limit, a limits value from the Config, and the DM-1/DM-2 maxima remain the upper bound. Under config/fixtures/small-limits.toml, keys of 15, 16 and 17 bytes and values of 63, 64 and 65 bytes behave as configured, multibyte straddling included. A test proves no accepted config lets a key or value past its effective limit. Option B (pinning the ranges) is rejected. My earlier recommendation of B is superseded. Claimed by SunnyDog; needs-owner removed. -- SunnyDog

title: raft_adapter tests: restart through journal::recover, a happy-path step, a firing test per RA-* invariant, persist's HardStop re-arm, the entry unknown-field branch
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.1 (raft_adapter, e1427a8, closed 3cbaf2d) that cc_1 asked for, 2026-10-04: SunnyDog plus an independent fresh reviewer, every finding verified by hand against the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0. Thread: br-w13-1-consensus-port-construction-3wc.

W13.1's claims outrun its tests. RAFT-ADAPTER has exactly its min_cases, 16 tests.
- **The restart never goes through recovery.** `a_restarted_node_keeps_its_term_and_refuses_an_applied_index_past_commit` (node_tests.rs:228-270) rebuilds from a clone of the live logical log, never from `journal::recover` over the journal bytes. So "initial_state maps the recovered hard state" (§7.7 step 6) is not exercised end to end.
- **No happy-path step.** Every `step()` call in the tests is a refusal. No test steps a valid peer message, for example a vote request or response between two nodes.
- **Invariants that never fire.** None of RA-PERSIST-WITHOUT-READY, RA-ADVANCE-WITHOUT-READY, RA-NO-SNAPSHOT, RA-ENTRY, RA-MESSAGE, RA-HARD-STATE or RA-BATCH has a fixture that makes it fire. AGENTS.md "Testing" asks for corrupt-state fixtures that must fire CD-7 assertions.
- **Two untested paths.** `persist()` re-arms the frame on a journal refusal such as HardStop (node.rs:140-146), and `decode_message` has an entry-level unknown-field branch (convert.rs:86-89). Neither is tested.

## Requirements
§7.7 step 6, CD-7, P10, the AGENTS.md testing standard.

## Area
raft_adapter (node_tests.rs, storage tests, convert tests, test_support.rs); registry RAFT-ADAPTER min_cases (raise it with the tests).

## Acceptance
- A two-node (or one-voter) test persists frames into a journal byte image, recovers it with `journal::recover`, constructs from the `Recovered` log, and checks the term, vote, commit and last index.
- A test steps a valid peer message to its effect.
- Each RA-* invariant has a fixture that fires it.
- The HardStop re-arm and the entry unknown-field refusal are tested.
- RAFT-ADAPTER's min_cases rises to the new count.

title: sim net: Dropped packet records carry no drop reason or copy identity, and drop counts never reach the trace (K-14 first divergence)
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fresh-eyes review of W16.1, the simulated network (5cc5ada, br-w16-1-network-model-40l), 2026-10-04, at HEAD 57cb984, for cc_1. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen copy; every claim was verified by hand at HEAD, where crates/sim is unchanged. Both reviewers raised it as P2.

**The trace's `Dropped` packet record carries no drop reason and no copy identity, and the drop counts never reach the trace.**

**Evidence:**
- `net.rs::record` (336-343) writes `Record::Packet {fate, from, to, bytes}` (trace.rs:241-250).
- Lost, CutAtSend, CutInFlight, QueueFull and Overflow all give the same `packet dropped <from> <to> <hex>` line.
- Sent and duplicated records carry no copy ID.
- `NetCounts` (net.rs:188-221) lives only in memory.

**Failure:**
- Run A loses packet P by chance, which consumes one Network-stream draw.
- Run B refuses P as CutAtSend (a nemesis cutting one event early) or QueueFull, which consumes no draw.
- Both write the same line, so the traces stay byte-identical past the real divergence. The streams are now one draw apart, and K-14's first differing event (§10.2, T-11) names a later, unrelated packet.
- §7.11's "count as a network failure" also leaves no trace evidence.

## Requirements
§10.2 (canonical trace; first divergence), T-3, T-11, K-14, §7.11.

## Area
crates/sim (net.rs, trace.rs: the canonical encoding), net_tests.

## Acceptance
- The drop reason is in the record and in its canonical line, e.g. `packet dropped:queue_full ...`.
- A dropped duplicate reads differently from a dropped original.
- `NetCounts` reaches the trace as deterministic metrics.
- There are canonical-line tests per reason.
- SIM-NET and SIM-TRACE pass. If the trace format version changes, bump it.

## Out of scope
W17's composition of arrivals.

title: BUG: DIFFERENTIAL's counter, final-map and unknown-ID comparisons are never shown live by any mutant; a re-executed replayed refusal is reached on 3 of 400 seeds
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W10.3 (b36a20d, crates/sim/tests/differential.rs), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen tree at f00a912, and both rated this P2. The reviewers re-measured the reach figures in scratch harnesses; JadeOx has not re-run them.

**Three comparison paths are never shown to be live by any mutant,** so if one regressed to `Ok(())`, DIFFERENTIAL would stay green. W10's acceptance ("a broken variant must fail it") is meant to exclude exactly that.
- The paths: `compare_counters` (differential.rs about 739-757), `compare_final` (map contents, order and stored versions; about 761-806), and the unknown-IDs and history check (about 976-1003).
- Measured, every mutant's first divergence is caught at `compare_apply` or `compare_get`. LooseKeyQuota 301, LooseByteQuota 91, VersionOffByOne 400, ReplayAsExecution 399, HistoryUnderWrongIds 400, StaleGet 115. None is caught by counters, the final map or `unknown_ids`.
- VersionOffByOne shifts the result version, which production derives from the already-compared index (`types/src/outcome.rs` about 107-114). So the realistic DM-3 bug, a wrong `Stored.version` seen only through GET and the final map, has no mutant.
- The reviewer's experiment: with the version comparison dropped from `get`/`map`, a state machine storing `version = index - 1` goes from 397 to 0 of 400 seeds caught. With counters off, an overwrite that doesn't reclaim old bytes goes from 391 to 236.

**Also, single reviewer (Opus) P2, not independently re-run:** a capacity refusal that is re-executed once room appears (breaking DM-6, §7.5 step 4 and C-6) is reached on only 3 of 400 seeds (45, 65, 124), and no coverage floor protects it. With PUT only, a key refusal never becomes admissible again; only a byte refusal after a shrinking overwrite does.

**Folded in: P3s both reviewers raised.**
- Every coverage floor is `> 0` (differential.rs about 950), while measured counts run 277 to 6,262. Make them proportional, for example 50 or more.
- Reach gaps:
  - no value above 40 B (nothing near DM-2's 65,536);
  - the 256-byte key is ASCII only;
  - profile (8, 4) has a dead key quota;
  - LooseByteQuota is equivalent to the real machine in two profiles.
- DM-7's `committed_command_bytes` is not compared. A cheap assertion: it grows by the encoded command length exactly on the model's first executions.

## Requirements
T-7, §10.14, W10's acceptance (a broken variant must fail it), §10.15, DM-3, DM-6, C-6.

## Area
sim (`tests/differential.rs`).

## Acceptance
- Wrapper mutants that are each caught **only** by their own path, each asserted caught (with a shrunk log that passes on the real state machine):
  - stored version off by one in `get`/`map` only;
  - live bytes not reclaimed on overwrite (`counters`);
  - reversed map order (DM-4);
  - a phantom history ID.
- A mutant that re-executes a replayed refusal, with a coverage floor for "a replayed refusal that would now fit", and generator bias so it's reached often.
- Coverage floors proportional to measured reach; the reach gaps above closed, or the checks.toml summary narrowed.
- DIFFERENTIAL passes, with min_cases raised.

## Out of scope
DELETE, CAS and SCAN (W27/W28 planned rows).

title: BUG: DOCTOR-CLI never checks the report's numbers (tail offset/length, frames, last index, hard state), and pre-log refusals report zeros as if read
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W23 (keyval doctor), 2026-10-04, at frozen tree e653520. The finding is the Opus reviewer's P2, verified by JadeOx. A P3 both reviewers raised is folded in.

**DOCTOR-CLI never checks the numbers the report gives an operator.** The tests in `crates/cli/tests/doctor.rs` assert only `verdict`, `tail.shape`, `refusal.code`, `lock`, `binding` and `genesis.node_id`, never:
- `tail.start`, `tail.len`, `tail.frame_len`;
- `frames`, `last_index`, `last_term`;
- `journal_len`, `durable_len`;
- `hard_state`.

So the CLI's mapping layer is untested. Swapping `start`/`len` in `tail_report` (`crates/cli/src/doctor.rs`, about lines 249-255), or swapping `last_index`/`frames` or the `hard_state` fields in `Report::examined` (about lines 305-314), passes all 7 DOCTOR-CLI tests and the schema. That leaves O-7's "discard 37-byte incomplete final frame" (offset and length, in the JSON output too) and its hard-state report without evidence at the CLI layer. (JOURNAL-EXAMINE checks the `Examination`; this is the CLI's report.)

**Folded in: both reviewers raised it as P3.** Pre-log refusals report zeros as if they were numbers.
- `Examination::durable_len()` and `last_index()` return 0 when the log was never built (`examine.rs`, about lines 91-112), and `Report::examined` wraps them in `Some`.
- Probe: `--node 2` on node 1's journal, a genesis mismatch. JSON: `frames: 1, durable_len: 0, last_index: 0`. Human: "1 frames read through byte 0; last index 0", which reads as an empty log.
- `Examination::binding()` also returns `Verified` before any genesis was read. The CLI corrects for that; the core API does not.

## Requirements
O-7 (what startup recovery would do, without misreading), O-6, §10.15.

## Area
cli (`src/doctor.rs`, `tests/doctor.rs`), journal (`examine.rs`) for the null-when-unread fields.

## Acceptance
- DOCTOR-CLI asserts full field values on at least these:
  - `torn-mid-payload`: tail start 347, len 44, frame_len 114, durable_len 347.
  - `clean`: frames, last_index, last_term and hard_state {term, vote, commit} equal the README's values.
  - A stale tail: its sequence.
  - A refusal: its `durable_len`.
- A mutant that swaps `start`/`len`, or two of `frames`/`last_index`/`hard_state`, fails a test.
- Fields that were never read (no log built) are `null` in JSON and omitted in text, never 0. The schema keeps them nullable.
- DOCTOR-CLI passes, with `min_cases` raised to match.

## Out of scope
Changing the report's schema version: this is a value fix within v1. If a field's type changes, bump it to v2.

title: fs_storage: let an interrupted init re-run (create_data_dir refuses an existing directory as Failed)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W12.3 (ca94989) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, with line numbers at HEAD 807e06e (fs_storage's reviewed code is unchanged since ca94989 apart from W23.1's read-only handle). Opus raised it as P2 and Fable as P3, and I verified it by hand.

**`create_data_dir` refuses an existing directory, and reports that the same way as a failed parent sync. An init interrupted after `mkdir` therefore cannot be re-run cleanly.**

**Evidence:**
- `crates/fs_storage/src/lib.rs:79-81`: "An existing directory is refused: initialisation never reuses one."
- `lib.rs:88-94` folds `AlreadyExists` into `StorageError::Failed`, the same error a failed parent sync returns (`:99`).
- No public function syncs the parent of a directory that already exists.

**Scenario:**
- `init` is killed after `create_dir` and before the parent fsync, or the parent fsync fails with EIO.
- §7.7 step 0 allows the re-run ("init may be re-run only while the journal holds no complete genesis frame and nothing after it").
- The re-run gets `Failed`, and can tell "exists" from "sync failed" only by comparing the `op` string, so the directory is stuck until the owner steps in.
- If init instead falls back to `FsStorage::open` for an existing directory, the parent is never synced, which breaks DUR-7. After a power loss, the whole data directory can vanish, synced genesis included.

## Requirements
§7.7 step 0 (interrupted-init re-run; sync the parent after creating the data directory); DUR-7; §7.6 "Directory durability".

## Area
crates/fs_storage (`lib.rs`, its tests).

## Acceptance
- `create_data_dir` reports an existing directory distinctly from a failed parent sync, with a typed outcome or error.
- A public way exists to make an existing data directory's entry durable (sync its parent), so the re-run path of init can restore DUR-7 before continuing.
- The doc comment states the §7.7 re-run case instead of denying it.
- There are tests for an existing directory and for a re-run that syncs the parent.

## Out of scope
Deciding in the adapter whether a journal is re-initialisable; recovery's `permits_init` owns that.
