title: M0: Foundations — workspace, gates, spec, spike, registry, commit protocol
description:
## What this milestone delivers
A working development substrate before any database code exists: the `./dev` entry point (a Rust xtask behind a thin launcher) with `doctor`, `check` and `gate fast`; the pinned toolchain and lint policy; AGENTS.md with the normative agent rules; DEPENDENCIES.md; the OpenAPI contract; the Raft determinism spike; domain types and ports; the validated config type with genesis fingerprint; the verification registry and its T0 gate; the work-graph manifest and idempotent bead importer; and the exact-candidate commit wrapper.

Items: W01–W08. M0 exists so that *everything later is verifiable from the first real commit*: gates, receipts, registry traceability and the commit protocol are in place before the first line of consensus or storage code lands.

## Why this ordering
The project's primary goal (G1) is to exercise the agentic development flywheel — plan → beads → parallel agents → mechanical gates → human review of outputs, not code. Nobody reviews code by hand (D-17), so the mechanical quality bar (lints, registry gate, exact-tree commits) must exist *before* the swarm starts. The Raft spike (W02) is the highest-risk item in the whole plan (RISK-1) and runs here, in parallel, so a no-go is discovered before anything is built on the library.

## Bootstrap process constraint
Until W07 (commit wrapper) lands, ALL commits go through a single coordinator agent which stages, runs the bootstrap gate on a frozen candidate copy, and commits; other agents code in parallel and hand files to the coordinator. The full self-serve swarm launches only once W04 + W06 + W07 have all landed.

## Owner checkpoint (after M0)
The owner runs `./dev doctor`, reads the API examples in `api/openapi.yaml`, and looks at `bv` and the list of `planned` checks. No database is advertised yet.

## Process guardrails (apply to every bead in this epic)
- Commits only via `./dev commit` once W07 exists; never raw `git add`/`git commit`; never branches/worktrees (D-16: all agents share `main`).
- Oracles are sacred (P9): never weaken a checker, test, fixture, golden file or corpus seed to get green.
- Evidence over claims (P5): close beads only with passing acceptance receipts; state claims in their class (§10.15).
- Precedence (§0.4): owner > PLAN.md > openapi.yaml > checkers/model/registry > tests > beads > code. If this bead text and PLAN.md ever disagree, PLAN.md wins — file a `conflict` bead, never silently pick a side.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §11.2, §12.1, §17; decisions D-15, D-16, D-17, D-32.

title: M1: Thin durable slice — durable PUT/GET on a real node and a simulated 5-node cluster
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The first runnable, honest slice of keyval: durable PUT/GET through the *real* Raft core — once as a single real node over HTTP (`keyval-server`), and once as a simulated five-node cluster with crash-restart — plus the beginnings of the verification stack (reference model, simulation scheduler, canonical trace, fresh-process replay).

Items: W09–W20 (state machine, reference model, journal, byte-storage adapters, raft-rs adapter + Ready loop, node controller, sim scheduler/network/composition root, production composition root, M1 demo, M1 drift audit).

## Why a thin slice first
D-40: the earliest runnable evidence must exercise *every* layer — HTTP boundary, controller, consensus, journal, recovery, simulation and determinism — before any breadth (DELETE/CAS/SCAN) is added. A convincing simulation without a real durable server is not acceptable, and neither is the reverse (P6: real slices only; no stub presented as the real thing).

## The two stop/go points live here
W13 (the Ready loop over raft-rs) is the second technical stop/go point after the W02 spike. The Ready loop (§7.4) is THE critical persistence protocol: entries, term and vote must be synced before any dependent message leaves the node; getting this ordering wrong is the classic way replicated systems lose acknowledged data (RISK-2).

## Determinism is non-negotiable from M1 on
Same seed + same build ⇒ byte-identical canonical trace, in fresh OS processes (P4, T-3, T-11). Any nondeterminism found later is a P0. The simulator runs the same state machine, Raft adapter and journal code as production (P3) — only adapters differ.

## Owner checkpoint (demo m1)
`./dev demo m1`: one real node, PUT and GET, kill and restart it, read the key back; `./dev sim run --seed 42 --profile slice` twice with identical trace hashes.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic (commit wrapper, P9 oracle protection, claim classes, §0.4 precedence). From M1 on, verification work (tracks D/E) runs in parallel with product work — it is never bolted on at the end.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §11.6; decisions D-28, D-40; risks RISK-2, RISK-6.

title: M2: Real cluster — five processes, routing, launcher, doctor, crash probes
description:
## What this milestone delivers
Five *real* OS processes forming a cluster on one machine: peer transport over HTTP, write routing (307 redirect to leader / 503 with node list), the `./dev cluster` launcher with PID receipts, the `keyval doctor` offline data-directory verifier, and the real-file process-crash probes + five-node lifecycle smoke test.

Items: W21–W26 (peer transport & routing, cluster launcher, CLI doctor, crash probes & smoke, M2 demo, M2 drift audit).

## Why this matters
Simulated bytes cannot prove that the real file adapter drives real files correctly (D-33). M2 closes the loop between the simulated world of M1 and physical processes: SIGKILL at defined write/sync boundaries, restart from the real data directory, and verification that every acknowledged write survived. Note the honest limit: SIGKILL does not drop the OS page cache, so these are *process-crash* probes, not power-loss tests; power-loss durability is a stated Assumption (D-46), partially covered by the sync-order check at the syscall boundary.

## Safety rules for real processes
The launcher records PID receipts and only ever signals processes it started; it never kills by port, never uses broad pkill, and never deletes data. Destructive re-initialisation is a separate, explicit owner action outside every gate (O-2). A node that lost its data directory must REFUSE to start blank — silent re-join is Raft amnesia and can lose committed entries (D-52).

## Owner checkpoint (demo m2)
`./dev demo m2`: a 5-node local cluster; the owner kills and restarts nodes by hand including the leader; watches `/v1/cluster`; runs `keyval doctor` on a stopped node's data directory.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. Manage nodes only through `./dev cluster …` (AGENTS.md rule 18).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §10.17, §11.6; decisions D-33, D-46, D-52.

title: M3: Full product surface — DELETE/CAS/SCAN/status, full API, CLI, conformance
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The complete product surface: DELETE, COMPARE_SWAP, SCAN, request-status lookup, the full retry/ambiguity lifecycle (attach, conflict, history_full, capacity_exceeded), the complete HTTP API passing an independent conformance suite, the reference model server, and the full `keyval` CLI with its durable pending store.

Items: W27–W35 (DELETE/CAS, SCAN, request status & retry lifecycle, model server, conformance suite, complete HTTP surface, full CLI, M3 demo, M3 drift audit).

## The semantic heart of keyval
Retry safety never expires: every write carries a client 128-bit Idempotency-Key; its first execution (log index, command digest, terminal result) is replicated state for the life of the cluster (DM-5, D-07). A CAS mismatch and a live-quota capacity_exceeded are *committed terminal decisions* that consume the request ID — they prove execution exactly like a success (§9.3). Unknown outcomes are first-class, never guessed (P8).

## Independence discipline
The conformance suite (W31) and reference model server (W30) depend on NO production crate and talk only HTTP (T-12). Semantic tests must pass against the model server *before* the real server is complete — this validates the suite and the spec independently, and is why suite and server can be built in parallel by different agents (§11.7 independent authorship).

## Owner checkpoint (demo m3)
`./dev demo m3`: two clients contend with CAS on one version; paginate Unicode keys; replay a request ID; resolve an unknown_outcome with `keyval status` and `keyval resume`.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. W32's closure is the single switch that turns registry spec↔code/spec↔tests conditions from report-mode to enforcing (D-49).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §8, §7.8, §10.8; decisions D-07, D-35, D-36, D-54.

title: M4: Evidence — checkers, swarm campaigns, bug injection, gates, crash packs
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The full evidence machine: workload generator, nemesis and swarm fault campaigns with coverage accounting, all fourteen checkers (K-1…K-14), non-vacuity enforcement, crash packs and scenario shrinking, the bug-injection checker self-test (B-01…B-22), staged gate tiers T0–T3 with receipts and the failure outbox, parity checks, fuzzing and code-coverage reporting, measurements, and the `./dev status` owner view.

Items: W36–W50 plus W53 (workload, nemesis/swarm/heal, checkers, non-vacuity+coverage, sim commands+crash packs, full-op profiles, shrinker, bug variants, gate tiers+scheduler, measurements, parity, status view, fuzz+coverage, M4 drift audit).

## The philosophy being exercised
Evidence over claims (P5): every MUST requirement has a registered, executed check; every claim carries its class — invariant / simulation-evidenced / measurement / assumption / proposal (§10.15). A weaker class never justifies a stronger claim: "no violation in 100,000 seeds on build X" is evidence, never "keyval is linearizable". No vacuous passes (P10): a zero-test selection, an unexercised fault, an exhausted budget or an incomplete campaign FAILS. Checkers are themselves checked: deliberately injected bugs must be caught by their designated checker, with the unmutated control passing (§10.6) — the mechanical guard against agents weakening oracles to get green (RISK-3).

## Parallelism note
M4 work starts as soon as its dependencies land (from M1 onwards); it runs in parallel with M2 and M3. Milestones are views over work items, not phases.

## Owner checkpoint (M4 review — reports, not a demo)
The owner opens a crash pack from the corpus, replays and shrinks it; reads the bug-variant report, coverage matrix and measurements; checks `./dev status`.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. Every failing case fixed goes into `sim/corpus/` in the same commit (AGENTS.md rule 9); the corpus is append-only (P9).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §10 (whole section), §12.1; decisions D-14, D-22, D-23, D-24, D-34, D-66, D-67.

title: M5: v1 — clean-state rehearsal, T3 release campaign, Definition of Done
description:
## What this milestone delivers
v1 itself: the final (M5) drift audit, the clean-state rehearsal (fresh clone → doctor → build → cluster init+up → smoke), the T3 release campaign (≥ 100,000 fresh swarm seeds, 100 fresh-process replay pairs, every bug variant, required coverage cells), and the Definition-of-Done reconciliation with the final evidence report.

Items: W51, W52.

## Definition of Done (condensed from §13)
1. Five-node system starts from one config, exposes API/CLI/status, persists real bytes, recovers without operator repair. 2. Every MUST requirement active and passed on the release build; registry gate green. 3. T3: 0 violations over ≥100k seeds, every required coverage cell non-zero, no incomplete runs; the release build is the exact tree T3 ran on (D-58). 4. Every bug variant caught, control passing. 5. Determinism self-check clean (100 replay pairs). 6. Conformance 100% vs model server, real single node and 5-node cluster. 7. Crash probes + lifecycle smoke + parity pass. 8. T0 enforced on every commit; a scheduled failure demonstrably becomes exactly one bead even across a tracker outage. 9. Measurements report generated. 10. No open P0 beads, no open P1 BUG beads (W51/W52 orchestration beads exempt while they run), no open conflict beads, no unanswered owner disposition. 11. Owner checkpoints M1–M5 complete; drift audits complete with no finding above P2 open. 12. All 53 work items closed with acceptance receipts. 13. Decision log up to date. 14. Final evidence report states every claim in its correct class.

Not required: human code review, hosted CI, performance numbers. A complete implementation with missing evidence is not v1; a convincing simulation without a real durable server is not v1 either.

## Sequencing rule (D-73)
The final audit runs BEFORE the T3 campaign (inside W51). A code-changing finding discovered after the campaign spawns a new release-campaign bead and T3 re-runs on the new tree — evidence is never silently carried across trees.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §13, §10.10 (T3), §10.11, §11.9; decisions D-58, D-73.

title: BUG: under sustained client writes the controller proposes ahead of every queued peer message, so a leader commits nothing and check-quorum deposes it
description:
## Context
Found in PeachAnchor's review of W14.1 (906fc83, the serial controller core) for cc_1, 2026-10-04. The code is unchanged at HEAD (6b84d9d, W14.2).

**Under sustained client writes, a leader processes no peer message: it commits nothing and check-quorum deposes it.**

`Controller::turn` (`crates/node/src/controller.rs`) proposes before it takes any queued input:

```rust
if self.library_idle() && self.propose(effects) {
    return true;
}
let peers_wait = self.raft.outstanding_sync().is_some();
match self.queue.next(peers_wait) { ... }
```

1. Each proposal leaves a sync outstanding.
2. While a sync is outstanding, peer envelopes wait (`peers_wait`), but client attempts are still handed over, so new writes become waiting proposals.
3. When the sync completes, the next turn proposes again before any peer envelope.

So whenever at least one write arrives per sync cycle, follower append and heartbeat responses never leave the queue.

## Evidence
A scratch test, not committed, over the crate's own harness: `test_support::Member` with three voters and the `Recorder` double. It is at `/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-keyval/d767163f-b7de-47a1-82c3-b6219ddfff4a/scratchpad/candidate/crates/node/src/review_scratch_tests.rs`.

**Setup:** elect a leader. Then, each round:
1. one client write reaches the leader while its sync is outstanding;
2. the leader's sync completes;
3. all envelopes are delivered both ways, and followers complete their syncs;
4. every node ticks once.

**Result:**

| round | leader role | leader commit | leader queued |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | Leader | 1 | – |
| 1 | Leader | 1 | 2 |
| 16 | Leader | 1 | 46 |
| 36 | Leader | 1 | 66 |
| 41 | Follower | 1 | 0 |

Not one write commits. Follower responses pile up in the leader's queue until check-quorum (on, §7.10) steps it down after about one election timeout of ticks without them.

**Control:** the same rounds with no extra writes. The first write commits in round 1 (commit 2), and the leader keeps leading, with nothing queued.

**With the real write path:** I re-ran the same scenario over `Member::fresh_writes`, with W14.2's `WritePath` behind the seam, at HEAD 6b84d9d. The result is identical: commit stays at 1, the queue reaches 66, and the leader is deposed at about round 41.

## Why it is a defect
- §7.10: overdue ticks are processed "interleaved with other inputs, so network and read work is not starved". The same principle is broken here, by proposals rather than ticks.
- §7.4 step 1 feeds "one input: a tick, a peer message, or a proposal". Nothing ranks proposals above peer messages.
- W14.1's commit message says inputs leave in arrival order. The proposal's absolute priority breaks that.
- Downstream: K-9 (liveness), and every write under load gets `unknown_outcome`, or `busy` once deadlines fill.

## Requirements
§7.4, §7.10, §7.11, F-7, K-9, CD-9.

## Area
`crates/node` (controller.rs `turn`): W14's area. W14.2 builds directly on it.

## Acceptance
- With the library idle, a turn takes queued peer envelopes and waiting proposals fairly: by arrival order (a proposal ordered by its attempt's admission), or alternating. Whichever rule it is, it is stated in the docs.
- A test in the controller's tests reproduces the scenario above: a three-voter cluster under one write per sync cycle. Every write commits, the leader keeps leading, and the queue stays bounded by the in-flight responses.
- The same test fails on 906fc83's `turn`.
- NODE-CONTROLLER passes with `min_cases` raised.

## Out of scope
Batching several proposals into one Ready. v1 feeds one input per Ready (§7.4).

title: BUG: matches! on domain enums hides catch-all arms past the CD-5 lint (Refusal::submitted fails open)
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W04 code (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03). Both independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) raised it, and I verified it by hand.

`matches!` on a domain enum expands to a `match` with a hidden `_ => false` arm. Clippy's `wildcard_enum_match_arm` does not lint inside macro expansions. So CD-5's catch-all ban is bypassed silently: `types` builds clean under `forbid`, and LINT-PROBES has no `matches!` probe to prove or disprove the lint's coverage. The two existing probes are `xtask/probes/deterministic/src/wildcard_arm.rs` and `binding_catch_all_arm.rs`.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01), production code only:**
- `crates/types/src/client.rs:243` `Refusal::submitted`: `matches!(self, Self::UnknownOutcome)`. **It fails open.** Say a later bead adds a `Refusal` variant for an attempt that was submitted and then lost, for example on shutdown or when superseded after submission (§7.8). `submitted()` returns false, the adapter renders `attempt_state: "not_submitted"` for a submitted attempt, and A-5 is violated.
- `crates/types/src/lifecycle.rs:32` `Lifecycle::can_become`: `matches!` over a `(self, next)` tuple, so a new state is silently refused every transition.
- `crates/types/src/lifecycle.rs:46` `Lifecycle::is_ready`.

The test-only use at `client.rs:403` is fine.

## Requirements
CD-5 ("No catch-all arms on domain enums, so adding a variant forces every handler to be updated"), A-5, P10 (lint probes prove enforcement).

## Area
types (`client.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`); xtask lint probes and the CD-5 AST check, as a short reservation.

## Acceptance
- The three functions use exhaustive `match`es with every variant spelled out. `can_become` lists each allowed pair explicitly.
- A LINT-PROBES case shows whether `matches!` on a domain enum is caught in a deterministic crate. If clippy can't catch it, extend the CD-5 AST check, or ban the pattern with a documented rule, and add a probe for that.
- `./dev check LINT-PROBES` and `./dev gate fast` pass.

## Out of scope
`matches!` in tests, and on non-domain types.

title: BUG: LogicalLog::apply accepts impossible hard-state and term histories (commit/term regression, second vote in a term, decreasing entry terms), so the truncation-below-commit guard can be bypassed
description:
## Context
Found in the fresh-eyes review of W11.1/W11.2 (PeachAnchor for cc_1, 2026-10-04, HEAD c2e53f0; an independent second reviewer agrees). Confirmed by scratch tests through the real `LogicalLog::append`, run in a private copy and never committed.

`LogicalLog::apply` is the single path for live appends and W11.3's recovery replay. It checks sequence, offset, index gaps, truncation at or below the persisted commit, and commit beyond the log. It never checks a new hard state or the entry terms against what is already persisted.
- `crates/journal/src/log.rs:315-317`: `if let Some(state) = hard_state { self.hard_state = state; }` is unconditional. A later hard state may lower `commit` or `term`, or change `vote` within the same term.
- `log.rs:289-292`: the truncation guard compares against the *latest* hard state's commit, so any regression weakens it.
- `record.rs:449-461` (`RaftBatch::new`) and `log.rs:279-295` check only that indices are consecutive.
  - Entry terms may decrease along the log, or exceed the persisted term.
  - `record.rs:547` accepts entry term 0, because `Term`'s minimum is 0, although only the dummy index 0 has term 0.
  - `record.rs:575-578` accepts a vote for a node outside the voter set.

**Counterexamples.** Each one is accepted:
1. Commit regression replaces committed entries.
   - F2: entries 1–3 in term 1, with hs{term 1, commit 3}.
   - F3: hs{term 1, commit 1}.
   - F4: entry 2 in term 2, with hs{term 2, commit 1}.
   - Result: last index 2, so entries 2–3, which F2 persisted as committed, are replaced.
2. A second vote in a term, then a term regression.
   - hs{term 5, vote 2}, then hs{term 5, vote 3}, then hs{term 3, vote 1}.
   - Result: `hard_state()` reports term 3, vote 1.
3. Entry terms going backwards.
   - hs{term 2}, then entries 1 (term 9) and 2 (term 4) with no hard state.
   - Result: accepted.

A correct raft-rs writer never produces these: commit and term are monotonic, a vote is fixed within its term, and entry terms are non-decreasing and at most the node's term. So there is no wrong result today. But `apply` is where recovery must stop on "an impossible index relationship", and the live path treats an `apply` error as an invariant failure. As it stands, a writer bug (for example in W13's adapter) or CRC-valid damage would be accepted silently. Recovery would then rebuild a node that has forgotten committed entries or its vote, a Raft-safety violation (C-1, C-2, DUR-2).

## Requirements
- §7.6 Logical truncation: "Replacing at or below the persisted commit index is an invariant violation". A persisted commit stays persisted; a later frame cannot lower the bound.
- §7.6 Fail closed: "An impossible index relationship or a genesis mismatch also stops the node with a specific error (DUR-6, DUR-8)". §7.7 step 3: "Any other damage → refuse".
- CD-7: assert invariants where state changes.
- DUR-2: term and vote are persisted before any message that depends on them. Recovering a lower term or a different vote defeats that.
- W11.3's bead: "genesis/index-relationship errors stop the node with specific errors".

## Area
journal: `crates/journal/src/log.rs`, possibly `record.rs`. SunnyDog holds `crates/journal/**` for W11.3, so this is best folded into W11.3 or landed right after it.

## Acceptance
`apply` refuses each of the following, each with its own `JournalError` and with nothing changed:
- a hard-state term below the persisted term;
- a hard-state commit below the persisted commit;
- a vote changed within the same term (Some(a) to Some(b), or Some to None);
- an entry term of 0;
- entry terms that decrease, against the preceding kept entry and within the batch;
- an entry term above the term in force after the batch.

Recovery (W11.3) also refuses a hard-state vote for a node outside the genesis voter set. Each rule has a test, including counterexample 1. JOURNAL-LOG passes, and W11.4 gains a refuse golden for the commit-regression journal.

## Out of scope
Changing the frame or record format.

title: sim net: the in-flight bound is a free parameter, not a registered limit, and overflow is silent loss instead of an incomplete run (CD-9, P10)
description:
## Context
GoldenHorizon's fresh-eyes review of W16.1, the simulated network (5cc5ada, br-w16-1-network-model-40l), 2026-10-04, at HEAD 57cb984, for cc_1. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen copy; every claim was verified by hand at HEAD, where crates/sim is unchanged. Opus rated it P2 and Fable P3 (its bounds note), so both raised it.

**The global in-flight bound `max_in_flight` is a free parameter, not a registered limit, and overflowing it is silent packet loss, not an incomplete run.**

**Evidence:**
- `NetConfig::max_in_flight` (net.rs:144-147, 355, 361) is caller-chosen; the tests use 1,000,000, 1,000 and 2.
- Nothing ties it to `Limit::SimEventsPerRun` the way `EventBudget::DEFAULT` is tied.
- An overflow is a `DropReason` that Raft tolerates.
- `loads` and `LinkMatrix::cut` are unbounded BTreeMap/BTreeSet; their "at most 20" is a comment.

**Failure:** a composition root picks a value below the event budget, so a fan-out bug becomes counted packet loss and the run passes. §7.11 says hitting the simulator's event bound makes the run incomplete (P10).

## Requirements
CD-9, §7.11, P10, §10.2.

## Area
crates/sim (net.rs, tests); limits registry if a row is added.

## Acceptance
- `max_in_flight` is derived from `Limit::SimEventsPerRun` or the run's `EventBudget` (or registered).
- Overflow is a typed refusal the harness reports as incomplete, like the scheduler's QueueFull.
- The link maps are bounded to voters × (voters − 1), or asserted.
- There are tests for both.

## Out of scope
Per-link queue limits (already registered).

title: ./dev commit --close leaves the bead closed and requirement flips in place when its gate fails, so every later closure fails too
description:
## Context
SunnyDog's W11 `--close` failed its gate at about 02:10Z on 2026-10-04: registry condition 2, because DUR-4 had no covering check. By then the closure had already changed shared state, and nothing undid it:
- `br close` had run and the tracker export was flushed, so the shared tracker showed W11 closed;
- `registry/requirements.toml` in the shared working tree had DUR-4/5/6/8 flipped to `active`.

Every closure recomputes every status from the export, both ways (xp14). So until SunnyDog restored things by hand (reopened W11, flushed, put `requirements.toml` back to HEAD's text), **every other agent's `./dev commit --close` would have recomputed W11 as closed, carried its flips and failed the same gate**. One failed closure blocks all closures.

**Evidence (HEAD 12fccff):** `xtask/src/closure.rs:295-330` `TrackerStep::apply` runs `tracker.close`, `tracker.flush` and writes `requirements.toml` before the gate (`commit::run_prepared`). On `Outcome::GateFailed` (`commit.rs:553-556`), `closure::run` (`closure.rs:172-178`) reports the failure and leaves the tracker and working tree as `apply` left them. The module doc (lines 19-23) assumes a re-run finishes an *interrupted* closure. A gate failure is not an interruption: the closure cannot pass until code changes.

## Requirements
§11.3 step 7, §11.10 (a refused commit leaves shared state as it was), §10.13 (statuses derived on every tree), rule 16.

## Area
xtask (`closure.rs`, maybe `commit.rs`'s `Prepare` contract).

## Acceptance
- When a closure's gate fails, the wrapper restores what `apply` changed before it returns: the bead's prior tracker status, a flushed export, and `registry/requirements.toml` back to its pre-apply text, but only if the wrapper wrote it. The report says so.
- This holds for `--failed` records too: the labels and comment, or at least a clear report of what stayed.
- A fixture: a closure whose gate fails leaves the tracker export and `requirements.toml` byte-identical to before.
- A second closure run right after a failed one does not inherit its flips.
- DEV-CLOSE passes with raised min_cases.

An alternative design is fine if it keeps the shared tracker untouched until the gate passes, for example by computing the closure's export into the candidate only.

## Out of scope
The W11 DUR-4 coverage itself (SunnyDog's follow-up).

title: Closure gap: a subtask whose acceptance check lands in a later split-off bead's commit cannot close (W02.1 / br-gqxq)
description:
## Context
`./dev commit --close <bead>` (W07.3; xtask/src/closure.rs work_commit and validate) requires the newest passing accept receipt to name the tree of the newest main commit whose message carries `Bead: <bead>`. W02.1 (br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi) had its xtask half split into br-gqxq because xtask/** was reserved for W07 at the time. W02.1's work commit is 07e9ec7 (tree 8c72e61a, which vendors raft). Its acceptance check, RAFT-VENDOR, only exists from br-gqxq's commit 79de0e8 (tree 3114abd4). So:
- `./dev accept br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi --tree 8c72e61a…` cannot select RAFT-VENDOR, which does not exist in that tree. It fails, as P10 requires.
- An accept receipt on 3114abd4 is refused by --close as 'wrong tree' (P11).
W02.1 therefore cannot close through the wrapper, and W02.2 → W02.3 → W02.4 → W02.5 → W02 (critical-path risk item; W13 depends on it) stay blocked. br-gqxq itself is unaffected: its work commit carries its own check.

## Requirements
P11, §11.3 step 7, §11.4 (closing needs a receipt for the tree that carried the work), rule 16.

## Options (owner decision)
A. Owner override for W02.1 (§0.4 rule 1): close it with a bead comment citing br-gqxq's committed-tree gate receipt (gate-fast-20261003T164707Z-3114abd48aec-2169983) and an accept receipt for RAFT-VENDOR on 3114abd4.
B. A W02.1-trailer commit on top of 79de0e8. This needs genuine W02.1-scoped content; an empty commit would be gaming the rule, and ./dev commit presumably refuses one.
C. Convention for future splits, needing no code change: commits of a split-off bead also carry the parent subtask's trailer (`Bead: <split-off>` and `Bead: <parent>`). closure.rs already matches any `Bead:` line, so the parent's work tree becomes the one that contains its check. Document it in AGENTS.md. This does not help W02.1 retroactively.
D. A wrapper change (W07 area, plan-level): treat the newest commit of a bead that <bead> depends on, and that was split from it, as carrying <bead>'s work. This weakens the exact-tree rule's simplicity; not recommended.
Recommendation: A for W02.1 now, plus C going forward.

## Area
.beads (decision); AGENTS.md if C is adopted.

## Acceptance
W02.1 is closed with receipt-backed evidence the owner accepts, and W02.2 becomes ready. If C is adopted, AGENTS.md states the trailer convention for split-off beads.

## Out of scope
Rewriting history (amending 79de0e8 to add a trailer is forbidden).

comments.text: OWNER DECISION (about 20:00Z, 2026-10-03, relayed by cc_1, which asked the owner directly): adopt option C. AGENTS.md documents that every commit of a split-off bead also carries the parent's 'Bead: <parent>' line, in the existing bead/commit conventions section (no new numbered rule). W02.1 was already closed by override A (7564015). SunnyDog takes the AGENTS.md change under br-njik.

title: BUG: the byte-storage port cannot report an I/O failure, so the core can never move to failed
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W04.3's ports (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand).

The byte-storage port's mutating effects have no way to report failure back to the core. The core can therefore never move a node to `failed` on an I/O error.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01):**
- `crates/types/src/effects.rs:85-111`: `Input` has `Client`, `Peer`, `Tick` and `SyncDone { seq, incarnation }`. `SyncDone` carries no result, and no input reports a failed `Append`, `Truncate` or `Sync`.
- `crates/types/src/effects.rs:127` onwards: the `Effect::Append`, `Truncate` and `Sync` variants.
- `StorageError` (`in_process.rs:56`) covers only the synchronous in-process reads and the `DataDir` calls.

Scenario: fsync returns EIO.
- **If the adapter drops the completion,** the node wedges. §7.4 feeds nothing more until `SyncDone` arrives, and health still says `ready`.
- **If the adapter sends `SyncDone` anyway,** the core releases acks and votes over unsynced data, violating §7.4.

## Requirements
- PLAN.md §7.11: "An unexpected I/O error stops writes on that node and moves it to `failed`, visible in health."
- CD-6: I/O errors are result values.
- §7.2: "Adapters turn outside events (… I/O completions) into inputs."
- DM-7: the journal hard stop leads to `Failed`.
- W04 acceptance: "all ports".

## Area
types (`effects.rs`); its consumers are W11 (journal engine), W12 (simulated disk), W14 (the node controller) and W22 (the file adapter).

## Acceptance
- An I/O completion can report failure. Two possible shapes:
  - `SyncDone` carries `Result<(), StorageFailure>`;
  - or a separate `IoFailed { seq, incarnation, … }` input.

  Either way it is incarnation-stamped and ignored when stale, like `SyncDone`.
- A test shows that a failed sync input is distinguishable, and that `is_stale_completion` covers it.
- The controller's transition to `Failed` itself belongs to W14, but the port must exist first.
- Related, needing confirmation: no shutdown input exists, yet §8.4 has `unavailable` while "shutting down" and §7.8 has "shutdown: 504". Decide whether the core needs a `Shutdown` input or the adapter handles this alone.

## Out of scope
Disk-full as a tested fault (§9.2 excludes it in v1).

title: BUG: after a queued owner's deadline its request ID stays in to_propose, so a retry is handed to the library twice and a drop of the copy answers busy (not_submitted) for a submitted attempt
description:
Context: found in SunnyDog's review of W14.2 (br-w14-2-write-path-attempts-h2t). Both fresh reviewers (Opus, Fable) raised it independently (review-w14-2 thread).
- `WritePath::expired` withdraws a Queued owner's pending proposal but leaves its request ID in `to_propose` (crates/node/src/write_path.rs, `expired`, Owner + `queued`).
- `next_proposal` hands over any pending with an owner without checking `Stage::Queued`.
- So a later pending with the same ID sits in `to_propose` twice, and the same attempt is handed to the library twice. The later pending comes from the client's retry with the same ID (A-1), or at once from a different-command waiter behind it that re-enters via `fail_pending`.
- If the library drops the second copy (`ProposalDropped`, e.g. at its uncommitted bound), `proposed(Err(Dropped))` removes the pending whose first copy is already in the log. It answers the attempt `busy` (`attempt_state: not_submitted`). When the first copy commits, nobody is answered.
- If the second copy is taken instead, a duplicate entry is appended. It applies as `Replayed` and costs commit index, journal bytes and in-flight accounting.

Reachable whenever a sync stays outstanding for `write_deadline_ticks`: `propose` runs only when `library_idle`, so attempts stay Queued meanwhile. The sim disk's latency faults produce exactly that. `NODE-WRITE-TABLE` does not catch it: `stage == Submitted || to_propose.contains(id)` holds with a stale duplicate. Also, `status_changed`'s early return, taken when `pending` is empty, leaves stale IDs behind.

Independent counterexample (bench, HEAD 51c5c69, private candidate, not committed). Both tests fail today:
1. attempt 1 = put(1,k,v) is Queued; `expire(1)` gives busy; attempt 2 = the same op (a retry) is Queued again.
   - `next_proposal()` gives attempt 2, and `proposed(2, Ok)`.
   - `next_proposal()` gives attempt 2 AGAIN; `proposed(2, Err(Dropped))` gives `Refused(Busy)` for attempt 2; `apply(cmd)` answers nothing.
2. Owner r/A Queued, waiter r/B behind it; `expire(owner)`. Then `next_proposal()` gives attempt 2, `proposed(Ok)`, and `next_proposal()` gives attempt 2 again.

Requirements: A-5 (MUST: only a never-submitted attempt may be reported not_submitted), K-12 (unknown-outcome honesty; B-15), §7.8 (Submitted row; a Dropped reclassifies only a copy with nothing appended), F-7 step 9, CD-7 (NODE-WRITE-TABLE should state it), CD-9 (`to_propose` bound).

Area: crates/node (write_path.rs, write_path_tests.rs, write_path/invariant_fixtures.rs). If the case count changes: NODE-WRITE-PATH's min_cases in xtask/src/check.rs + registry/checks.toml (short shared reservation).

Acceptance:
- a withdrawn Queued proposal leaves no ID in `to_propose`;
- `next_proposal` hands over only `Stage::Queued` pendings;
- `NODE-WRITE-TABLE` asserts that `to_propose` names each Queued pending exactly once and nothing else, with a firing fixture for a stale or duplicate entry;
- bench tests for both counterexamples above (retry after a queued expiry; behind-waiter re-entry after a queued expiry) assert one hand-over, and that the attempt is answered only by its entry's apply;
- `proposed(Err)` treats only the copy just handed over as "nothing appended" (Opus).
- Folded in, raised by both reviewers (P3): the uncommitted-bytes tests cover a submitted proposal (not only queued ones) and the exact boundary (in_flight + len == max admitted, + 1 refused), and show that a write refused `busy` is admitted once the in-flight proposals apply (`pending()`/`in_flight_bytes()` back to 0).
- `./dev check NODE-WRITE-PATH` passes; T0 green.

Out of scope: the attached-waiter classification for a never-submitted proposal (spec question, P3); step 8 vs the library's empty-uncommitted admission (P3).

title: journal recovery: a CRC-valid header with an impossible version, kind, reserved byte or length is cut as a torn tail (or offered for re-init) instead of refusing
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W11.3 (c0a65ba) and W11.1 (decd328) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7beeb19, at cc_1's request. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) both raised it, and I verified it by hand. Severity P2 from both reviewers; filed at priority 1 because it touches DUR-6/DUR-9 and, through a lost vote, C-2.

**A header whose CRC-32C validates but whose fields are impossible is treated as crash damage.** It can be discarded as a torn tail, or reported as an interrupted init that `init` may then overwrite.

**Evidence (HEAD 7beeb19):**
- `crates/journal/src/frame.rs:285-305`: `decode_header` checks the header checksum first, and only then returns `UnsupportedVersion`, `UnknownKind`, `NonZeroReserved` or `PayloadTooLong`. Those errors therefore mean "intact header, impossible content".
- `crates/journal/src/recovery.rs:252-254`: `let Ok(header) = decode_header(&header_bytes) else { return Ok(Slot::Damaged); };` folds all of them into `Damaged`.
- `recovery.rs:329`: the resync then resumes one byte later. If no later valid frame exists, the region is a torn tail and `truncate_to()` cuts it. For the first frame, `recovery.rs:371-373` returns `IncompleteGenesis`, and `permits_init()` (`:164`) is true.

A real torn append is a prefix of a frame this build wrote, so its intact header always has version 1, kind 1 or 2, reserved 0 and length ≤ 1 MiB. Anything else is detectable damage outside the crash model.

**Scenarios:**
- `clean.bin` plus a synced F4 whose version byte is 2, with both CRCs recomputed: `recover` returns Ok and truncates F4, discarding its entries and its hard state (term 2, vote 3, commit 3). The node restarts in term 1 with no vote and can vote again in term 2.
- A v1 binary opening a small v2 journal gets `IncompleteGenesis`, and the journal is offered for re-init (§7.7 step 0 forbids this).

**Related hardening, which both reviewers touched:**
- `decode_header` accepts sequence 0, which nothing writes. A CRC-valid seq-0 frame after garbage is never "later" than genesis (`recovery.rs:294`), so it too yields `IncompleteGenesis` (Fable).
- `IncompleteGenesis` permits init with up to one maximum frame of content, although an interrupted init can leave at most one genesis frame's worth (Opus).

## Requirements
DUR-5 (the format version exists to be detected), DUR-6 (never silently erase synced data), DUR-9 (fail closed outside the crash model), §7.6 ("unless the header checksum validates"), §7.7 step 0, C-2.

## Area
crates/journal (`recovery.rs`, `frame.rs`, `recovery_tests.rs`, `golden/` only by adding new files).

## Acceptance
- A CRC-valid header with an unsupported version, unknown kind, non-zero reserved byte or over-length payload refuses recovery with a typed `RecoveryError`, whether it is the first frame or later. It is never truncated, and it never permits `init`.
  - Over-length is named a tail marker in §7.6. If you read that as applying to CRC-valid headers too, raise it with the owner, since §7.6's own sentence says intact headers are trusted.
- Sequence 0 is refused by `decode_header`.
- `permits_init()` holds only when what follows a missing genesis fits one genesis frame.
- There is a recovery test or new golden for each case: version, kind, reserved, length, seq 0, the first-frame variant, and the v2 downgrade. JOURNAL-RECOVERY passes with raised min_cases.

## Out of scope
Changing the frame format.

title: BUG: DOCTOR-CLI flakes under load: a sibling test's child inherits data_dir's LOCK flock, so the doctor sees a live node and reports no numbers
description:
## Context
VioletOwl's private gate for W14.3 (tree 7a5906ca on 6ef9b09, `crates/node` only) failed `-p cli --test doctor` once:

```
panicked at crates/cli/tests/doctor.rs:513:13: rule: the report gives exactly the numbers recovery read (O-7); golden=logical-truncation
  left:  every number null
  right: durable_len 461, frames 4, ...
```

The log is `artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261004T075729Z-7a5906ca1256-2591636/tests.log`, around line 26. The same tree then passed 5/5 alone and 8/8 for the whole binary. A T0 test that fails at random is a red gate (P0).

**Cause, reproduced in mechanism:**
- `data_dir()` in `crates/cli/tests/doctor.rs` makes every fixture directory "locked once": `FsStorage::open`, then `lock()`, then `drop`.
- libtest runs the binary's tests on parallel threads, and nearly every test spawns `keyval`.
- A child spawned by another thread while this thread holds the LOCK fd inherits the fd, and so the flock, until it execs. `O_CLOEXEC` releases it only at exec.
- Under gate load that child can stay unexec'd long enough for this test's doctor to probe `LockProbe::Live`. The verdict is then `live` and every number is null, which is exactly the failure above.
- The assertion printed only the numbers, so the log did not show the verdict. That breaks W01.6 rule 1.

**Probe (private, C):** one thread takes a flock, holds it 200 µs, releases it, and then spawns `flock -n LOCK true`. Six threads spawn `/bin/true` in a loop. Out of 2,000 probes, 209 (with fork) and 216 (with posix_spawn) still found the lock held after the release.

## Requirements
O-7 (the doctor's verdicts), W01.6 rules 1 and 4 (assertion context; no flaky required cases), P10.

## Area
`crates/cli/tests/doctor.rs` (the test fixture only; the doctor itself is right: a held lock is a live node).

## Acceptance
- `data_dir()` never takes the lock in the test process. It writes the empty `LOCK` file that `FsStorage::lock` leaves (create, no truncate, no bytes), so the directory is the same on disk and no flock can leak to a sibling's child.
- The numbers assertion prints the report's verdict and lock state, so a recurrence is diagnosable from its log.
- `./dev check DOCTOR-CLI` passes (min_cases unchanged: no case is added or removed); T0 green.

## Out of scope
The same race class in `crates/fs_storage` unit tests, filed separately.

xtask (`src/registry.rs` files module, its tests); the REGISTRY-FILES row.

title: BUG: the doctor's golden suites skip impossible-version-final (17 of 18) and nothing ties them, or the schema's enums, to their sources
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W23 (keyval doctor: 807e06e, 72d19aa), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Two independent reviewers worked on a frozen tree at e653520 (Opus and Fable), and JadeOx verified the finding by hand. Both reviewers rated it P2.

JOURNAL-EXAMINE ("reaches recovery's verdict on every recovery golden") and DOCTOR-CLI ("on every recovery golden") overclaim. So does §12.2's W23 acceptance ("Correct verdict on every journal golden recovery case").
- `crates/journal/golden/recovery/` holds **18** goldens, and `golden_recovery.rs` lists all 18.
- Both doctor tables hold **17**: `examine_tests.rs` (rows from about line 92) and `crates/cli/tests/doctor.rs` (about lines 152-200). Both omit `impossible-version-final.bin`.
- That golden landed in 76af4b0 (br-o69w), **before** W23.1's 807e06e, so the omission is W23's. W23.1's closure comment also says "all 17 recovery goldens".
- Consequence: `RefusalCode::ImpossibleHeader` (schema value `impossible_header`) is produced by no test. Nothing ties either table to the golden directory, unlike `golden_recovery::every_golden_has_a_readme_line`.
- A black-box probe shows the verdict itself is right today: `refuse` / `impossible_header` at offset 347.

**Folded in: both reviewers raised it as P3.** The schema's enums are hand-maintained, and no test syncs them with the Rust enums (`schemas/cli/doctor.v1.schema.json` vs `RefusalCode`, `ShapeReport`, `Conclusion`, `LockState` and `BindingState` in `crates/cli/src/doctor.rs`).
- No CLI test emits these codes: `not_an_interrupted_init`, `impossible_header`, `not_genesis`, `genesis_record`, `record`, `storage`.
- No CLI test emits the shape `stale`.
- So a serde rename, or a new variant, would pass every test while breaking the published schema (O-6).

## Requirements
O-7, O-6, §10.15 (claims match their evidence), §12.2 W23 acceptance.

## Area
journal (`examine_tests.rs`), cli (`tests/doctor.rs`).

## Acceptance
- Both tables include `impossible-version-final`. In the CLI table that's `"refuse", Some("impossible_header")`.
- Each test asserts that every `*.bin` under `golden/recovery/` appears in its table, so a new golden fails until it is added.
- A test serialises every variant of the five report enums and asserts set equality with the schema's enum arrays. Precedent: `xtask/src/schemas.rs` `assert_enum`.
- JOURNAL-EXAMINE and DOCTOR-CLI pass, with `min_cases` raised if tests are added.

## Out of scope
The other W23 review beads.

title: raft_adapter: peer-decoder no-panic evidence is thinner than claimed; raw-byte and codec-level unknown-field cases missing
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9. Both reviewers raised it as P3, so it is filed.

**The no-panic evidence for the peer decoder is thinner than its claim.**

**Evidence:**
- `envelope_tests.rs:375-388`: the 5,000 random inputs are under 200 bytes and almost never pass the 4-byte magic (probability about 2⁻³² each). So the protobuf decoder sees only about 80 single-byte mutations of one heartbeat.
- The PEER-ENVELOPE row cites §10.19 in claim class Invariant, but the no-panic property belongs to W53's fuzz target.
- Missing cheap raw-byte cases:
  - a known field with the wrong wire type (e.g. `to` as `12 01 01`);
  - an unknown `EntryType` value;
  - a payload truncated mid-varint.
- Opus also noted: H-3 (spike/raft-audit.md:160-163) owes "a codec test with an unknown field present → dropped and counted". The unknown-field cases run only through `admit`, which counts nothing, and `PeerCodec` counts it under `message`.

## Requirements
§10.15 (claims in their class), §10.19, W02 audit H-3, P10.

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (envelope_tests.rs, admit_tests.rs); the PEER-ENVELOPE row's summary (a facade turn).

## Acceptance
- Random and mutated payloads are generated under a valid sealed header, so they reach the decoder.
- The raw-byte cases above are added.
- A PeerCodec-level unknown-field case asserts `DropCounts.message`, and H-3's wording is aligned with the counter.
- The PEER-ENVELOPE summary claims what the tests show, and leaves fuzzing to W53.

## Out of scope
cargo-fuzz (W53).

title: BUG: SERVER-RESTART flakes under load: a restarted test server's port can be taken by another test during the restart gap (cross-talk)
description:
## Context
PeachAnchor's private gate on 2df10de plus their W17.2 paths (tree 2b5c6c87; artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261004T111355Z-2b5c6c87f053-1532670/tests.log lines 2622-2645) failed 2 of 3 SERVER-RESTART cases under load. Run alone, the tests passed 3 of 3. GoldenHorizon diagnosed it and I confirmed it in the code.
- every_acknowledged_write...: 'read: Connection reset by peer' at tests/support/mod.rs:120.
- a_sigkill_mid_burst...: the retry of w0-0 (request 00000001...) got 409 request_id_conflict, original_index 2, on 127.0.0.1:41111.

**Cause:** free_port() (tests/support/mod.rs) binds 127.0.0.1:0, drops the listener and returns the number. That is a check-then-use race in Linux's ephemeral range (32768-60999). The restart tests widen it: after the SIGKILL the port is free until the restart binds it again. A parallel test's free_port(), an outgoing socket, or another gate's test can take it. The test's client then talks to another test's server; every test uses request IDs from 00000001..., so a fresh ID conflicts. A client reaching a server that another test killed gets ECONNRESET.

## Requirements
T0 determinism of a registered check (P10/P4 spirit; a red-gate flake is P0); rule 18 (a test must only ever talk to the node it started).

## Area
crates/server/tests/** (support/node.rs, support/mod.rs, binary.rs restart_tests).

## Acceptance
- Restart tests take their ports outside the ephemeral range, from a per-process counter with a pid-derived base, probed free. A bind to port 0 or an outgoing socket can never take one during the restart gap.
- Each restart test's node has a unique cluster_id, and the harness checks it on /v1/cluster at every wait. Cross-talk then fails loudly, naming both identities, never as a data assertion.
- The restart tests stay green under parallel load: the binary target runs alongside concurrent server-package runs at least 30 times with 0 failures. ./dev check SERVER-RESTART passes; T0 green.

## Out of scope
The in-process serve_tests (no restart gap) and cli_tests' single run test.

comments.author: SunnyDog
comments.text: Accept receipt: artifacts/receipts/accept-br-p9fm-1df3145e72a3-20261004T112737Z-1750104.json, ok=true, on work tree 1df3145e (commit 495210b). Selector: ./dev check SERVER-RESTART passed. The wrapper's gate passed on its first run (gate-fast-20261004T112416Z-1df3145e72a3-1702303.json). Root cause, from PeachAnchor's failing gate's scratch dirs: free_port() handed 127.0.0.1:41111 to two parallel tests; one server failed with 'Address already in use' and its test talked to the other's node. Fix: per-process port counter below the ephemeral range, probed free, plus a cluster_id identity check at every wait. Evidence (test class): a shared-port mutant fails loudly with 'answers as another cluster'; a stress run of 120 concurrent test processes (40 with the restart tests) had 0 failures. The original collision wasn't reproduced locally (32 concurrent HEAD runs passed); the failing gate's dirs show it directly.

title: model: DM-7 history accounting (committed entries and command bytes) so DIFFERENTIAL and the model server cover history_full
description:
## Context
Two independent reviews raised this: JadeOx's review of W10.1 (P3 #3) and a W10.3 reviewer (P3). The reference model (`crates/model`) keeps no DM-7 history accounting: no count of committed entries against `max_log_entries`, and no committed-command-bytes counter against `max_history_bytes`. The state machine keeps the bytes counter (`StateMachine::committed_command_bytes`, §7.5) and admission refuses with `507 history_full` (§8.4, W29.3).

Consequences:
- The W10.3 differential test (DIFFERENTIAL) cannot compare `committed_command_bytes`, because the model has nothing to compare it with.
- The reference model server (W30) cannot answer `history_full`. Every operation in the spec is meant to be implemented there.
- The byte half depends on the canonical command encoding's length (§7.5, codec v1). The plan describes that encoding only through `crates/statemachine/src/codec.rs`. An independent model would need the length rule written into the plan, or would have to take it as data.

## Requirements
DM-7, T-7, §10.14, §8.4 (`history_full`), W30.

## Area
`crates/model` (an oracle; no production dependency, T-12). Possibly a plan note on how the canonical command length is defined (owner).

## Acceptance
- The model tracks committed entries and committed command bytes, as DM-7 defines them, and refuses admission as §8.4 says.
- DIFFERENTIAL (or a W29.3 extension of it) compares the counters with the state machine's.
- If the plan doesn't define the byte length independently, a `plan-change` question goes to the owner first.

## Out of scope
The production admission path (W29.3).

comments.author: PeachAnchor
comments.text:
## Decision: split into an entry half now and a byte half later (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04 ~06:10Z)

PLAN.md §7.5 says only that commands have "one canonical, versioned byte encoding". The v1 layout is defined only in `crates/statemachine/src/codec.rs`, so the model can't compute DM-7's byte counter independently from the plan. As this bead's acceptance requires, the question went to the owner first, as a dialog relayed by cc_1 overnight. cc_1 adopted the recommendation, which is logged here for the owner:

1. **Plan change (owner): br-camk.** It proposes codec.rs's v1 table as normative text in §7.5, or at least its length rule, plus a §16 decision row. This bead now depends on br-camk, for its byte half.
2. **Entry half, now, under this bead.** It is fully defined by the plan:
   - `model::HistoryLimits` (`max_log_entries`, default 1,000,000, 0 refused);
   - `Model::admit`, which refuses once the commit index (the model's applied index; empty entries count) reaches `max_log_entries`. It changes nothing, and apply never refuses, so the ceiling is soft;
   - the model server answers `507 history_full` with `{request_id, limit: "max_log_entries", attempt_state: "not_submitted"}`, in F-7's order: after validation and the history's short-circuit, and before the append;
   - `model-server --max-log-entries N`.
   - The work commit carries `Bead: br-q37e`. The bead stays open.
3. **Byte half, after br-camk.**
   - `HistoryLimits` gains `max_history_bytes`, and the model counts first-execution command bytes by the plan's rule.
   - `HistoryLimit` gains `MaxHistoryBytes`.
   - DIFFERENTIAL compares the counter with `StateMachine::committed_command_bytes`, and this bead gains `accept:DIFFERENTIAL`.
   - Then this bead closes.

Rejected:
- computing the length from codec.rs's doc now, because the oracle's spec would come from the implementation until the owner ratified it;
- taking the length as data, because the model server could not compute it;
- deferring all of q37e.

comments.author: PeachAnchor
comments.text:
## Entry half landed (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04 06:35Z)

**Work:** fd4bd2b, tree 05e88aed, on cf52cd4. The wrapper's gate passed on the first attempt (`artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261004T063351Z-05e88aed4b43-857809.json`). The private gate before it passed on 038f97dc, the same paths on 9538df4.

**What landed:**
- `HistoryLimits` (`max_log_entries`, 1 to 2^53 − 1).
- `Model::admit` and `HistoryLimit`.
- The model server's `507 history_full`, in F-7's order, plus `--max-log-entries`.
- MODEL 32 → 34 and MODEL-SERVER 27 → 29.

**Review:** Opus and Fable, no P1. Their shared P2 (stale module docs) and the P3s both raised (the ceiling's upper bound, the tie-break, a long summary line) are fixed. The tie-break question is now on br-camk.

**Still open:** the byte half, after br-camk. This bead isn't accepted or closed yet. Its `accept:MODEL` and `accept:MODEL-SERVER` labels pass on this tree's checks, and `accept:DIFFERENTIAL` comes with the byte half.

title: node: emit LogEvent::RoleChanged when the library's role, term or believed leader changes, so node logs record elections (O-3)
description:
Context: found by SunnyDog while wiring the production log (W18.2, br-w18-2-production-wiring-l8v).
- O-3 requires each node's structured log to include role changes and elections. The core owns that event, `types::LogEvent::RoleChanged { role, term, leader }`, which the types define.
- Nothing in `crates/node` or `crates/raft_adapter` emits it: grep finds no producer. The controller already detects exactly this change in `observe_status`, comparing `StatusKey`'s role, term and leader, and hands it to the request lifecycle. It doesn't log it.
- So a production node's JSON-lines log carries boot, lifecycle changes, `applied` observations and stop, but no role change or election. The simulator's trace (W36) will want the same event.
- The roots only translate (CD-1), so deriving the event in each root would duplicate core logic.

Requirements: O-3 (role changes, elections), §7.2 (Telemetry port: `Log(event)`), CD-1.

Area: crates/node (controller.rs `observe_status`, controller_tests.rs). If the case count changes: NODE-CONTROLLER's min_cases in xtask/src/check.rs + registry/checks.toml, under a short shared reservation.

Acceptance:
- whenever the library's role, term or believed leader changes, the controller emits `Effect::Log(LogEvent::RoleChanged { role, term, leader })`, once per observed change and in effect order;
- a controller test drives an election through inputs (a one-voter start, and a three-voter election with a leader change) and asserts the records;
- `./dev check NODE-CONTROLLER` passes; T0 green.

Then the production log (crates/server `logs.rs`, W18.2) writes them as `role_changed` records with no change on its side. Its test can assert them once this lands.

Out of scope: `Observation::Responded` (the sim trace's, W36); log formats.

title: BUG: a journal read failure in raft_adapter's storage view panics through raft's fatal! with no cause, instead of failing the node (CD-6, §7.11)
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.1 (raft_adapter, e1427a8, closed 3cbaf2d) that cc_1 asked for, 2026-10-04: SunnyDog plus an independent fresh reviewer, every finding verified by hand against the vendored raft-rs 0.7.0. Thread: br-w13-1-consensus-port-construction-3wc.

`JournalStorage::entries` (crates/raft_adapter/src/storage.rs:84-86) maps every `JournalError` from a cache-miss read-back (an I/O failure, a short read, a damaged frame or record, an entry mismatch) to `raft::Error::Store(StorageError::Unavailable)`. `RaftLog::slice` (vendor/raft/raft/src/raft_log.rs:599) treats `Unavailable` as `fatal!`, which is a panic. The message does not name the node, the index or the journal error.

The doc comment at storage.rs:71-72 says "the node fails (§7.11)". But §7.11 means the `failed` lifecycle state: "An unexpected I/O error stops writes on that node and moves it to `failed`, visible in health." CD-6 makes I/O errors result values, so in simulation an injected read failure would be a false failing seed.

## Requirements
CD-6, CD-7, §7.11 (an unexpected I/O error → `failed`), types::StorageError::Failed's doc ("The node moves to `failed`").

## Area
raft_adapter (storage.rs, node.rs); possibly the Consensus port in types if `failed` must be surfaced.

## Acceptance
- A storage-view read failure never panics without its cause.
  - **Preferred:** the adapter records the failure (with the JournalError, node and index) and surfaces it, so the node moves to `failed` without stepping the library further. For example, return `LogTemporarilyUnavailable` where raft-rs tolerates it, and refuse further input.
  - **At minimum, with an owner-approved `conflict` bead recording the deviation from §7.11:** a named `invariant!` (for example RA-STORAGE-READ) carrying the node, the index and the error.
- A test injects a read failure through a failing `JournalRead` and shows the chosen outcome.
- RAFT-ADAPTER passes.

## Out of scope
Write-side failures (`StorageFailed` inputs, W13.2/W14).

comments.author: VioletOwl
comments.text: Fixed in 81289f2 (VioletOwl). Design asked as a dialog overnight; cc_1 took the Recommended option (logged for the owner): the acceptance's PREFERRED outcome, implemented as record + short read, with no plan deviation and no conflict bead needed. JournalStorage::entries now ends its list at the first failed journal read and records it as ReadFailure { index, error }. raft-rs's slice() accepts a short read like a size-capped one (vendor raft_log.rs:609), so the library never panics and never sees wrong data. RaftNode::storage_failure() exposes the failure. ReadyLoop checks after every library call (the input, each ready(), advance(), the applied report) and stops with LoopError::StorageFailed(ReadFailure), persisting, sending and applying nothing more; the node moves to failed (§7.11, W14's lifecycle). Tests: storage::tests (RAFT-ADAPTER, 23) and ready_loop_tests::a_failed_journal_read_stops_the_loop_with_its_cause (RAFT-READY-LOOP, 13), both through a failing JournalRead (test Journal::fail_reads). Accept receipt (rule 16): ./dev accept on work tree 1983800b (commit 81289f2) passed, with RAFT-ADAPTER at 23 cases and RAFT-READY-LOOP at 13 (class invariant). Receipt: artifacts/receipts/accept-br-qxao-1983800bbea9-20261004T040020Z-1996904.json

title: BUG: deleting or demoting a registered check passes the registry gate (forward-only D-56, §10.6 removal)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, cross-checked by the Fable reviewer, verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e).

The REGISTRY gate never compares `registry/checks.toml` with the committed version at HEAD. So it can't see a check being **removed** or **moved backwards**:
- `xtask/src/registry_gate.rs:137-156`, `212-230`: the gate reads only the working copy.
- `registry_gate.rs:509-513`, `537`: planned rows skip conditions 3 and 4.
- W05.2's acceptance (closed) listed "Fixtures cover … backwards check-status transitions"; no such fixture exists.

**Scenario today.** One commit deletes a check completely:
- its `CATALOGUE` entry;
- its `checks.toml` row;
- its `// check: <ID>` marker;
- its tests.

The example is K-14 (`eae350c`). Its requirements (T-3, T-11) are still covered by other implemented checks, so condition 2 holds, and REGISTRY plus REGISTRY-FILES both pass. An oracle disappears without any failure.

**Scenario once W05.4 lands.** Today a demotion to `planned` is caught only incidentally: REGISTRY-FILES (`xtask/src/registry.rs:556-593`) forbids every non-`implemented` row. W05.4 stages T0 from `checks.toml` and needs `planned` rows, so that incidental guard has to go. From then on, demoting a failing check to `planned` would drop it from T0 silently.

## Requirements
- §10.13: "moving a check backwards, or an `implemented` selector that no longer resolves, fails the gate unless an owner-approved `plan-change` covers it".
- §10.6: "Requirement manifests, … are protected: removal, skipping or silent reclassification fails the gate".
- D-56.
- §11.5 rules 3 and 12: "Never delete registry rows … to make a gate pass".

## Overlap
**br-2q2o (W05.4, GoldenHorizon, in progress)** already owns "a row moved backwards from implemented to planned fails unless an owner-approved plan-change covers it". This bead adds **row removal**, which needs the same comparison against HEAD, plus the fixture W05.2 promised. GoldenHorizon may fold this into W05.4 and close this bead as a duplicate with a note.

## Area
xtask (`registry_gate.rs`, `registry.rs`), with fixtures.

## Acceptance
- REGISTRY fails when a `checks.toml` row present at HEAD is missing from the tree under test, or moved from `implemented` to `planned`, unless an owner-approved `plan-change` covers it.
- Fixtures for both cases; condition 4's unresolved-selector case still fails.
- `./dev gate fast` passes on the real registry.

## Out of scope
T1–T3 staging (W46).

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: GoldenHorizon: folded into W05.4 (br-2q2o). This is cc_1's relay, confirmed with the owner via dialog at about 00:40Z 2026-10-04. The gate's new forward-only step compares the candidate's registry/checks.toml with the parent commit's (./dev commit hands it over). Two moves fail the gate: removing a row, and marking an implemented row anything else. The only exception is ./dev commit --allow-demotion <CHECK-ID>=<bead> naming a closed plan-change bead in the committed tracker export (owner decision: flag + closed plan-change bead). A deleted check (row, catalogue entry, marker and tests) therefore fails T0 even when its requirements are covered elsewhere. Fixtures: staging::tests::removing_a_row_or_demoting_an_implemented_one_is_a_demotion, only_a_closed_plan_change_bead_approves_a_demotion, an_allowance_that_covers_no_demotion_fails, and gate::tests::registry_forward_only_refuses_a_removed_check_unless_a_closed_plan_change_allows_it, all in GATE-STAGING. The W05.4 commit carries Bead: lines for this bead and W05.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: Closure evidence (GoldenHorizon). Fixed in 497e738 (W05.4, tree 63a1bdc5), which carries Bead: br-registry-check-removal-passes-kdo9. Accept receipt artifacts/receipts/accept-br-registry-check-removal-passes-kdo9-63a1bdc533d0-20261004T012939Z-3187672.json passed: GATE-STAGING 12, invariant check, test-class evidence. Since 497e738, removing any checks.toml row, or marking an implemented row anything else, fails gate fast's forward-only step unless ./dev commit --allow-demotion <ID>=<closed plan-change bead> approves it. The wrapper hands the gate the parent commit's checks.toml. The commit that landed it was itself judged that way (forward-only over 44 parent rows).

title: BUG: the §7.10/§7.11 send-queue rule admits configs whose catch-up bursts are dropped (one entry larger than the queue; message count unchecked; no overhead room)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e).

The code implements the plan's rule exactly. The **rule itself** is too weak to deliver what the plan promises, and §7.10/§7.11 are normative (§0.5), so the fix needs an owner decision. Hence `plan-change` and `needs-owner`.

**Evidence:**
- `crates/types/src/config/rules.rs:186-204` (`replication_fits`) checks only `replication_inflight_batches × replication_batch_bytes ≤ peer_send_queue_bytes`. That is exactly §7.11's wording.
- Ranges (`crates/types/src/config/params.rs:265-268`): batch up to 256 KiB, in-flight up to 16, queue up to 64 messages and 8 MiB. Each has a low minimum.
- raft-rs always sends at least one entry, whatever `max_size_per_msg` says (`vendor/raft/raft/src/util.rs:52-75`).

**Gaps.** Each is an accepted config whose catch-up bursts *are* dropped.
- **(a) One entry can exceed the whole queue.** Take the default limits plus `replication_batch_bytes = 1024` and `peer_send_queue_bytes = 16384` (16 × 1024; uncommitted 4 MiB ≥ 1024). The config is accepted. A PUT of a 64 KiB value becomes one ~66 KiB `MsgAppend`, larger than the 16 KiB queue. It is dropped on every retransmission; the entry never commits, and everything after it stalls. If the W13 adapter asserts output bounds against `max_size_per_msg`, it hits an invariant panic instead.
- **(b) Message counts are never compared.** `peer_send_queue_messages = 4` with 16 in-flight batches is accepted, and a 16-message burst is dropped.
- **(c) Equality leaves no room for overhead.** `config/fixtures/small-limits.toml:23-26` sits exactly at 1 × 1024 = 1024 bytes, with a 1-message queue. A full batch plus its protobuf and peer-envelope overhead (including the 32-byte fingerprint) exceeds 1024 bytes. Note that `small-limits.toml` works today only because its key and value limits are tiny.

## Requirements
- §7.11 per-peer send queue row: "Drop and count as a network failure; never grow. Config validation requires in-flight batches × max batch size ≤ queue bytes (§7.10), so ordinary catch-up bursts are never dropped".
- O-5: inconsistent values are rejected at startup.
- §7.10: "a config the parser accepts can never fail at `RawNode` construction". A config that is accepted but stalls replication is the runtime analogue.

## Area
PLAN.md §7.10/§7.11 (owner) first; then types (`config/rules.rs`, `params.rs`), the fixtures, and possibly the W21 queue accounting.

## Acceptance (once the owner decides)
- The parser also requires each of the following, each as its own rule with its own test:
  - `peer_send_queue_bytes ≥` the largest single replication message (the max canonical command plus the envelope bound);
  - `peer_send_queue_messages ≥ replication_inflight_batches`;
  - a stated per-message overhead allowance in the byte comparison.
- `small-limits.toml` is adjusted or kept, as decided.
- Alternatively, the owner records that the W21 transport handles an oversized single message, for example by never queueing it past the bound.

## Out of scope
Changing the §7.11 default values.

comments.author: PeachAnchor
comments.text:
PROPOSAL FOR THE OWNER (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04, at cc_1's request; no code or PLAN.md changed). The status quo stays until the owner decides: the rule is exactly §7.10's, and that rule is too weak (see the description).

## Facts the proposal rests on (verified at HEAD 6954eda)
- raft-rs 0.7 `util::limit_size` (vendor/raft/raft/src/util.rs:52-75) always keeps the first entry. One MsgAppend's entries total at most **max(max_size_per_msg, the first entry's encoded size)**. `max_size_per_msg` is `replication_batch_bytes`.
- Each entry inside a Message adds protobuf framing (1 B tag plus a 1-3 B length varint below 2 MiB) that `limit_size` does not count. A Raft entry is at least 4 B (term and index fields), so framing is at most 50% of the counted bytes (2 B on a 4 B entry; at most 3 B for entries of 128 B and over; 4 B at 16 KiB and over).
- Each queued message also carries the Raft message header (type, to, from, term, log_term, index, commit, …) and the §8.2 peer envelope (16 B instance ID, protocol version, 32 B fingerprint, two node IDs, length prefixes).

## Proposed definitions (new named constants, pinned by codec tests)
- `RAFT_ENTRY_OVERHEAD_BOUND` = 32 B: an Entry's fields besides its data (term, index, type, data length). W13 proves it, as W09 proves `COMMAND_ENVELOPE_BOUND`.
- `PEER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_BOUND` = 256 B: the Raft message header plus the §8.2 envelope. W13 and W21 prove it.
- largest_entry = `max_key_bytes` + `max_value_bytes` + `COMMAND_ENVELOPE_BOUND` + `RAFT_ENTRY_OVERHEAD_BOUND`.
- message_payload = max(`replication_batch_bytes`, largest_entry).
- message_bound = ⌈3/2 × message_payload⌉ + `PEER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_BOUND`. The 3/2 covers per-entry framing.

## Proposed rules (§7.10 cross-limit list, each its own parser rule, error and test)
1. **One message fits:** `peer_send_queue_bytes` ≥ message_bound (gap a). Rule 3 implies it, because in-flight batches are at least 1. It stays its own rule, in the house style of rules.rs ("each rule is its own function … even where the ranges already make it unreachable from a file"). It also gives a clearer error.
2. **Message counts fit:** `peer_send_queue_messages` ≥ `replication_inflight_batches` (gap b).
3. **A full burst fits, with overhead:** `replication_inflight_batches` × message_bound ≤ `peer_send_queue_bytes` (gaps a and c). This replaces today's `in-flight × batch ≤ queue bytes`.

## Proposed PLAN.md text (v1.11)
- **§7.10**, the cross-limit bullet. Replace "replication in-flight batches × max batch size must be ≤ per-peer send-queue bytes (§7.11);" with:

  "the per-peer send queue must hold a full catch-up burst (§7.11). Let one replication message's bound be ⌈3/2 × max(max batch size, the largest single entry)⌉ + `peer_message_overhead_bound`, where the largest entry is `max_key_bytes` + `max_value_bytes` + command-envelope overhead + `raft_entry_overhead_bound`. The consensus library always sends at least one entry, and the 3/2 covers per-entry framing. Send-queue bytes must be ≥ one message's bound; send-queue messages must be ≥ in-flight batches; and in-flight batches × one message's bound must be ≤ send-queue bytes;"
- **§7.11**, the per-peer send queue row. Replace "Config validation requires in-flight batches × max batch size ≤ queue bytes (§7.10)" with:

  "Config validation requires the queue to hold a full catch-up burst: in-flight batches messages, each up to one replication message's bound (§7.10)."
- **§7.11:** add the two named constants (`raft_entry_overhead_bound` 32 B, `peer_message_overhead_bound` 256 B) next to `journal_protocol_allowance`. Their sizes are derived from the codecs and pinned by tests.
- **§16:** a D-row recording the decision. I can draft its text if wanted.

## Impact, computed
- **Defaults, `local.toml`, and `five-voters-explicit-limits.toml`** (256 KiB × 16, 64 messages, 8 MiB), all accepted:
  - largest_entry = 256 + 65536 + 1024 + 32 = 66848; message_payload = 262144;
  - message_bound = 393216 + 256 = 393472;
  - 16 × 393472 = 6295552 ≤ 8388608; 64 ≥ 16.
- **Range maxima** (batch 256 KiB, in-flight 16, queue 8 MiB) are still accepted, so **no §7.10 range changes**.
- **`small-limits.toml`** is now refused: largest_entry = 16 + 64 + 1024 + 32 = 1136 > the 1024 batch, so message_bound = 1704 + 256 = 1960 > its 1024 queue bytes. Proposal: set `peer_send_queue_bytes = 1960`, which keeps it "exactly on the boundary" as its header says, and update that comment. Messages 1 ≥ in-flight 1 already holds.
- **`one-voter`, `three-voters`, `fastest-timing`:** §7.11 defaults; unaffected.
- **Bead (a)'s example** (defaults with batch 1024 and queue 16384) is now refused by rule 3: 16 × (⌈1.5 × 66848⌉ + 256) = 1608448 > 16384. Each part of it is caught.

## Implementation once approved (one bead, types and fixtures only)
- `params.rs`: the two constants.
- `limits.rs`: registry rows for them.
- `rules.rs`: `message_fits`, `queue_counts_fit` and the strengthened `replication_fits`, in that order.
- `error.rs`: two new ConfigError variants with line-free messages, like the existing cross-limit errors.
- `tests.rs`: N-1/N/N+1 boundary tests per rule, including bead (a)'s case.
- `small-limits.toml` as above.
- **W13 / W21 obligations:** a test that the encoded Raft message header plus envelope is ≤ 256 B, and an entry's non-data fields are ≤ 32 B.

## For the owner to decide
1. Approve rules 1-3 and the text above, or the bead's alternative: W21 never queues an oversized single message past the bound. I don't recommend that alternative, because a dropped oversized append is retransmitted and dropped forever, so the entry never commits.
2. Should rule 2 reserve room for control messages (heartbeats, votes), e.g. `≥ in-flight + 4`? **Recommendation: no.** They are small, the library resends them, and a drop is counted as a network failure. The §7.11 promise is about catch-up appends.
3. The 3/2 framing factor versus an adapter-side encoded-size cap. **Recommendation: 3/2.** It is sound from the protobuf layout, needs no adapter logic, and the defaults keep 25% headroom.

title: BUG: without --config the doctor says init may re-run on a journal that held data; with no LOCK file it reads unguarded; storage errors lose their cause
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W23 (keyval doctor), 2026-10-04, at frozen tree e653520. Two independent reviewers looked at it: Opus rated it P1, Fable P3. JadeOx verified the mechanism by hand and triaged it **P2**. The verdict is still `refuse`; what is wrong is the `init` advice. The backstop is that `keyval-server init` runs with a config and would refuse. Two P3s both reviewers raised are folded in.

**Without `--config`, the doctor says "`init` may (re-)run" on a journal that held data, and startup would never re-initialise it.**
- **Code path:**
  - `journal::recovery::scan` (`recovery.rs`, about lines 559-571) tells `NotAnInterruptedInit` from `IncompleteGenesis` only through `genesis_frame_len(config, node)`. With no binding it always returns `IncompleteGenesis`, so `permits_init()` is true.
  - `Report::examined` (`crates/cli/src/doctor.rs`, about lines 349-358) prints "`init` may (re-)run on it" and `"init_allowed": true`.
  - `examine.rs`'s docs say only the binding goes unchecked without a config, so the doc is wrong too.
- **Probes:** each was run without a config and then with `--config config/local.toml --node 1`.
  - A 4096-byte zero-filled `journal.log`: `incomplete_genesis`, `init_allowed: true`, with the text "the journal holds no complete genesis and nothing after it", then `not_an_interrupted_init` ("never re-initialised").
  - A genesis frame plus 2 batch frames (3 entries, a vote, commit 2), with the first byte of each frame damaged: same split.
  - 347 zero bytes: same split.
- Plain `keyval doctor <dir>`, the default invocation, tells an operator a journal that held a vote and committed entries may be re-initialised. That would be Raft amnesia if acted on by hand.
- O-7: the doctor "reports what startup recovery would do", and startup always has the config.

**Folded in, P3, raised by both reviewers:**
1. **No LOCK file means no exclusion.**
   - Where: `doctor.rs` (about lines 427-443) and `fs_storage` `ReadOnlyDir::probe_lock`.
   - With `LockProbe::NoLockFile`, the doctor reads without holding anything. The module doc's "a free lock is held while the doctor reads, so no node starts meanwhile" does not hold on this path.
   - First sequence: a node starts meanwhile (it creates LOCK and appends). Its half-written frame N+1 reads as torn, and a later valid N+2 then gives a false `corruption` refusal.
   - Second sequence: a live node whose LOCK was deleted is examined as not live. Probe: "discard the 44-byte incomplete final frame … then start", exit 0, on a live directory.
   - `LockState::NoLockFile`'s doc ("no process ever took the directory's lock") can't be known.
2. **A storage error is reported as `refuse` with no OS cause.**
   - Where: `RecoveryError::Storage` is mapped to `Conclusion::Refuse` with "journal read: storage I/O failed", and `handle.last_failure()` is ignored.
   - Probe: `journal.log` is a directory (EISDIR); the cause is lost. The same happens on EIO.
   - An unreadable directory is `unreadable` elsewhere.

## Requirements
O-7, DUR-6, DUR-8, §7.7 step 0 (re-init only while the journal holds no complete genesis and nothing after it).

## Area
journal (`recovery.rs`, `examine.rs` docs), cli (`src/doctor.rs`), fs_storage (`ReadOnlyDir` docs or probe).

## Acceptance
- **Without a config, the doctor never reports `init_allowed: true` for a journal longer than any possible genesis frame.** For example, use a config-independent maximum: §7.10 bounds `cluster_id` and the voter set, which gives about 387 bytes; the Opus reviewer computed 101 to 387 bytes. Report `not_an_interrupted_init` above it, `incomplete_genesis` at or below the minimum, and in between `init_allowed: null`, meaning rerun with `--config`/`--node`. The schema must allow that.
- A test for each probe above, with and without a config, asserts the code, `init_allowed` and the text.
- **`NoLockFile`:** the doctor re-probes after the scan. If a LOCK now exists, or the journal's length or mtime changed, it concludes `live` or "changed while reading", never a verdict on bytes that moved. It also flags "journal present but no LOCK file". The docs are corrected.
- **`RecoveryError::Storage`** maps to `unreadable`, with `last_failure()`'s op, path and cause. A test covers it, for example `journal.log` being a directory.
- JOURNAL-EXAMINE, FS-DOCTOR and DOCTOR-CLI pass, with `min_cases` raised to match.

## Out of scope
`keyval-server init`'s own guard (W18/W22). This bead fixes the doctor's report.
