title: The inbound bound is applied twice: the production hand-off and the core queue each hold controller_queue_inputs, and busy is decided in both
description:
## Context
JadeOx's read-only review of W18.2 (1a120d4) at HEAD 5febcdb, for cc_1. Verified at HEAD in `crates/server/src/inbox.rs`, `runtime.rs` and `crates/node/src/controller.rs:248,265`.

**The inbound bound is applied twice, so up to 2 × `controller_queue_inputs` are buffered, and `busy` is decided in two places.**

§7.11 sets one "Inbound controller queue" of 1,024 inputs. §7.12 says client attempts and peer messages reach the controller "through one bounded input queue".
- The production hand-off (`Inbox`) bounds its inputs lane at `controller_queue_inputs` (1,024) and refuses past it. `Node::client` maps the refusal to `Busy`, and `Node::peer` drops and counts.
- The core's own `InboundQueue` (`controller.rs:265`) has the same bound, `Limit::ControllerQueueInputs`.
- The controller takes the whole inbox each wake and admits it into the core queue.

So while a sync is outstanding, peers wait in the core queue (1,024) and another 1,024 can wait in the hand-off: twice the registered bound. Peer envelopes can be large, so the memory bound is twice what §7.10's margins assume.

Admission is also decided by the adapter. Busy refusals and peer drops are counted in the root's `Snapshot` and in the core's `Counters`, separately (against CD-1 "adapters only translate", and §7.11's single counted bound).

## Requirements
§7.11 (one inbound bound of 1,024), §7.12 (one bounded input queue), CD-1, CD-9 (the registered bound is the real bound).

## Area
`crates/server` (`inbox.rs`, `runtime.rs`).

## Acceptance
- Client attempts and peer messages pass through at most one bound of `controller_queue_inputs` end to end. One way: size the hand-off by what the core queue can still take, or make the hand-off the only queue and let the core judge each input as it arrives. Busy and drop decisions then have one source, counted once.
- A test fills the node while a sync is outstanding and shows no more than `controller_queue_inputs` client attempts and peer messages are held at once.
- `./dev check SERVER-RUNTIME` passes; T0 green.

## Out of scope
The unrefusable (completions) and tick lanes, which are right as they are.

title: journal log: CD-7 assertions for commit <= last index and the cache bound; a named bound for the offset index (CD-9)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W11.2 and W11.3 by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7beeb19. Both reviewers raised overlapping P3s (Fable: the offset index has no named bound or CD-7 assertion; Opus: stated invariants are not asserted), and I verified them by hand. It's filed because both raised it. Memory and assertion hygiene, not correctness today.

**Evidence:**
- `crates/journal/src/log.rs:360`: `positions: Vec<Position>`, the offset index, is bounded only transitively by `max_journal_bytes`. At about 58 B per no-op frame, that is roughly 74 M positions, about 1.2 GB, at the 4 GiB default.
  - §7.6 says the index is "bounded by DM-7", but DM-7 bounds the commit index through admission and never refuses no-ops.
  - CD-9 wants a named maximum in the limits registry (`types::Limit`); CD-7 wants it asserted.
- `apply` asserts only `JOURNAL-TERM-IN-FORCE` (`log.rs:501-508`). The stated invariants "commit ≤ last index" (`log.rs:354`) and "cache bytes ≤ limit" (`log.rs:254`) are never asserted where state changes.

## Requirements
CD-7 (assert invariants where state changes), CD-9 (every queue, map or cache has a registered bound), §7.6 (offset index), §7.11.

## Area
crates/journal (`log.rs`); maybe a `types::Limit` entry, coordinated with its owner.

## Acceptance
- `invariant!` assertions for commit ≤ last index and the cache's byte bound, at the points that change them, each with a corrupted-state fixture that fires it.
- The offset index's maximum is named, either through a registry entry or as a documented derivation from `max_journal_bytes`, with a test at the bound.
- JOURNAL-LOG passes.

## Out of scope
Changing DM-7.

title: K-14 can pass vacuously: empty or incomplete traces compare identical, and the comparison is line-based, not byte-for-byte
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W15.3 (eae350c), run by GoldenHorizon on 2026-10-04 at HEAD 4f26119 at cc_1's request. Two independent reviewers (Opus, Fable) both raised this, and I verified it by hand. **K-14 can pass when it should fail.** Severity P2 (both reviewers); filed at priority 1 because K-14 is the T0 determinism checker and W17 builds on it.

**Evidence (HEAD 4f26119):**
- `crates/sim/src/replay.rs:457-530` `fresh_processes` rejects only `seeds.is_empty() || processes < 2`. Two children that exit 0 and write empty (or event-less) traces compare `Identical`, with no divergence, and the report says byte-identical. The T0 test survives only because it separately cross-checks each file against an in-process run (`replay.rs:653-665`), which is outside the checker.
- An incomplete run leaves no mark in its canonical bytes: `Trace::canonical()` (`trace.rs:450-464`). Incompleteness exists only in the in-memory `is_complete()` (`trace.rs:401-405`, `433`), so two processes that both write the same truncated trace pass.
- `compare` is line-based (`trace.rs:521-523`, `str::lines`). A missing final newline, or `\r\n` against `\n`, is `Identical`, while §10.5 says K-14 compares "byte-for-byte".
- Repeated seeds are counted twice: `[s, s]` reports 2 seeds, though both write the same `trace_path` (`replay.rs:289-292`).
- Child output is buffered whole by `Command::output()` (`replay.rs:479-492`), and children have no timeout. Only the report's copy is cut (CD-9; the commit's "stderr is bounded" overstates it).
- The test fixture at `replay.rs:857` uses `n1@0`; the encoder writes `n1/0` (`trace.rs:131`).
- Untested claims: that `event()` resets the per-step record bound, that incompleteness is sticky across later steps, and `compare` on empty traces.

## Requirements
T-11, T-3, P10; §10.5 K-14 row ("byte-for-byte"); §10.7 ("compare event counts and complete canonical traces"); CD-9.

## Area
crates/sim (`replay.rs`, `trace.rs`).

## Acceptance
- `fresh_processes` returns a `ReplayError` for a trace with zero events, or one marked incomplete, or for repeated seeds.
- An incomplete trace carries a terminal marker in its canonical bytes.
- `compare` decides on exact bytes, so a final-newline difference is reported at its line.
- Child stdout and stderr are bounded, and children have a timeout.
- The fixture uses `n1/0`.
- There is a test for each of the above, plus the per-step reset and sticky incompleteness.
- `./dev check K-14` and SIM-TRACE pass with raised min_cases.

## Out of scope
Linking K-14 to W17's real slice (W17's own acceptance).

title: BUG: PLAN.md's 2^53 integer boundary disagrees between §8.1 ('below' vs 'above 2^53') and §7.10 (node IDs '≤ 2^53')
description:
## Context
PLAN.md gives three different boundaries at exactly 2^53 for API integers. A boundary conformance test (2^53 - 1 / 2^53 / 2^53 + 1) and W08's config parser must agree with the spec, so the plan needs one rule.

## The conflicting locations
1. §8.1 Integers: "all validated **below** 2^53" (so 2^53 itself is invalid; max = 2^53 - 1 = 9007199254740991, which is also JavaScript's Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER).
2. §8.1, same bullet: "a CAS `expected.version` **above** 2^53 is `invalid_request`" (read literally, this leaves 2^53 itself unaddressed rather than invalid).
3. §7.10 Config validation: "node IDs must be nonzero and **≤ 2^53** (R-22)" (so a node ID of exactly 2^53 is accepted at config parse, then reported in `served_by.node_id`, `/v1/cluster` and health, violating rule 1). W08's bead copies "≤ 2^53".

## What the spec does meanwhile
`api/openapi.yaml` (W03.1) follows the general §8.1 rule: every integer schema has `maximum: 9007199254740991`, and the conventions say a request integer at or above 2^53 is `400 invalid_request`. That is the reading where every reported integer is a safe JSON integer. If the owner picks "≤ 2^53" instead, the spec's maxima change to 9007199254740992.

## Requirements
§8.1, §7.10, R-22, F-5, O-5; W03, W08, W31 boundary tests.

## Area
PLAN.md (owner-owned): a plan-change to one wording, then api/openapi.yaml and W08 follow.

## Acceptance
The owner picks one boundary; §8.1 and §7.10 state it identically; api/openapi.yaml and W08's parser match it.

## Out of scope
Changing integer encoding (R-22 stays rejected).

title: BUG: the simulated disk's sync copies the whole journal every time, so a node's run is quadratic in its journal (11 s for 1,000 syncs of 64 KiB frames)
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W12.2 (5735d10, br-w12-2-sim-disk-oqq), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Verified at HEAD 86b3a65.

`DiskHandle::sync` (crates/sim/src/disk.rs:318-325) clones the **whole** volatile journal into `durable` on every sync:
```rust
let journal = state.volatile.clone().ok_or(StorageError::Missing)?;
state.keep = journal.len();
state.durable = journal;
```
Each sync therefore costs O(journal size). The core syncs once per persisted Ready (§7.4 step 3), so a node's run costs O(syncs × journal size): quadratic in its length. Every node also holds two full copies of its journal (volatile and durable), where the unsynced difference is at most one frame (§7.4: one append batch per Ready, ≤ 1 MiB).

**Evidence.** A scratch probe in my candidate copy of HEAD, never committed: one SimDisk, 64 KiB frames, each followed by a sync, in the test profile as `./dev` and the gate run it.
```
frames=250  journal=15 MiB  time=1.693s
frames=500  journal=31 MiB  time=5.111s
frames=1000 journal=62 MiB  time=11.343s
```
That's one node; a run has five, plus crashes and replays. A large-value workload (DM-2 allows 64 KiB values, and the §10.3 profiles must exercise the boundary) would spend most of a seed's time copying journals. §10.10's budgets (T0: about 50 small seeds within about 2 minutes; T1: 2,000 seeds within about 15 minutes) cannot absorb that, and §10.10 forbids dropping regression evidence to fit.

## Requirements
§10.2 (simulated disk: volatile and durable images), §10.10 (budgets), CD-9 (bounded resources).

## Area
sim/disk (`crates/sim/src/disk.rs`).

## Acceptance
- `sync` costs O(unsynced bytes): cut `durable` to `keep`, then append `volatile[keep..]`. Better still, keep one image plus the unsynced suffix and the pending truncation point, so a node never holds two full copies of its journal.
- The crash model's results are byte-identical for every seed: SIM-DISK's `the_same_seed_keeps_the_same_bytes` and the prefix/fill/truncation tests pass unchanged. Add a test that a long run of append+sync keeps `durable == volatile` after each sync.
- A test bounds the work. For example, assert that a sync after N frames copies at most the unsynced bytes: count the bytes moved through a test hook, or time-box a 1,000-frame run of 64 KiB frames well under the current 11 s.

## Out of scope
The crash model itself, which matches §10.2.

comments.author: SunnyDog
comments.text: Accepted on its work tree 08af7aa0 (commit 3e2006a): ./dev accept passed, SIM-DISK 8 cases, STORAGE-CONTRACT-SIM 11. Receipt: artifacts/receipts/accept-br-sim-disk-sync-copies-journal-c861-08af7aa08270-20261004T045802Z-2930084.json. Wrapper gate: gate-fast-20261004T045542Z-08af7aa08270-2893017.json. Claims by class. Test evidence: a sync writes exactly its unsynced bytes (counted by the durable image's write counter); durable == journal after every sync over 300 rounds; mutation pass 11/11 killed. Differential evidence (scratch test, not committed): 120,000 op results byte-identical to HEAD's disk over 2,000 seeded programs. Measurement: 1,000 syncs of 64 KiB frames, 13.262 s before vs 0.037 s after (test profile, same machine).

title: BUG: the sim scheduler's pending-event queue is unbounded (CD-9)
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W15.1 (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03). Both independent reviewers raised it at low confidence, and I verified it by hand. It is filed at P3 under the review protocol: a P3 is filed only when both reviewers raise it.

The scheduler's pending-event queue has no bound. `EventBudget` (1,000,000 dispatches) gates only `step()`.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01):**
- `crates/sim/src/scheduler.rs:167`: `queue: BTreeMap<Order, Pending<E>>`.
- `crates/sim/src/scheduler.rs:217-238`: `schedule()` always inserts, with no cap and no typed refusal.

Scenario: a fan-out bug, such as a runaway duplicator in a W16 fault scenario where every event schedules two more, grows the queue geometrically before the dispatch budget trips. The run then ends in out-of-memory instead of a typed `Incomplete` (P10).

## Requirements
CD-9 ("Every queue, map, buffer … has a named, configured maximum … Hitting it is a typed outcome, not silent growth"). §7.11 names only "Simulation events per run".

## Area
sim (`scheduler.rs`); a limits-table row if a new limit is added. PeachAnchor is extending `crates/sim` for W15.2, so coordinate.

## Acceptance

title: BUG: keyval doctor --json prints nothing on usage or config errors (O-6); adopt the suite's pre-parse --json error envelope
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W23 (keyval doctor), 2026-10-04, at frozen tree e653520. The Opus reviewer rated it P2 and the Fable reviewer P3; JadeOx verified it by hand and triaged it **P2**.

**`keyval doctor --json` prints nothing on stdout for usage errors or a bad `--config`/`--node`.**
- `crates/cli/src/main.rs` calls `Cli::parse()`, so clap's errors go to stderr as text and exit 2.
- The `binding()` failures (`--config nope.toml`, a config that does not parse, `--node 0`) also go to stderr as text and exit 2.
- With `--json`, a robot caller gets 0 bytes on stdout and no `schema` field. Probes: `keyval doctor --json` (missing argument), `--config nope.toml --node 1 --json`, `--node 0 --json`.

O-6: "Every tool (CLI, sim, ./dev commands, doctor, report generators) supports --json: machine-readable output with a versioned schema identifier". The suite already has a convention for exactly this case. `xtask/src/output.rs` `Format::detect` looks for `--json` before parsing, "so that even a usage error is reported in the format the caller asked for", as `keyval.dev.error/v1` (`schemas/dev/`). The CLI is the first non-xtask tool, and §8.7 says every `keyval` command takes `--json`, so it should follow the same convention from its first command.

## Requirements
O-6, §8.7, §11.13 (exit 2 = usage error).

## Area
cli (`src/main.rs`, plus a new error schema under `schemas/cli/`).

## Acceptance
- `--json` is detected before parsing, as `Format::detect` does it.
- A usage error, or a configuration or node error, under `--json` prints one JSON document, for example `{"schema":"keyval.cli.error/v1","error":{"kind":"usage"|"config","message":…}}`, and exits 2.
- The error schema lives at `schemas/cli/error.v1.schema.json`, and tests validate the real outputs against it.
- Without `--json`, the text and the exit code are unchanged.
- Tests cover a missing argument, `--config` without `--node`, an unreadable config, and `--node 0`.
- DOCTOR-CLI passes, with `min_cases` raised to match.

## Out of scope
Other `keyval` commands (W33). They should reuse the same envelope.

title: BUG: traceability reports requirements passed on evidence the judged tree does not support (case counts ignored; registry read from the working tree)
description:
## Context
Found in the second fresh-eyes review (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03; Opus reviewer, verified by hand at HEAD 1b2cf2e).

`./dev report traceability` can report a requirement **passed** when the judged tree's evidence doesn't support it, for two reasons.

**1. "Passed" ignores case counts.**
- `xtask/src/traceability.rs:407-416` (`parse_check_line`) parses `(N cases)` but nothing compares it to `min_cases`. `CheckRow` doesn't even read `min_cases`.
- `traceability.rs:494-500` counts a check as passed when its newest on-tree evidence has `outcome == "passed"`.
- Gate-receipt static steps don't check `min_cases` either (`xtask/src/gate.rs:649-668`).
- Scenario: `./dev accept` supports `--case` selectors (`accept.rs:137`). A run of `./dev check DEV-GATE --case isolation` writes `DEV-GATE passed (1 cases)`. DEV-GATE has `min_cases` 8, yet it counts as passed on that tree, and so do the requirements it covers.

**2. The registry comes from the working tree, but receipts are judged on another tree.**
- `traceability.rs:275-325` (`load`) reads `requirements.toml`, `checks.toml`, `workgraph.toml`, the tracker export and the registry-gate verdict from files under `root`.
- "Passed" is judged on `HEAD^{tree}`, or on `--tree <id>`.
- `registry.rs:54-56` states the project's own rule: read the registry from committed trees.
- Scenario: in the dirty shared checkout, an uncommitted edit drops a failing check from a requirement's `covers`. `--tree <T>` then reports the requirement passed on T, although at T it had a failing covering check.

## Requirements
- §10.13: a requirement is "passed on a build when … every covering check's latest receipt on that tree reports passed".
- §10.13: "A broad family is never reported `passed` while any of its registered cases is missing".
- P10: a run below `min_cases` fails.

## Area
xtask (`traceability.rs`), possibly a schema update in `schemas/dev/traceability.v1.schema.json`.

## Acceptance
- Evidence counts as passed only if its case count is at least the check's `min_cases`, and only for a full, unfiltered selection; a `--case` run never satisfies a family.
- The registry inputs are read from the judged tree (`git show <tree>:registry/…`) whenever a tree is given.
- Fixtures for both.
- DEV-SCHEMAS still passes.

## Out of scope
The registry gate's own conditions.

title: BUG: spec-invalid values are constructible in types (Refusal::Recovering{Ready}, Conflict at index 0; Entry/Ready/ScanPage invariants doc-only)
description:
## Context
Found in a fresh-eyes review of W04 code (VioletOwl for cc_1, 2026-10-03). Both independent reviewers raised the first two cases, the Opus reviewer added the rest, and I verified them all by hand.

Several port and response types have public fields, or carry a field type wider than the spec allows. As a result, values that the API spec or the type's own doc forbids can be constructed, and only doc comments guard them. `TerminalResult::new` (`outcome.rs:79`) shows the intended pattern: it refuses index 0. The `Conflict` outcome, which is also terminal for its ID, has no such guard.

**Evidence (HEAD 412cd01):**
1. **A 503 body that fails the schema.** `crates/types/src/client.rs:214` has `Refusal::Recovering { lifecycle: Lifecycle }`, documented "never `Ready`". `Lifecycle::Ready` is accepted, and the spec's `NotReadyLifecycle` is `[starting, recovering, failed]` (`api/openapi.yaml:1164-1168`).
2. **A 409 body below the spec's minimum.** `crates/types/src/client.rs:266` (`Response::Conflict`) and `crates/types/src/outcome.rs:118` (`AttemptOutcome::Conflict`) both have `original_index: LogIndex`, which accepts `LogIndex::ZERO`. The spec's `original_index` is `EntryIndex`, minimum 1 (`api/openapi.yaml:1346-1347`).
3. **An entry at index 0.** `crates/types/src/consensus.rs:51-53`: `Entry { pub index: LogIndex, .. }` is documented "index is at least 1", but `index: LogIndex::ZERO` builds.
4. **Acks released over unsynced entries.** `crates/types/src/consensus.rs:89-96`: `Ready { entries: non-empty, must_sync: false }` builds. The core would write no frame and release append acks over unsynced entries, contradicting §7.4 ("never release … an append acknowledgement based on unsynced state").
5. **SCAN pages with no single point of enforcement.** `crates/types/src/client.rs:170-174`: `ScanPage { pub items, pub continuation }` is documented as having unique, ascending, in-range items, at most the page limit and 1 MiB, with `continuation` equal to the last returned key. Any caller can build an inconsistent `has_more`/`next_after` pair or an over-limit page (§7.11 SCAN page, §8.5).

## Requirements
CD-2 ("Make invalid states unrepresentable"), CD-3 (private fields and smart constructors), §7.4, §7.11, §8.1 ("details schemas, matched exactly"), §8.5.

## Area
types (`client.rs`, `outcome.rs`, `consensus.rs`).

## Acceptance
For each case, either:
- make it unrepresentable: a `NotReadyLifecycle`-style enum, an entry-index newtype, or private fields with a checked constructor; or
- assert the invariant in the one constructor (CD-7).

Each needs a test, or a compile-fail fixture where the type system carries the rule. `./dev gate fast` passes.

## Out of scope
Adapter-side rendering. W13 may need to adapt to the changed `Entry`/`Ready` constructors.

title: raft_adapter: peer decode allocates before any bound (1 MiB of empty entries, pre-allocated lengths); no registered entries-per-message bound (CD-9)
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of W13.3 + br-xx08 (fd96d6d) by GoldenHorizon, 2026-10-04, at HEAD 7d4ddd9. Opus rated it P2 and Fable P3; I verified it in protobuf 2.28.0.

**Every refusal happens after a full protobuf decode, and the 1 MiB envelope payload bound does not bound what that decode allocates. There is no registered bound on entries per message (CD-9).**

**Evidence:**
- `convert.rs:85` calls `parse_from_bytes` on the whole payload.
- `envelope.rs:56` bounds it only by `MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (1 MiB, the journal-frame limit), not by what v1 sends inbound: at most `replication_batch_bytes` (256 KiB) plus one command entry plus fixed overhead (§7.11).

**Failure (a):** the payload `3a 00` × 524,288 (1 MiB of empty `entries`) builds about 524K default `Entry` values (tens of MiB) before admission refuses it, for its type or at position 0. About 260K distinct unknown field numbers similarly build a large UnknownFields map before `decode_message` rejects it.

**Failure (b):**
- `62 ff ac e2 04` declares `context` with length 9,999,999 in 5 bytes.
- For slice input, `BufReadIter::read_exact_bytes` (buf_read_iter.rs:243-275) runs `BytesMut::with_capacity(len)` for any len below 10,000,000 before checking that the bytes exist. `read_exact_to_vec` does the same for unknown length-delimited fields.

Each case is transient and per message, so no panic. But it is roughly 50× amplification on an input path, against CD-9.

## Requirements
CD-3, CD-9 (a registered bound for every queue, map or cache), §7.11, DM-7, §10.19's peer-decoder property.

## Area
crates/raft_adapter (convert.rs, envelope.rs, tests); a limits-registry row if a new bound is added; the PEER-ENVELOPE and PEER-ADMISSION rows.

## Acceptance
A cheap wire pre-scan in `decode_message`, before `parse_from_bytes`:
- only known field numbers and wire types, and no groups;
- every declared length checked against the remaining bytes;
- the count of field-7 entries capped by a bound derived from `replication_batch_bytes`;
- entry `data` capped at `MAX_COMMAND_BYTES`.

And/or the envelope payload bounded by what v1 sends inbound, as a registered limit. Decoding from `Bytes` (`parse_from_carllerche_bytes`) also avoids (b).

Tests: the two inputs above are refused without the allocation, which can be shown by a bound on the scan, or by refusal before decode.

## Out of scope
Fuzzing (W53).

title: BUG: DIFFERENTIAL's counter, final-map and unknown-ID comparisons are never shown live by any mutant
description:
## Context
Found in JadeOx's fresh-eyes review of W10.3 (b36a20d, crates/sim/tests/differential.rs), for cc_1, 2026-10-04. Two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable) worked on a frozen tree at f00a912, and both rated this P2. The reviewers re-measured the reach figures in scratch harnesses; JadeOx has not re-run them.

**Three comparison paths are never shown to be live by any mutant,** so if one regressed to `Ok(())`, DIFFERENTIAL would stay green. W10's acceptance ("a broken variant must fail it") is meant to exclude exactly that.
- The paths: `compare_counters` (differential.rs about 739-757), `compare_final` (map contents, order and stored versions; about 761-806), and the unknown-IDs and history check (about 976-1003).
- Measured, every mutant's first divergence is caught at `compare_apply` or `compare_get`. LooseKeyQuota 301, LooseByteQuota 91, VersionOffByOne 400, ReplayAsExecution 399, HistoryUnderWrongIds 400, StaleGet 115. None is caught by counters, the final map or `unknown_ids`.
- VersionOffByOne shifts the result version, which production derives from the already-compared index (`types/src/outcome.rs` about 107-114). So the realistic DM-3 bug, a wrong `Stored.version` seen only through GET and the final map, has no mutant.
- The reviewer's experiment: with the version comparison dropped from `get`/`map`, a state machine storing `version = index - 1` goes from 397 to 0 of 400 seeds caught. With counters off, an overwrite that doesn't reclaim old bytes goes from 391 to 236.

**Also, single reviewer (Opus) P2, not independently re-run:** a capacity refusal that is re-executed once room appears (breaking DM-6, §7.5 step 4 and C-6) is reached on only 3 of 400 seeds (45, 65, 124), and no coverage floor protects it. With PUT only, a key refusal never becomes admissible again; only a byte refusal after a shrinking overwrite does.

**Folded in: P3s both reviewers raised.**
- Every coverage floor is `> 0` (differential.rs about 950), while measured counts run 277 to 6,262. Make them proportional, for example 50 or more.
- Reach gaps:
  - no value above 40 B (nothing near DM-2's 65,536);
  - the 256-byte key is ASCII only;
  - profile (8, 4) has a dead key quota;
  - LooseByteQuota is equivalent to the real machine in two profiles.
- DM-7's `committed_command_bytes` is not compared. A cheap assertion: it grows by the encoded command length exactly on the model's first executions.

## Requirements
T-7, §10.14, W10's acceptance (a broken variant must fail it), §10.15, DM-3, DM-6, C-6.

## Area
sim (`tests/differential.rs`).

## Acceptance
- Wrapper mutants that are each caught **only** by their own path, each asserted caught (with a shrunk log that passes on the real state machine):
  - stored version off by one in `get`/`map` only;
  - live bytes not reclaimed on overwrite (`counters`);
  - reversed map order (DM-4);
  - a phantom history ID.
- A mutant that re-executes a replayed refusal, with a coverage floor for "a replayed refusal that would now fit", and generator bias so it's reached often.
- Coverage floors proportional to measured reach; the reach gaps above closed, or the checks.toml summary narrowed.
- DIFFERENTIAL passes, with min_cases raised.

## Out of scope
DELETE, CAS and SCAN (W27/W28 planned rows).

title: raft_adapter: no invariant stops input (propose, step, tick) while a Ready is outstanding (§7.4 step 3; raft-rs ready() contract)

title: RAFT-READY-LOOP's seeded runs never leave term 1: no later-term vote, leader change or log-suffix overwrite is ever judged against DUR-2
description:
## Context
Found in the read-only review of W13.2, the Ready loop (VioletOwl; br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa, 7eb3316), for cc_1 on 2026-10-04. The review was at HEAD 7ec6be4, by SunnyDog plus two independent fresh reviewers (Opus and Fable). Both reviewers raised it as P2, and SunnyDog measured it. Thread: br-w13-2-ready-loop-hsa.

RAFT-READY-LOOP claims DUR-2 from "scripted and seeded three-voter runs judged against each sender's synced journal".

**The measurement.** A scratch probe (not committed) at HEAD 7d4ddd9 covered all 12 seeds of `no_message_leaves_on_unsynced_state_in_seeded_cluster_runs` (`seeded_run`, ready_loop_tests.rs:588-630). Every node of every seed ends at term 1, with 0 frames that overwrite a log suffix, that is, a frame whose first entry index is at or below the previous last. Per seed, the nodes write 6–53 frames and send 70–186 messages.

**Why.** The network never drops, duplicates or partitions anything. Ticks go to random nodes, but the leader's heartbeats keep everyone following, so the first election is the only one.

**What the randomised evidence never sees:**
- a vote in a later term, or a vote rejected by term;
- a leader stepping down;
- a follower's conflicting suffix being replaced;
- the journal's logical truncation, driven by raft-rs.

The scripted tests (vote request, vote grant, append acknowledgement) are all first-election, term-1 cases too.

**Why the overwrite path matters.** It is the most intricate interaction between raft-rs and the journal:
1. `truncate_and_append` lowers the unstable offset below storage's last index, and `maybe_append` lowers `persisted` (raft_log.rs:264-271).
2. The batch's first index is at or below the journal's last.
3. `LogicalLog::apply` truncates the offset index and the cache, and checks `TruncatesCommitted` against the persisted commit.
4. After SyncDone, `stable_entries` and `maybe_persist` re-advance `persisted` through `store.term`.

All three reviews found it correct by reading; nothing runs it.

## Requirements
- DUR-2, C-1, C-2.
- §7.4 rules: never release a vote grant or an append acknowledgement on unsynced state.
- §10.15: claims match their evidence.

## Area
raft_adapter tests (`ready_loop_tests.rs`). This overlaps the adversarial-ordering scope of W13.4 (JadeOx, br-w13-4-adversarial-ordering-tests-xsn); cc_1 may fold it in there.

## Acceptance
- **Adversarial seeded runs.** The seeded runs inject message loss or delay and leader isolation, or partitions.
  - Across the seeds, there must be elections in later terms, leader changes, rejected votes, and frames that overwrite a suffix.
  - Non-vacuity counters assert that each happens at least once.
  - The DUR-2 oracles (`dur2_violation` and `sends_wait_for_syncs`) stay clean.
- **A scripted conflicting-suffix test.**
  1. Leader A appends entries that nobody receives.
  2. B wins a later term and appends different entries.
  3. A receives B's append.
  4. Assert: A's frame has a first index at or below its previous last, and A's acknowledgement is held until that frame syncs.
  5. After SyncDone, the storage view serves B's entries and terms, and `applied` and `commit` stay consistent.
- RAFT-READY-LOOP's min_cases is raised to match, and T0 is green.

## Out of scope
A crash or restart in the middle of a run (W16 simulation, K-11).

title: W01.6: Project-wide test logging & diagnostics standard
description:
Codify the project-wide TEST LOGGING & DIAGNOSTICS STANDARD, documented in AGENTS.md's Testing section and enforced from the first bead onward, so every later suite inherits it:

1. **Assertion context.** Every assertion message carries enough state to diagnose without a debugger: the CD-7 `invariant!` style (node, index, invariant ID) extends to ALL test suites — a failing test names the inputs, the expected value, the observed value and the rule violated.
2. **Re-runnability.** Property-test failures persist their seed and shrunk case, and the failure output contains the exact re-run command (mirroring the simulator's seed/replay discipline, T-4). A failing test you cannot re-run from its log is a defect.
3. **E2E/probe/demo step logging.** Every scripted end-to-end flow (demos in --assert mode, the lifecycle smoke, crash probes, parity scenario, clean-state rehearsal, the CLI journey) logs each step as a structured record — step name, action, expected, observed, outcome, duration — to stderr AND a log file in the run's artifact directory, and exits non-zero on the first failed step. Gate runs tee these logs next to their receipts.
4. **No silent skips.** A skipped step or vacuous selection is logged as such and fails per P10.
5. **Bounded.** Test logs respect CD-9 (bounded size; oldest-dropped-and-counted) and the Q9 .local/ retention rule (pruned only by ./dev prune).
6. **Helpers stay out of production.** Any shared logging helper is a dev-dependency/test-support module only, never compiled into production builds (T-6 discipline), and never logs from inside deterministic-core production paths (the canonical trace and Telemetry port own those).

Acceptance: the standard is written into AGENTS.md's Testing section; a minimal test-support helper exists where it pays; W01's probe tests demonstrate a failing test producing a context-rich, re-runnable log record. Part of W01.

title: W01: Bootstrap workspace, pinned toolchain, ./dev (doctor/check/gate fast), lint policy, AGENTS.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, beads init
description:
## Context
Everything in this project flows through one repo-owned entry point: `./dev` (a Rust xtask behind a small launcher). W01 creates the workspace, the pinned toolchain, the lint policy that substitutes for human code review, the AGENTS.md rulebook, DEPENDENCIES.md, and the first (bootstrap) gate — before any database code exists. Local verification is the authority (P7): there is no hosted CI; every gate is a command on the dev machine that writes a receipt.

## Requirements covered
- P7 (local verification is the authority), CD-8 (no unwrap/expect/panic/todo/unimplemented/unsafe in first-party production code), CD-12 (every dependency justified in DEPENDENCIES.md; lockfile committed), O-8 (`./dev status` / `./dev doctor` surface — doctor part here).

## Area (file reservations)
`root` (workspace Cargo.toml/lock, rust-toolchain.toml, dev launcher, AGENTS.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, .gitignore), `xtask`.

## Depends on
Nothing — this is the first item. Until W07 lands, only the coordinator agent commits (bootstrap exception, §11.2 step 2).

## Design & key rules
- `./dev doctor`: probes the environment — toolchain, br, bv, NTM, UBS, DCG, Agent Mail — records each installed version, and FAILS on a missing capability (never assumes documented behaviour; RISK-16).
- `./dev check <ID>`: unknown IDs and zero-test selections fail (P10 — no vacuous passes).
- `./dev gate fast` (bootstrap form): runs a FIXED set until the registry (W05) takes over: format check, lints with denied warnings, dependency-rule check, xtask unit tests, UBS on staged files. Writes a receipt with the tree ID.
- Lint policy (enforces §5.2 mechanically, because nobody reviews code — D-17): `unsafe_code` forbidden; `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`panic`/`todo`/`unimplemented` denied outside tests; wildcard enum match arms denied in deterministic crates (CD-5); missing docs denied on public items in deterministic crates (CD-11); determinism lints (no `Instant::now`/`SystemTime::now`, no thread/async spawns, no randomly-hashed maps in deterministic crates — §7.14). Lints are pinned to the project toolchain and PROVEN effective: a probe file that violates each lint must be rejected (never assume a lint works from its docs).
- The project `invariant!` macro (built on `assert!`) is the only sanctioned panic path (CD-7/CD-8), so bare `panic!` stays denied without allowing any CD-enforcing or determinism lint. Any unrelated narrow allow must satisfy the documented escape-hatch policy and bead decision log in AGENTS.md.
- AGENTS.md carries the 18 normative rules of §11.5 (owner override; §0.4 precedence + `conflict` beads; P9 oracle protection; determinism; hexagonal core; real slices only; plan is owner-owned; stay in your area; seeds to corpus; robot mode; CD rules; registry discipline; claim classes; JSON schemas; `./dev commit` only — no raw git, no branches/worktrees, no `ntm --worktrees`; receipts as the only evidence; test-only code gating; node-data safety). It must state explicitly that this project REPLACES the ACFS landing-the-plane git checklist.
- DEPENDENCIES.md: every direct dependency with purpose, scope, version, licence, source. Deterministic crates start from std + vendored raft only.

## Acceptance
- `./dev doctor` reports every required tool with its version and fails when one is missing.
- `./dev check NOPE` fails.
- `./dev gate fast` runs the bootstrap set on the clean workspace and writes a receipt containing the tree ID.
- A probe file using `unwrap` outside tests is rejected by the lint gate.
- AGENTS.md contains every §11.5 rule.

## Out of scope
The verification registry and registry-driven gate staging (W05); the commit wrapper (W07); any server/db code; beads import (W06). Do not create empty placeholder crates (P6) — crates are created by the first bead that needs them.

## Notes for the future
- Budget target for T0 is ≤ 2 min warm with a 3-min alert threshold; keep the bootstrap gate lean from day one (RISK-19: serialised commits make T0 latency the commit throughput bound).
- UBS is pinned for gate runs; auto-update disabled during verification; partial scan = failure.

PLAN.md wins over this bead on any disagreement (§0.4) — file a `conflict` bead. Plan refs: §11.1, §11.5, §11.13, §10.10, §5.2.

title: W02: Raft library determinism spike — vendor, audit, entropy patch, fresh-process proof, go/no-go
description:
## Context
Decision 1 of the whole plan: prove the deterministic consensus boundary FIRST, before building anything on it. We borrow Raft rather than writing it (D-05, R-02): primary is TiKV `raft-rs` (`raft` + `raft-proto` 0.7.0, last release Mar 2023 — RISK-1), a consensus-module-only library the application drives via tick/step/propose/Ready/advance, which fits a discrete-event simulator naturally. But it randomises election timeouts internally and may hide other nondeterminism; P4 demands: same seed + same build ⇒ byte-identical traces across fresh OS processes. This spike vendors, audits, patches and PROVES that, with an explicit go/no-go.

## Requirements covered
P4 (determinism), T-3 (byte-identical canonical trace), T-11 (fresh-process replay identity).

## Area
`vendor` (vendor/raft/, third_party/raft.patch), `spike` (spike/ — kept as evidence).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace, toolchain, gate).

## Design & key rules
- Vendor `raft`/`raft-proto` 0.7.0 into `vendor/raft/` with recorded checksums, enabled features, toolchain.
- AUDIT: enumerate every path reachable from construction, campaign, tick, step and timeout reset that could introduce nondeterminism — entropy, ambient clocks, threads, unordered collection iteration, randomly seeded hashers, pointer formatting, logging side effects. Also enumerate unbounded entry fetches on election/commit paths (e.g. `maybe_commit_by_vote` materialising entries with no size limit); each finding gets a bounded-handling policy (W13 adds the large-log test). Unproven "probably fine" items get a test.
- PATCH (`third_party/raft.patch`): minimal; routes every randomness source — notably randomised election timeouts at construction and on every reset — through a MANDATORY, self-contained entropy trait defined INSIDE the vendored crate (D-57: the vendored crate never depends on first-party code; upstream tests supply a seeded source; no ambient default). The patch MUST NOT touch vote, log-matching, quorum or commit rules. Setting a timeout from outside after construction is NOT sufficient (reset paths re-randomise).
- Codegen pinning: `PROTOC` forced to a bundled binary, or the generated code vendored, so no PATH-dependent protoc can vary the build; recorded in `build_id`; checked by `./dev doctor`.
- Determinism proof: a seeded 3-node in-memory loop gives identical spike-local traces for 100 seeds × 3 fresh processes, including crash-restart and re-election.

## Acceptance
- Vendored 0.7.0 with checksums; audit report lists every finding with its policy; the patch defines and injects the vendored entropy trait; upstream tests pass with the patch; protoc pinning recorded and doctor-checked; 100 seeds × 3 fresh processes byte-identical; go/no-go recorded in the decision log (§16).

## Out of scope
The Consensus port and Ready loop (W13). Never patch vote logic; never write our own Raft.

## Notes for the future
- FAILURE HANDLING IS SPECIAL: if the spike fails, the bead is NOT closed (closing a blocker would unblock dependants). `./dev commit --close W02 --failed` records the evidence report, labels the bead `failed`+`needs-owner`, and leaves it OPEN so dependants stay blocked until the owner's recorded plan revision (D-70).
- Fallback (recorded, not improvised): OpenRaft 0.9.x behind the same Consensus port with fully controlled runtime and entropy; switching is a plan revision in §16, never a quiet change (§7.3). If OpenRaft is adopted, R-03 (madsim/turmoil rejection) is reopened.
- raft-rs 0.7 hardwires the election-timeout range shape to [election_tick, 2×election_tick); the entropy-only patch does not change that — config validation (W08) encodes it.

PLAN.md wins over this bead on any disagreement (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.3, §12.2 W02, D-05, D-57, RISK-1, §11.4 (failed spikes).

title: W03: Complete api/openapi.yaml per the API contract, with fixtures
description:
## Context
OpenAPI-first (D-12): `api/openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1.0) is the precise HTTP contract, completed BEFORE any server code is written. The independent conformance suite (W31) derives from it; on conflict with PLAN.md §8, the plan wins (§0.4). This item authors the complete spec and its test fixtures.

## Requirements covered
F-1…F-10 (all operations incl. request IDs, routing, status), O-1 (health + cluster endpoints).

## Area
`api` (api/openapi.yaml + fixtures).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace + `./dev check` plumbing for the SPEC check).

## Design & key rules (the contract, condensed from §8)
- Base path `/v1`; strict JSON (unknown fields, duplicate members, bad UTF-8/numbers → 400 invalid_request); keys are QUERY parameters, never path segments (keys may contain `/ ? &`); RFC 3986 percent-decoding with an unescaped `+` REJECTED (form-encoding ambiguity would corrupt keys; literal plus = %2B, space = %20); every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; byte limits recorded via `x-maxUtf8Bytes` (JSON Schema length counts characters, not bytes); writes require `Idempotency-Key`: 32 lowercase hex chars (128 bits); integers are JSON numbers validated < 2^53.
- Endpoints: PUT /v1/kv?key=K {value} → {request_id,index,version,replayed,served_by}; GET /v1/kv?key=K → {key,value,version,served_by{node_id,applied_index}}; DELETE /v1/kv?key=K → {…existed…}; POST /v1/cas?key=K {expected:{kind:absent|version},value}; GET /v1/scan?start&end&after&limit → {items,has_more,next_after,served_by}; GET /v1/requests/{id} → state known (embedded original result) | unknown; GET /v1/health/live (lifecycle starting|recovering|ready|failed); GET /v1/health/ready (200 only when a complete committed read view is available); GET /v1/cluster (role, term, leader, indices, peers).
- Error envelope: {"error":{code,message,details}} with exactly three write-details shapes: (1) terminal execution results (version_mismatch, capacity_exceeded): request_id, index, replayed, decision — immutable; (2) conflict refusal (request_id_conflict): request_id, original_index; (3) non-terminal refusals (307 not_leader, 429 busy, 503 unavailable/recovering, 504 unknown_outcome, 507 history_full): request_id + attempt_state (not_submitted|submitted) + code-specific fields. 400/413 carry request_id only when a well-formed Idempotency-Key was present.
- Outcome table (§8.4): 307 not_leader (Location = leader, same path+query); 409 version_mismatch (TERMINAL, consumes the ID); 409 request_id_conflict; 413 too_large; 429 busy; 503 unavailable (+nodes)/recovering (+lifecycle); 504 unknown_outcome (+guidance retry_same_request_or_query_status, +nodes); 507 capacity_exceeded (TERMINAL committed decision) vs 507 history_full (not submitted, retry only after v2 compaction) — two distinct codes by design (D-54, to avoid RISK-15 double-writes).
- Per-operation response schemas: a PUT cannot validate as a DELETE result.

## Acceptance
- Validates as OpenAPI 3.1; every endpoint, status, code, byte limit (x-maxUtf8Bytes) and example of §8 present; per-operation response schemas; positive and negative fixtures pass `./dev check SPEC`; NO server code.

## Out of scope
Any server implementation; the peer channel (`POST /raft` on peer addresses) is internal and excluded from the public contract.

## Notes for the future
- Client guidance strings live in the spec descriptions (307 → follow with same ID; 504 → retry same ID or query status; an error on a later attempt is never evidence an earlier attempt did not commit).
- SCAN semantics: range [start,end) byte-wise UTF-8 order; `after` exclusive continuation; item cap 1–128 (default 32) and 1 MiB decoded-bytes page cap; has_more/next_after; no server-side cursor.
- A late contract change joins the critical path — get this right early (§12.4).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §8 (all), D-09, D-12, D-29, D-35, D-54, R-11, R-22, R-23.

These exact fields belong in workgraph.toml. Leaf reservations and additional check coverage do not alter the canonical Reqs activation set. Acceptance in the parent remains cumulative with its subtasks; no feature or existing criterion is removed.

comments.text:
SunnyDog — design notes and readings for W04.1:
- D-77 by type: NodeId (1..=2^53-1), Term and LogIndex (0..=2^53-1) and Version (1..=2^53-1) refuse anything else at construction, through one OutOfRange{quantity, value} error, so every value the core reports is a safe JSON integer. checked_next and checked_prev return None at the edges.
- Version converts to and from LogIndex only explicitly (Version::at(index) / version.index()); index 0 is no version.
- Tick and ByteCount are unbounded u64 with checked add/sub. PageSize is 1..=128 with DEFAULT 32 (F-4).
- RequestId is 16 bytes parsed from exactly 32 lowercase hex characters, and its Display is canonical.
- Key and Value have separate error types (KeyError -> 400, ValueError -> 413, per §8.4) and expose byte_len, as_str and into_string. Keys order by str (byte-wise, DM-4).
- READING for W08 to confirm: ClusterId (the display name) is 1..=255 UTF-8 bytes, a bound chosen so the genesis encoding has a limit (CD-9). The plan gives none.

title: W04: Domain types, newtypes, enums, error type and all ports
description:
## Context
Ports first (§11.7): the domain types and port definitions are created early so the production, simulation and oracle tracks can all proceed in parallel against stable interfaces. This crate is the heart of the hexagonal architecture (CD-1): the deterministic core defines ports in its OWN types; adapters translate; dependencies point inward only.

## Requirements covered
CD-1 (hexagonal), CD-2 (invalid states unrepresentable), CD-3 (parse, don't validate), CD-4 (distinct types per quantity), CD-5 (exhaustive matching), CD-11 (boring over clever; doc comments stating invariants), DM-1 (key: UTF-8, 1–256 bytes after decoding, stored exactly, no normalisation), DM-2 (value: UTF-8, 0–65,536 bytes after decoding), DM-4 (byte-wise lexicographic key order), T-1 (deterministic logic reaches time/randomness/network/disk only through ports).

## Area
`types` (crates/types).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace, lints), W03 (the error enum must match the spec's codes exactly — registry condition 5 later checks this).

## Design & key rules
- Newtypes (CD-4): NodeId, ClusterId, Term, LogIndex, Version, Tick, RequestId, ByteCount, PageSize — no bare integers cross a module boundary; comparing Version with LogIndex needs an explicit conversion; arithmetic is checked.
- Smart constructors (CD-3): `Key::parse` enforces DM-1 (255/256/257-byte cases, multibyte, composed vs decomposed Unicode are DIFFERENT keys); `Value::parse` enforces DM-2 (empty OK, 64 KiB max). Private fields; the core never re-checks.
- Enums (CD-2): node lifecycle Starting → Recovering → Ready → Failed; attempt NotSubmitted | Submitted | Terminal(result) — never independent booleans (unknown outcome is a RESPONSE about a Submitted attempt, not a fourth state); ExpectedVersion Absent | Version(v); Mutation (Put/Delete/Cas); error enum matching every spec code.
- Ports (§7.2): inbound `step(input) → effects`; effect ports returned as VALUES (Send, Append/Sync, Respond, Log/Observe) executed by the composition root, completions come back as inputs (SyncDone carries the node incarnation — completions from a previous incarnation are ignored); in-process ports called synchronously (entropy; bounded byte-storage reads, because raft-rs storage callbacks are synchronous). Effects are emitted in deterministic order. Port types are owned by the core.
- Every public domain type documents its invariants (CD-11 lint).

## Acceptance

title: W05: Verification registry, T0 registry gate, traceability report
description:
## Context
Evidence over claims (P5) is enforced mechanically: a small machine-readable registry in `registry/` indexes ALL verification, and a T0 gate keeps plan ↔ registry ↔ code ↔ spec ↔ tests ↔ work graph consistent on every commit. This is the project's substitute for anyone "keeping track" by memory, and the guard against vacuous coverage (D-22, RISK-13).

## Requirements covered
P5; the whole of §10.13.

## Area
`registry` (registry/*.toml), `xtask` (the gate + report code).

## Depends on
W01 (xtask/gate), W03 (spec for conditions 5–6), W04 (code markers to validate), W06 (workgraph.toml for condition 8).

## Design & key rules
- Files: `registry/requirements.toml` (one row per §6 requirement: id, level MUST/SHOULD/MAY, status planned|active, title, disposition notes); `registry/checks.toml` (one row per check: id, kind, covers (req IDs), api (operation IDs/error codes), class (§10.15 claim class), tier, run (exact `./dev check` selector), min_cases (non-zero), catches (bug variants only)); `registry/workgraph.toml` (from W06).
- Code linking: every check declares its id in code as a greppable marker (e.g. `// check: K-5`) AND its row names an executable selector; marker alone is not enough — the selector must run ≥ min_cases assertions.
- The gate FAILS on: (1) requirements.toml differs from §6 (plan wins); (2) an ACTIVE MUST requirement with no implemented covering check; (3) implemented check without exactly one code marker, or marker without row; (4) implemented selector that does not resolve — in T0 the selector check is STATIC (resolve + list cases); min_cases execution is enforced by the tier that runs the check (D-72, so T0 never executes T1–T3 campaigns); (5) spec error codes differ from the domain error enum, or an operation lacks a handler; (6) an operation/error code no conformance test exercises; (7) a bug-variant row without a designated catcher; (8) workgraph.toml differs from §12.2, has a cycle, or disagrees with imported bead dependencies (plan:W edges only).
- Conditions 5–6 are REPORTED, not failed, until W32 closes (W18 implements only PUT/GET; enforcing earlier would fail every commit between W18 and W32 — D-49).
- Status lifecycle: requirements start planned; a requirement becomes ACTIVE when ALL work items listing it in their Reqs have closed (activation derived from workgraph.toml by `./dev commit --close`, never typed by hand — the gate REJECTS hand-edited statuses, rule 12). Check statuses are declared, forward-only, protected like oracle manifests (D-56): a broken selector can never silently demote a check to planned. "Passed on a build" is computed from receipts, never stored.
- W05 initialises requirements.toml with correct statuses for beads already closed by then.
- T1 renders `reports/traceability.md`: each requirement, status, qualifications, covering checks with claim classes and latest receipts.

## Acceptance
- Each of the eight gate conditions demonstrated by a fixture that makes it fail (5–6 in report mode; condition 8 against W06's workgraph.toml); a hand-edited requirement status is rejected; requirements.toml matches §6; the traceability report renders.

## Out of scope
The bead importer (W06); gate TIERS and scheduling (W46); bug-variant execution (W45).

## Notes for the future
- B-21 (meta bug variant, W45) will mutate a registry row in a sandboxed tree copy and expect THIS gate to catch it — keep the gate honest.
- The registry gate catches mechanical drift continuously; semantic drift is the drift audits' job (§11.9).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.13, D-22, D-56, D-72, RISK-13.

title: W06: Work-graph manifest (workgraph.toml) and idempotent bead import
description:
## Context
The work graph lives in three places that must never drift: PLAN.md §12.2 (authoritative), `registry/workgraph.toml` (machine mirror), and the beads tracker (execution state). W06 builds the mirror and the idempotent importer. Plan changes flow plan → workgraph.toml → beads, NEVER the other way (§11.11).

## Requirements covered
G1 (the dev-process goal itself), §11.11.

## Area
`registry`, `xtask`.

## Depends on
W01.

## Design & key rules
- `workgraph.toml`: one row per §12.2 item — id, title, deps, reqs, area, milestone (derived from m0–m5 epic labels), accept (executable acceptance selectors; the §12.2 acceptance column is their prose description), and the tracker's bead ID once imported (recorded, never guessed).
- `./dev beads import --dry-run` prints the diff; `./dev beads import` applies idempotently: beads are identified by their `plan:W<nn>` label; repeated imports never duplicate; hand-created beads (this very bead set!) are ADOPTED by label.
- The importer uses supported `br` CLI operations only — it never hand-edits the tracker's files; `br` never runs git itself (§11.1).
- The drift check (feeding registry condition 8): workgraph.toml vs §12.2 on id/deps/reqs/area (ranges like "F-1…F-10" expand); the bead comparison covers ONLY edges between plan:W beads — bug and discovered-work beads (and the sub:W subtask beads) may add edges freely.
- Cycles are rejected.

## Acceptance
- workgraph.toml matches §12.2 and the drift check fails on a changed dependency; --dry-run prints the diff; a second import creates no duplicates; plan-ID ↔ bead-ID mapping stored; cycles rejected.

## Out of scope
The eight-condition registry gate itself (W05); milestone epic management.

## Notes for the future
- After import, run `bv --robot-insights` (no cycles) and `bv --robot-suggest` (missing deps, duplicates); fix findings in the PLAN first (§0.4), then re-import (§11.2 step 4).

title: W07: Exact-candidate commit wrapper, acceptance runner, closure lifecycle
description:
## Context
Up to six agents edit ONE shared checkout on `main` (D-16, no branches/worktrees). Running tests in that shared checkout proves nothing about the tree that actually gets committed (R-21). `./dev commit` therefore serialises the COMMIT BOUNDARY (not the coding): it stages only the agent's files, materialises the exact candidate tree, gates it in isolation, and commits exactly that tree (P11: exact-tree evidence; D-32). W07 also owns `./dev accept` and the bead-closure lifecycle.

## Requirements covered
P11, §11.10 (commit protocol), §11.3 (work loop steps 6–7).

## Area
`xtask`.

## Depends on
W01.

## Design & key rules (the protocol, condensed from §11.10)
1. Acquire an exclusive local commit lock (a real lock). Confirm HEAD on main, no other git op in progress, the bead valid and in_progress (or just-closed for a --close commit), every staged path inside the agent's live reservation. Refuse any unexpected staged path.
2. Stage only the agent's named paths (never `git add -A`). Record parent commit + candidate tree ID.
3. Materialise the tree into the FIXED `.local/candidate/` directory, refreshed in place under the lock; verify the directory's content manifest against the tree — leftover or missing files REFUSE the run (cargo auto-discovers stray tests/*.rs, which would silently test a different tree — D-55). One stable path keeps cargo caches warm; the receipt records the tree ID, never the path. Not a branch, not a linked worktree.
4. Run T0 on the candidate with git discovery DISABLED (GIT_DIR → nonexistent, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES → candidate root): nothing in there — UBS, cargo VCS info, stray git calls — can see the shared checkout. Changed-file list passed to UBS explicitly; build_id computed from the recorded tree ID (D-74). A fixture proves a git call inside the candidate sees no repository.
5. Re-check parent, tree ID, lock, index; if anything changed, re-run against the new candidate — never commit a different tree because tests already finished.
6. Commit exactly the tested tree; record receipt (tree, parent, bead IDs); release the lock.
- `./dev accept <bead> --tree <id>`: materialises the NAMED committed tree into `.local/accept/<tree-id>/` (content-verified AND git-isolated like the candidate), runs the bead's acceptance selectors there, writes a receipt naming that tree — never a shared checkout, never the commit-locked candidate dir.
- `./dev commit --close <id>`: one-step closure — validates the acceptance receipt, `br close`, `br sync --flush-only`, recomputes requirement activation in registry/requirements.toml, commits .beads/ + that registry file in the same wrapped commit (the wrapper accepts the just-closed bead for this closure commit).
- `./dev commit --close <id> --failed`: records the failure-evidence report, labels the bead failed+needs-owner, leaves it OPEN so dependants stay blocked (critical for the W02 spike; closing a blocker would unblock dependants — D-70).

## Acceptance
- Adversarial fixtures pass: foreign staged path refused; HEAD moving during the gate forces a re-run; a file edited in the shared checkout during the gate is not committed; receipt tree ID equals the committed tree; candidate manifest check refuses leftovers; no branch or worktree ever created. `./dev accept` runs in .local/accept/<tree-id>/ with a receipt naming the tree. `--close` validates receipts, closes the bead and commits .beads/ + registry flips (tested against a FIXTURE registry — W05 provides the real one); `--failed` leaves the bead open with failed/needs-owner. Fixtures cover a missing receipt, a wrong tree ID and a failed spike.

## Out of scope
The real registry gate (W05); gate tier contents (W46); any push behaviour beyond the wrapper hook (a remote does not exist yet — owner action).

## Notes for the future
- A failed gate preserves the agent's work and NEVER cleans up anyone else's edits.
- Commits are serialised (~2-min T0 ⇒ ~30 commits/hour max) — an accepted cost of shared-main development with exact evidence (RISK-19). Keep T0 fast.
- Until this lands, the coordinator-commit bootstrap flow applies (§11.2 step 2); the full swarm launches only after W04+W06+W07.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §11.10, §11.3, D-32, D-55, D-58, D-74, R-21, RISK-5.

title: W08: Config type, genesis fingerprint, limits registry
description:
## Context
One static config file drives everything: cluster identity, membership, addresses, data dirs, semantic limits, timing. It is parsed ONCE into a validated Config type (CD-3) that rejects inconsistent values with specific errors — a config the parser accepts can never fail later at RawNode construction. W08 also builds the semantic-config fingerprint (part of genesis binding, DUR-8) and the limits registry (CD-9: a named, configured maximum on EVERYTHING).

## Requirements covered
O-5 (one static config; no silent default overrides), O-9 (loopback defaults + warning), DUR-8 (genesis binding), CD-3, CD-9.

## Area
`types`, `config` (config/local.toml).

## Depends on
W04 (domain types).

## Design & key rules (validation rules, condensed from §7.10)
Reject, with a specific error: voter count other than 1/3/5 (one odd count per config; release+local profiles pin 5; 1- and 3-voter configs exist for dev/tests/probes/demos — D-45); duplicate/zero node IDs or duplicate client/peer addresses or data dirs; missing cluster ID or protocol version; cross-limit inconsistency — max_key_bytes + max_value_bytes + command envelope must fit the 66 KiB canonical-command limit, which fits the 1 MiB journal-frame and 512 KiB HTTP-body limits; max_journal_bytes ≥ 1.25 × max_history_bytes + max_log_entries × per-entry overhead bound (≈64 B, derived from the frame spec and PINNED BY A TEST) + journal_protocol_allowance (named constant, default 64 MiB) — same formula applies to small test limits so capacity profiles are not flaky; replication in-flight batches × max batch size ≤ per-peer send-queue bytes; node IDs nonzero and below 2^53 (at most 2^53 − 1 = 9007199254740991; D-77, br-s4dg); heartbeat ≥ 1 tick; election-min ≥ 5 × heartbeat; election-max > min; election_max_ticks_exclusive = 2 × election_min_ticks EXACTLY (raft-rs 0.7 hardwires the [t, 2t) range shape — D-75); write deadline ≥ election max; CLI deadline ≥ write_deadline_ticks × tick_ms (reject a shorter CLI deadline, comparing durations in the same units); raft-rs Config::validate constraints honoured so every accepted fixture config constructs a RawNode (proven by a test); every limit within its declared range.
- Timing defaults: tick 50 ms; heartbeat 2 ticks; election [20,40) ticks; write deadline 100 ticks; CLI deadline 15 s. Timers control progress and give-up only — NEVER commitment, versions or history retention.
- Fingerprint (DUR-8/§7.10): covers every parameter that can change a result — key/value limits, live-state limits, history capacity (max_log_entries, max_history_bytes), command-format version, canonical (sorted) voter set. max_journal_bytes is LOCAL, not fingerprinted. Stable across re-parse; changes with every semantic parameter.
- Limits registry (§7.11): every allocation-bearing collection has an entry BEFORE it is introduced; bounded wrapper types; each numeric parameter's allowed range declared alongside its entry and enforced by this parser (OpenAPI and codec limits are checked against the same table — no bound lives in two places).

title: W09: State machine — PUT/GET, versions, request history, live-state quota, invariants
description:
## Context
The state machine is the pure heart of keyval: an ordered map plus the never-expiring request history, changed ONLY by the deterministic apply function. Everything else (journal, Raft, HTTP) exists to feed it committed entries in order. This item covers the PUT/GET slice; DELETE/CAS land in W27, SCAN in W28.

## Requirements covered
DM-3 (version = log index of first successful execution; strictly increasing per key incl. across delete/re-create; same-value PUT gets a new version; replay returns the ORIGINAL version; gaps expected), DM-5 (request history: request_id → (first_index, command_digest, terminal_result); NEVER expired or evicted for the life of the cluster), DM-6 (live-state capacity: 10,000 keys / 64 MiB default; over-quota write ⇒ committed terminal `capacity_exceeded`; DELETE and shrinking overwrites always possible), F-1 (PUT), F-2 (GET), F-6 (request-ID semantics), C-6 (each ID takes effect at most once, forever), CD-7 (invariant assertions).

## Area
`statemachine` (crates/statemachine — leaf areas apply later: apply, history, scan, codec).

## Depends on
W04 (types), W08 (limits/config).

## Design & key rules (condensed from §7.5)
- Contents: ordered map key → (value, version); request history; live-state counters (keys, bytes) for DM-6; the committed-command-bytes counter for DM-7 (each FIRST execution adds the canonical encoded command length, whatever its terminal result — mismatch/capacity consume bytes too; replays, conflicts and no-ops add nothing; replay reproduces the counter exactly); applied_index.
- Commands (canonical, versioned byte encoding, ≤ 66 KiB): Put{request_id,key,value}, Delete{request_id,key}, Cas{request_id,key,expected,value}; empty (no-op) entries carry no command.
- Apply(state, index, entry) is PURE and deterministic — the only place writes change state: (1) empty entry → advance applied_index only; (2) decode; a committed entry that fails to decode is an invariant violation (leader validated before proposing); (3) seen request_id: same digest → stored result, nothing changes (replay); different digest → nothing changes, waiters get request_id_conflict, original result stays authoritative; (4) first execution: PUT over DM-6 quota → capacity_exceeded, else set key with version = index; record (index, digest, result) in history INCLUDING mismatch/capacity results (they are terminal); (5) applied_index = index.
- Digest: SHA-256 over canonical command bytes, implemented IN-CRATE (like CRC-32C; no new dependency, CD-12), tested against FIPS 180-4 vectors. Conflict detection rests on collision resistance — a stated Assumption (§10.15), because full command comparison would need disk reads inside apply (R-17).
- Memory: ~120 B per history record ⇒ ~120 MB at the 1M-entry cap — the price of never-expiring retry safety (RISK-4); v2 compaction MUST carry the history.
- No persistence of state-machine state (D-10): rebuilt by replaying the committed log; replay recomputes every result identically because apply is deterministic.
- Invariants (CD-7, via `invariant!` with node/index/invariant-ID context, active in ALL builds): applied_index ≤ commit_index; a key's version never decreases; bounded collections never exceed their limit.

## Acceptance
- Property tests: version = execution index; a replay returns the original result; a conflicting digest changes nothing; the quota outcome is terminal and deterministic; corrupted-state fixtures FIRE the assertions (prove the invariants are armed, not decorative).

## Out of scope
DELETE/CAS (W27), SCAN (W28), status endpoint semantics (W29), journal encoding (W11 owns frames; the command codec lives here as statemachine/codec).

## Notes for the future
- A different agent should write the reference model (W10) from §6/§8 prose — never from this code (independent authorship, §11.7; RISK-8).
- The DM-7 byte counter is read at the leader's applied index for admission (W14/W29) — keep it exact under replay (a test proves identical accounting after recovery).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.5, D-07, D-10, D-13, R-15, R-17, RISK-4.

comments.text:
## Closure: W10.2 (PeachAnchor, 2026-10-04)

**Work:** 2e587cb, tree f87b6100. The wrapper's gate passed on the first attempt (receipt `artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261004T042904Z-f87b6100703f-2595818.json`).

**What landed:** `schemas/observation/`.
- **Schema:** `keyval.observation/v1`, with 19 record kinds.
  - Client side: invocations, attempts and responses with their outcomes, deliveries.
  - Node side: logs, syncs, acceptances, releases, god-view states.
  - Run level: commits with decoded commands, faults, phases, markers, drain, resolutions.
  - Outcomes are checked per operation and code, matching §8.4 and openapi.
- **README:** documents each record kind and the checkers that read it, what the oracles derive themselves (including the DUR-2 cover rule), the 11 stream rules a producer guarantees, and the properties of a correct run.
- **Fixtures:** two runs built by a generator (a marker heal and a DM-7 drain heal), an (operation, code) outcome table, and 22 negative fixtures.
- **Check OBSERVATION-SCHEMA:** T0, invariant, covers T-12, 7 cases. W10's accept list now includes it.

**Review:** four rounds, each with two independent reviewers (Opus and Fable), triaged P1/P2/P3.
- **Round 1:** 4 P1s, including:
  - no per-node logs for K-8;
  - no sound link from committed entries to commands;
  - read refusals forced to carry `attempt_state`;
  - a fixture that broke DUR-2.
- **Round 2:** 1 P1, rule 8 forbidding commit by prefix, raised by both reviewers. Also a lossy DUR-2 cover rule.
- **Round 3:** no P1. Two P2s: releases weren't tied to responses, and an invalid scenario couldn't be represented.
- **Round 4:** no P1. One P2, fixed before commit: the K-4 correct-run rule now lets a misuse command commit later as a no-effect conflict.

Every P1 and P2 is fixed. P3s were fixed where both reviewers raised them.

**Claims:** the tests check the contract's invariants against its fixtures. They are not evidence about any producer: none exists yet. W17's harness and W36's recording must validate their real output against this schema (O-6), as the README says.

**Deferred P3s:** each was raised by one reviewer, and none is blocking.
- `manifest.seed` is limited to 2^53−1, while `MasterSeed` is a u64. The README says seeds are drawn below 2^53; W17 must keep to that.
- Fixture timing realism: check-quorum and the 100-tick write deadline against the fixtures' short chaos window.

title: W10: Reference model, observation schema, differential tests
description:
## Context
Checkers must never compute expected results with the code under test (D-21, RISK-8). The reference model is a deliberately simple, obviously correct, single-threaded in-memory model of keyval's semantics — the oracle for checkers K-4/K-5/K-10, the differential property tests, and (W30) the model server the conformance suite validates against. Written FROM §6 and §8 prose, ideally by a different agent than W09's author.

## Requirements covered
T-7 (reference model defines expected semantics), T-12 (oracle independence: depends on NO production crate, not even domain types — defines its own small key/value types; consumes the documented observation schema), §10.14.

## Area
`model` (crates/model).

## Depends on
W03 (spec), W09 (the differential test needs the state machine to diff against — the model itself is written from prose).

## Design & key rules
- The model: ordered map + request history; applies commands one at a time in log order; returns exactly what the API promises — version, existed, CAS success/mismatch with current version, replay, conflict, capacity outcomes, SCAN pages. No consensus, no I/O, no cleverness.
- The observation schema (versioned, in schemas/): the documented format in which the harness records invocations, responses, first executions etc.; the model reads commands from it. This schema is the contract between the sim/workload side (W36) and the whole oracle stack (W38–W40) — design it here, carefully.
- Differential property tests (T0): random command sequences applied to BOTH the state machine and the model; results and final states must match. For this item PUT/GET pass; DELETE/CAS/SCAN rows are registered as `planned` (reported, not enforced) until W27/W28.
- Disagreement between model and state machine: the PLAN (§6/§8) decides which is wrong; a model bug is fixed like a checker bug — `conflict` + `needs-owner` bead with an independent counterexample (§11.5 rule 3).

## Acceptance
- The model covers every operation and outcome in §6/§8; the dependency check proves no production dependencies; the differential test passes for PUT/GET (others planned); a deliberately broken state-machine variant FAILS the differential test (proves the oracle has teeth).

## Out of scope
The model HTTP server (W30); checkers themselves (W38–W40).

## Notes for the future
- B-22 (W45) will mutate this model in a sandboxed copy and expect fixture suites to catch it.
- Keep it boring: every clever optimisation here is a place a shared conceptual bug can hide (RISK-8).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.14, T-7, T-12, D-21.

title: W11: Journal engine — frames, genesis, logical truncation, offset index, entry cache, recovery
description:
## Context
The journal is the ONE durable authority (CD-10, D-10): an append-only framed file per node; everything else (key-value map, request history) is derived by replay. Raft is only safe if entries and votes are synced before the node acts on them — this engine provides the frames, recovery and fail-closed guarantees that make that true.

## Requirements covered
DUR-1 (ack only after commit+apply — journal side), DUR-4 (no compaction in v1), DUR-5 (format version + golden vectors), DUR-6 (torn tail discarded; corruption refuses; never silently repair synced data), DUR-8 (genesis binding), DUR-9 (recovery correct under the stated crash model), CD-9, CD-10.

## Area
`journal` (crates/journal, incl. golden/ vectors).

## Depends on
W04 (types/ports), W08 (config, fingerprint).

## Design & key rules (condensed from §7.6–§7.7)
- One append-only `journal.log` + `LOCK` file (exclusive data-directory ownership).
- Frame layout (little-endian): magic `KVJ1` (4B) | format version (2B) | kind (1B: Genesis|RaftBatch) | reserved zero (1B) | payload length (4B, ≤ 1 MiB) | frame sequence (8B, strictly increasing) | HEADER checksum (CRC-32C over the fixed header fields — lets the resync scan trust an intact header's length, D-69) | payload | checksum (CRC-32C over header+payload) | trailing length (4B, = payload length; detects incomplete final frames).
- Records: Genesis{format_version, instance_id (random 128-bit, stamped at init), cluster_id (display only), node_id, voters, semantic_config_fingerprint} — always frame 1; RaftBatch{entries[], hard_state?} — one per persisted Ready.
- Logical truncation: a RaftBatch whose first entry index ≤ current last index REPLACES the logical log from that index; old bytes stay (append-only); replacing at or below the persisted commit index is an invariant violation.
- Offset index in memory: LogIndex → (offset, term), ~16 B/entry, bounded by DM-7. Entry cache: bounded (8 MiB); misses read via the byte-storage port in bounded chunks; eviction changes cost, never results.
- CRC-32C implemented in-crate, tested against standard vectors (CD-12). Detects accidents, not adversaries.
- FAIL CLOSED recovery scan: first invalid frame ends the durable prefix at last valid frame N; then a RESYNC SCAN over the ENTIRE remainder (bounded-memory chunks) searches at every byte offset for a complete checksum-valid frame with sequence > N: found ⇒ damage inside the durable prefix ⇒ CORRUPTION, refuse (covers corrupted mid-journal frame with valid N+2 after it, and sequence gaps); none ⇒ torn tail, discarded AND physically truncated (through the port's Truncate, then synced) before the next append. Lengths in a damaged tail are untrusted UNLESS the header checksum validates (an intact torn frame's header gives a trustworthy length; the scan skips its payload range, so client bytes in a torn payload cannot masquerade as a later frame — residual crafted-payload case is a stated Assumption, D-69). A legitimate torn tail is ≤ one maximum frame (because §7.4 keeps at most one Ready unsynced); longer trailing region ⇒ corruption, refuse.
- Recovery sequence (§7.7): lock → genesis verify (node ID, voters, fingerprint; load instance ID) → scan → rebuild logical log/offset index/hard state → replay 1..commit through ordinary apply → construct Raft with applied position → Ready. Ordinary start REFUSES a missing directory or missing genesis (blank rejoin = Raft amnesia, D-52). `init` may re-run only while the journal holds no complete genesis and nothing after it.
- Golden vectors (committed byte files, each with a README line): encoded genesis + RaftBatch (decode→expected; encode→identical bytes); recovery cases: empty journal; clean; incomplete final frame cut mid-header/mid-payload/mid-trailer (discard); bad checksum on final complete frame (discard as torn); zero-filled tail; garbage/bad-magic tail (discard); bad checksum mid-journal with valid continuation (refuse via resync); corrupted N+1 followed by valid N+2 (refuse); sequence gap with valid continuation (refuse); trailing region longer than one max frame (refuse); logical truncation + replacements; truncation below commit (refuse); crash during physical tail truncation (recovery converges); incomplete genesis-only journal (recoverable only by explicit init).
- Goldens are ORACLES (P9): a format change bumps the format version, adds NEW goldens, records in §16. NEVER regenerate goldens to make a test pass.

## Acceptance
- Every §7.6 golden vector passes; recovery returns hard state and logical log; fail-closed cases refuse with specific errors; cache eviction never changes results.

## Out of scope
The real-file and simulated byte-storage adapters (W12); the Ready loop that produces frames (W13); crash probes (W24).

## Notes for the future
- DUR-2 nuance: entries, TERM and VOTE are synced before dependent messages; the COMMIT INDEX is volatile — persisted only opportunistically inside a frame being written anyway, never worth a frame alone (D-44; frame-stream identity everywhere depends on this rule).
- The crash model (single definition §10.2): a PREFIX of the unsynced append survives (none/some/all), optionally followed by zero/garbage bytes up to the append's extent, never longer than one max frame; synced bytes never damaged. Recovery fails closed on anything outside it (§10.15 Assumption).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.6, §7.7, §10.2, D-50, D-52, D-60, D-63, D-69.

title: W12: Byte-storage adapters — real files and simulated disk, one contract suite
description:
## Context
The byte-storage port has two adapters — real files (production) and the simulated disk (volatile + durable byte images) — and ONE shared contract test suite that both must pass (P3: what simulation proves must hold for production). The simulated disk is where the crash model lives: a seed-chosen prefix of unsynced bytes survives, optionally followed by garbage.

## Requirements covered
DUR-1, DUR-7 (directory durability: created files volatile until parent dir synced), DUR-9 (crash model), T-2 (same engine code against both adapters).

## Area
`fs_storage` (real-file adapter), `sim/disk` (leaf area of crates/sim).

## Depends on
W11 (journal engine defines usage), W15 (the sim crate and its facade are created by W15 — D-74 orders W15 before W12).

## Design & key rules
- Contract suite: append, read_at (bounded), Truncate (relied on only after its own sync), Sync(seq) → SyncDone(seq, incarnation), create-file + sync-directory, exclusive lock. Runs identically against both adapters.
- Simulated disk (§10.2): per-node volatile and durable byte images; appends land volatile; sync makes durable. On crash a seed-chosen portion of unsynced appended bytes survives as a prefix — none, some or all — optionally followed by zero or garbage bytes up to the append's extent (the seed chooses; never ONLY "all unsynced bytes vanish"). Directory entries modelled: a created file stays volatile until the parent directory is synced (crash between create and dir-sync loses the file). Truncate uses the same volatile/durable split incl. crash between truncation and its sync. A sync can become durable while its completion notification is lost to a crash; the scheduler sometimes delivers the stale completion to the NEXT incarnation, which must ignore it (B-17's fuel). Synced bytes are never damaged (corruption deferred, §9.2). Reads are instantaneous and deterministic.
- Real-file adapter: real fsync/fdatasync; syncs the parent directory on create (DUR-7); exclusive lock refuses a second process. Used by the server, CLI doctor and the crash probes.

## Acceptance
- One contract suite runs against both adapters; the simulated disk covers partial unsynced survival (none/some/all), a lost sync completion, directory-entry volatility until directory sync, and a crash during Truncate; the file adapter syncs directories on create and its lock refuses a second process.

## Out of scope
Failpoint instrumentation and SIGKILL probes (W24 adds them inside fs_storage behind the `failpoints` feature); the simulator scheduler (W15).

## Notes for the future
- Keep fs_storage thin — adapters only translate (CD-1). The sync-order check (W24) will instrument BELOW this adapter at the OS-call boundary.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.2 (byte storage), §10.2 (simulated disk), DUR-7/9, D-50, D-74.
